knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lie bracket of vector fields
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-free definition on an open set where both vector fields are defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\xi\) and \(\zeta\) be smooth vector fields whose domains contain an open set \(\mathcal U\). Their Lie bracket is the operator on \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal U)\) defined by \([\xi,\zeta]f:=\xi(\zeta f)-\zeta(\xi f)\). It is \(\mathbb R\)-linear and satisfies \([\xi,\zeta](fg)=f[\xi,\zeta]g+([\xi,\zeta]f)g\), hence is a derivation and defines a tangent vector field on \(\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For smooth vector fields defined on a common open set, the Lie bracket acts on a smooth function by applying the fields in opposite orders and subtracting. This operator is real-linear and obeys the Leibniz rule, so it is itself a tangent vector field.
assumptions_latex: \(\xi,\zeta\) are smooth vector fields whose domains contain an open set \(\mathcal U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: [\xi,\zeta]f=\xi(\zeta f)-\zeta(\xi f),\qquad [\xi,\zeta](fg)=f[\xi,\zeta]g+([\xi,\zeta]f)g;\quad [\xi,\zeta]\in\mathfrak X(\mathcal U).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometric Newton Iteration for a Manifold Vector Field
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithm for seeking a zero of a vector field using its covariant derivative and a retraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M\) have a retraction \(R\) and affine connection \(\nabla\), let \(\xi\) be a vector field, and choose \(x_0\in\mathcal M\). For \(k=0,1,2,\ldots\), solve for \(\eta_k\in T_{x_k}\mathcal M\) the Newton equation \(J(x_k)[\eta_k]=-\xi_{x_k}\), where \(J(x_k)[\eta_k]:=\nabla_{\eta_k}\xi\), and set \(x_{k+1}:=R_{x_k}(\eta_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a point on the manifold, repeatedly solve the intrinsic Newton equation for a tangent-space correction and map that correction back to the manifold with a retraction. The iteration seeks a point where the vector field vanishes.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M\text{ is a manifold equipped with a retraction }R\text{ and an affine connection }\nabla\).
\(\xi\text{ is a vector field on }\mathcal M\).
\(\eta_k\in T_{x_k}\mathcal M\text{ solves }J(x_k)[\eta_k]=-\xi_{x_k}\text{ at each executed iteration.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(\eta_k),\qquad J(x_k)[\eta_k]=\nabla_{\eta_k}\xi=-\xi_{x_k}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smooth vector fields and their coordinate decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition, action on functions, module operations, and local coordinate representation of smooth vector fields.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A smooth vector field on \(\mathcal M\) is a smooth map \(\xi:\mathcal M\to T\mathcal M\) such that \(\xi_x\in T_x\mathcal M\) for every \(x\in\mathcal M\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unique expansion in a coordinate frame
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents an arbitrary vector field locally in the coordinate frame and characterizes smoothness through its coefficient functions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Covariant derivative represented through a general transporter
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An exact limit representation whose correction term accounts for variation of the transporter-induced frame.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let c:I\to\mathcal M be a smooth curve on a Riemannian manifold equipped with a transporter \mathrm T. Fix t_0\in I, let v_1,\ldots,v_d be a basis of T_{c(t_0)}\mathcal M, and define V_i(t)=(\mathrm T_{c(t_0)\leftarrow c(t)})^{-1}(v_i). If Z\in\mathfrak X(c) and Z(t_0)=\sum_{i=1}^d\alpha_i(t_0)v_i, then
\[
\frac{\mathrm D}{\mathrm dt}Z(t_0)=\lim_{\delta\to0}\frac{\mathrm T_{c(t_0)\leftarrow c(t_0+\delta)}Z(t_0+\delta)-Z(t_0)}{\delta}+\sum_{i=1}^d\alpha_i(t_0)\frac{\mathrm D}{\mathrm dt}V_i(t_0).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The covariant derivative of a vector field along a smooth curve is the limit of its transported difference quotient plus a correction for the covariant variation of the frame induced by the transporter.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vector-Transport Finite-Difference Jacobian
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a basiswise forward-difference Jacobian approximation in a common tangent space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M\) have a vector transport \(\mathcal T\) with associated retraction \(R\). Let smooth vector fields \(E_1,\ldots,E_d\) form a basis of \(T_x\mathcal M\) throughout a neighborhood, let \(\xi\) be smooth, and let \(h>0\). Define the linear operator \(A(x):T_x\mathcal M\to T_x\mathcal M\) on the basis by \[A(x)[E_i(x)]=\frac{(\mathcal T_{hE_i(x)})^{-1}\xi_{R_x(hE_i(x))}-\xi_x}{h},\qquad i=1,\ldots,d,\] and extend it linearly to every tangent vector in \(T_x\mathcal M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A manifold finite-difference Jacobian transports the displaced vector-field value back to the original tangent space, subtracts the original value, divides by the step length, and extends the resulting basis values linearly.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M\) is endowed with a vector transport \(\mathcal T\) and associated retraction \(R\).
\(E_1,\ldots,E_d\) are smooth local vector fields forming a basis of each nearby tangent space.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Error Bound for a Vector-Transport Finite-Difference Jacobian
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local basiswise consistency bound near a nondegenerate zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\xi\) be a smooth vector field on a manifold \(\mathcal M\) endowed with vector transport \(\mathcal T\). Let \(x_*\) be a nondegenerate zero of \(\xi\), let \(E_1,\ldots,E_d\) be a smooth local frame on a neighborhood of \(x_*\), and let \(A\) be the vector-transport finite-difference operator with step \(h\). Then there exists \(c>0\) such that, for all \(x\) sufficiently close to \(x_*\), all sufficiently small \(h\), and each \(i=1,\ldots,d\), \[\|A(x)[E_i(x)]-J(x)[E_i(x)]\|\le c\bigl(h+\|\xi_x\|\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a nondegenerate zero, each basis column of the vector-transport finite-difference Jacobian differs from the exact Jacobian by at most a constant times the finite-difference step plus the vector-field residual.
assumptions_latex: \(\xi\) is a smooth vector field on \(\mathcal M\).
\(\mathcal M\) is endowed with vector transport \(\mathcal T\).
\(E_1,\ldots,E_d\) form a smooth local frame near \(x_*\).
\(A\) is defined by the vector-transport finite-difference formula.
\(x\) is sufficiently close to \(x_*\) and \(h\) is sufficiently small.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists c>0\;\forall i:\quad \|A(x)[E_i(x)]-J(x)[E_i(x)]\|\le c\bigl(h+\|\xi_x\|\bigr).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convexity Criterion for the Energy of a Torse-Forming Field
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient differential inequality for convexity, together with the stated consequence for critical points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\) be torse forming, with \(\nabla_YX=aY+\omega(Y)X\), and let \(f\) be its energy. Then \(f\) is convex if and only if, for every \(Y\in\mathfrak X(M)\),
\[
\bigl(Y(a)+3a\omega(Y)\bigr)g(X,Y)+2\bigl((\nabla_Y\omega)(Y)+2\omega(Y)^2\bigr)f+a^2g(Y,Y)\ge0.
\]
If \(f\) is convex, then its critical points, its global minimizers, and the zeros of \(X\) coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The energy of a torse-forming vector field is convex exactly when the displayed differential inequality holds in every smooth vector-field direction. Under this convexity, its critical points, global minimizers, and the zeros of the field coincide.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left[f\text{ is convex}\iff\bigl(Y(a)+3a\omega(Y)\bigr)g(X,Y)+2\bigl((\nabla_Y\omega)(Y)+2\omega(Y)^2\bigr)f+a^2g(Y,Y)\ge0\ \forall Y\in\mathfrak X(M)\right],\quad \operatorname{Crit}(f)=\operatorname{argmin}(f)=\{x\in M:X_x=0\}\text{ when }f\text{ is convex}

knowledge_statements.title: Local Trivializations of Tangent Bundles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chart-induced local product representation of the tangent bundle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a chart \((U,\varphi)\) on a smooth \(n\)-manifold \(M\), define \(\tau_U:\pi^{-1}(U)\to U\times\mathbb R^n\) by \(\tau_U(v)=(p,d\varphi_p(v))\) for \(v\in T_pM\). Then \(\tau_U\) is a diffeomorphism, is linear on every fiber, and satisfies \(\operatorname{pr}_1\circ\tau_U=\pi\). On an overlap, the fiber coordinate changes by \(w\mapsto D(\psi\circ\varphi^{-1})(\varphi(p))w\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A manifold chart identifies the tangent bundle locally with a product, and overlap maps act on tangent coordinates through transition Jacobians.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(TM|_U\cong U\times\mathbb R^n\) as smooth vector bundles.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometry of a regular zero-level-set manifold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regular zero sets in finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces, with tangent-normal projections, derivatives of restricted functions, and the local metric-projection retraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h:\mathcal E\to\mathbb R^k\) be smooth, let \(\dim\mathcal E>k\), and suppose \(\operatorname{rank}\mathrm Dh(x)=k\) for every \(x\in\mathcal M=h^{-1}(0)\). Then \(\mathcal M\) is an embedded submanifold of dimension \(\dim\mathcal E-k\). For \(x\in\mathcal M\), \(T_x\mathcal M=\ker\mathrm Dh(x)\) and \(N_x\mathcal M=\operatorname{im}\mathrm Dh(x)^*=\operatorname{span}\{\operatorname{grad}h_i(x)\}_{i=1}^k\). Every \(v\in\mathcal E\) has a unique orthogonal decomposition \(v=\operatorname{Proj}_x(v)+\mathrm Dh(x)^*[\alpha]\), where \(\alpha=(\mathrm Dh(x)^*)^\dagger[v]\), so \(\operatorname{Proj}_x(v)=v-\mathrm Dh(x)^*[(\mathrm Dh(x)^*)^\dagger[v]]\). If \(f=\bar f|_{\mathcal M}\), then \(\operatorname{grad}f(x)=\operatorname{Proj}_x(\operatorname{grad}\bar f(x))=\operatorname{grad}\bar f(x)-\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i(x)\operatorname{grad}h_i(x)\), where \(\lambda(x)=(\mathrm Dh(x)^*)^\dagger[\operatorname{grad}\bar f(x)]\), and, on \(T_x\mathcal M\), \(\operatorname{Hess}f(x)=\operatorname{Proj}_x\circ\bigl(\operatorname{Hess}\bar f(x)-\sum_{i=1}^k\lambda_i(x)\operatorname{Hess}h_i(x)\bigr)\circ\operatorname{Proj}_x\). The nearest-point map \(R_x(v)\in\arg\min_{h(y)=0}\|x+v-y\|\) is a second-order retraction when locally defined for sufficiently small \(v\in T_x\mathcal M\); it may fail to be unique for arbitrary \(v\) and can be difficult to compute. The same geometric formulas apply locally when the manifold has only a local defining map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth equality system whose derivative has full rank on its zero set defines an embedded manifold of codimension k. Its tangent space is the derivative's kernel, its normal space is spanned by the constraint gradients, and the pseudoinverse yields the orthogonal projection. Projecting the ambient gradient and the constraint-corrected ambient Hessian gives the Riemannian gradient and Hessian of a restricted function. Local nearest-point projection is a second-order retraction, although it can be nonunique outside its local domain and difficult to compute.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal E\) is a finite-dimensional Euclidean space with \(\dim\mathcal E>k\).
\(h:\mathcal E\to\mathbb R^k\) is smooth and \(\operatorname{rank}\mathrm Dh(x)=k\) for every \(x\in h^{-1}(0)\).
\(x\in\mathcal M=h^{-1}(0)\); the derivative formulas assume a smooth extension \(\bar f:\mathcal E\to\mathbb R\) with \(f=\bar f|_{\mathcal M}\).
The metric-projection formula is considered for sufficiently small \(v\in T_x\mathcal M\), where the nearest feasible point is locally well defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal M\) is an embedded manifold of dimension \(\dim\mathcal E-k\) with the stated tangent-space, normal-space, projection, Riemannian-gradient, Riemannian-Hessian, and local second-order-retraction formulas.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y\text{ is a regular value of }H\iff\forall x\in H^{-1}(y),\;\operatorname{rank}\nabla H(x)=t.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate definition of smoothness between manifolds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) and \(N\) be smooth manifolds. A map \(F:M\to N\) is smooth if, for every \(p\in M\), there are smooth charts \((U,\varphi)\) about \(p\) and \((V,\psi)\) about \(F(p)\), with \(F(U)\subseteq V\), such that \(\psi\circ F\circ\varphi^{-1}:\varphi(U)\to\psi(V)\) is smooth as a map between open subsets of Euclidean spaces. Compatibility of atlases makes this definition chart-independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A map between smooth manifolds is smooth when its expression in local coordinates is an ordinary smooth Euclidean map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is smooth exactly when its local coordinate representatives are smooth.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ambient Differential and the Manifold Straight-Line Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the ambient differential and records why its straight-line formula cannot generally be applied directly to manifold-domain maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar F:U\subseteq\mathcal E\to\mathcal E'\) be smooth, where \(U\) is open. For \(x\in U\), its differential is the linear map \(\mathrm D\bar F(x):\mathcal E\to\mathcal E'\) satisfying \[\mathrm D\bar F(x)[v]=\lim_{t\to0}\frac{\bar F(x+tv)-\bar F(x)}{t}.\] If \(F:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M'\) is defined only on an embedded submanifold and \(v\in T_x\mathcal M\), the same expression cannot generally be used directly because \(x+tv\) need not lie in \(\mathcal M\) for nonzero \(t\). The manifold differential is instead obtained using curves in \(\mathcal M\), equivalently in the embedded setting by differentiating a suitable smooth ambient extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ambient differential is the linear directional-derivative map given by the usual difference quotient. For a map defined only on a manifold, ambient straight lines generally leave its domain, so one must use manifold curves or a smooth ambient extension.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal E\) and \(\mathcal E'\) are linear spaces, \(U\subseteq\mathcal E\) is open, and \(\bar F:U\to\mathcal E'\) is smooth.
\(F:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M'\) is a smooth map between embedded submanifolds, \(x\in\mathcal M\), and \(v\in T_x\mathcal M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm D\bar F(x)[v]=\lim_{t\to0}(\bar F(x+tv)-\bar F(x))/t\), whereas this straight-line expression is not generally defined for \(F\) because \(x+tv\notin\mathcal M\) may occur.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Curve segments and their regularity classes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines curve segments, their regularity classes, and endpoint connection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A curve segment on a manifold \(\mathcal M\) is a continuous map \(c:[a,b]\to\mathcal M\), where \(a\leq b\). It is smooth if it extends to a smooth map on a neighborhood of \([a,b]\), with endpoint derivatives defined using that extension. It is regular if it is smooth and \(c'(t)\neq0\) for every \(t\in[a,b]\). It is piecewise smooth, respectively piecewise regular, if a finite partition \(a=t_0<\cdots<t_k=b\) makes each restriction \(c|_{[t_{i-1},t_i]}\) smooth, respectively regular. Every piecewise regular curve is piecewise smooth. It connects \(x\) to \(y\) if \(c(a)=x\) and \(c(b)=y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A curve segment is a continuous manifold-valued map on a closed interval. Smoothness requires a smooth extension beyond the endpoints, regularity also requires nonzero velocity, and piecewise versions use a finite partition. Its endpoint values determine which points it connects.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The extension, nonvanishing-velocity, finite-partition, and endpoint conditions define smooth, regular, piecewise-smooth, piecewise-regular, and connecting curve segments.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smoothness of maps between embedded submanifolds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines pointwise and global smoothness through local extensions to the ambient Euclidean spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M\) and \(\mathcal M'\) be embedded submanifolds of \(\mathcal E\) and \(\mathcal E'\), respectively. A map \(F:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M'\) is smooth at \(x\in\mathcal M\) if there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x\) in \(\mathcal E\) and a smooth map \(\bar F:U\to\mathcal E'\) such that \(F(y)=\bar F(y)\) for all \(y\in\mathcal M\cap U\). The map \(\bar F\) is called a local smooth extension of \(F\) around \(x\). The map \(F\) is smooth if it is smooth at every \(x\in\mathcal M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A map between embedded submanifolds is smooth at a point when it locally agrees, on the source manifold, with a smooth map defined in the ambient space. It is smooth when this condition holds at every source point.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal E\) and \(\mathcal M'\subseteq\mathcal E'\) are embedded submanifolds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is smooth at }x\iff \exists\,U\subseteq\mathcal E\text{ open with }x\in U,\ \exists\,\bar F\in C^\infty(U,\mathcal E')\text{ such that }\bar F|_{\mathcal M\cap U}=F|_{\mathcal M\cap U};\quad F\text{ is smooth}\iff \forall x\in\mathcal M,\ F\text{ is smooth at }x.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Differential of a Smooth Map Between Manifolds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic curve-based definition of the differential, or tangent map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M'\) be smooth and let \(x\in\mathcal M\). The differential at \(x\) is the linear map \(\mathrm DF(x):T_x\mathcal M\to T_{F(x)}\mathcal M'\) defined for \(v\in T_x\mathcal M\) by \[\mathrm DF(x)[v]=\left.\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}F(c(t))\right|_{t=0}=(F\circ c)'(0),\] where \(c\) is a smooth curve in \(\mathcal M\) satisfying \(c(0)=x\) and \(c'(0)=v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The differential of a smooth map between manifolds sends each tangent vector to the initial velocity of the image of a smooth curve realizing that vector.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M'\) is smooth and \(x\in\mathcal M\).
\(v\in T_x\mathcal M\), and \(c\) is a smooth curve with \(c(0)=x\) and \(c'(0)=v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm DF(x):T_x\mathcal M\to T_{F(x)}\mathcal M'\) is linear and \(\mathrm DF(x)[v]=(F\circ c)'(0)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smooth Map Between Manifolds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines pointwise and global smoothness using a coordinate representative in charts around the source point and its image.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $F:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M'$ and $x\in\mathcal M$. If $(\mathcal U,\varphi)$ is a chart around $x$ and $(\mathcal V,\psi)$ is a chart around $F(x)$, then $F$ is smooth at $x$ when the coordinate representative $\widetilde F=\psi\circ F\circ\varphi^{-1}:\varphi(\mathcal U)\to\psi(\mathcal V)$ is smooth at $\varphi(x)$. The map $F$ is smooth when it is smooth at every $x\in\mathcal M$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A map between manifolds is smooth at a point when its local coordinate representation is smooth there. It is smooth globally when this holds at every point.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Energy Functional and Harmonic Map
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Records the map energy and defines harmonicity by its Euler–Ostrogradsky equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a smooth map \(f:(M,g)\to(N,h)\), locally represented by \(y^i=y^i(x^\alpha)\), its energy is \[E(f)=\int_M g^{\alpha\beta}h_{ij}y^i_\alpha y^j_\beta\,dv.\] The associated Euler--Ostrogradsky equations are \(g^{\alpha\beta}y^i_{\alpha\beta}=0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,\dim N\). The map \(f\) is harmonic when its components satisfy these equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The energy of a smooth map is the integral of the metric contraction of its first derivatives. The map is harmonic when its components satisfy the associated Euler–Ostrogradsky equations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ is harmonic}\iff g^{\alpha\beta}y^i_{\alpha\beta}=0\quad\text{for }i=1,\ldots,\dim N.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Retraction on a Smooth Manifold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Includes the ambient-extension interpretation of smoothness for embedded manifolds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A retraction on a smooth manifold \(\mathcal M\) is a smooth map \(R:T\mathcal M\to\mathcal M\), written \(R(x,v)=R_x(v)\), such that for every \(x\in\mathcal M\) and \(v\in T_x\mathcal M\), the curve \(c(t)=R_x(tv)\) satisfies \(c(0)=x\) and \(c'(0)=v\). If \(\mathcal M\) is embedded in a Euclidean space \(\mathcal E\), smoothness means that there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(T\mathcal M\) in \(\mathcal E\times\mathcal E\) and a smooth map \(\overline R:U\to\mathcal E\) with \(R=\overline R|_{T\mathcal M}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A retraction is a smooth map from the tangent bundle back to the manifold whose radial curve from any tangent vector starts at its base point with that vector as its initial velocity. For an embedded manifold, smoothness is understood through a smooth ambient extension near the tangent bundle.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal E\text{ is embedded for the ambient-extension clause}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c(t)=R_x(tv)\implies c(0)=x\ \text{and}\ c'(0)=v;\qquad \mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal E\implies R=\overline R|_{T\mathcal M}\ \text{for some smooth ambient extension }\overline R.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ambient-extension characterization of smooth maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes smooth maps on embedded submanifolds using one smooth extension defined on a neighborhood of the entire source manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M\) and \(\mathcal M'\) be embedded submanifolds of \(\mathcal E\) and \(\mathcal E'\), respectively. A map \(F:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M'\) is smooth if and only if there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\mathcal M\) in \(\mathcal E\) and a smooth map \(\bar F:U\to\mathcal E'\) such that \(F=\bar F|_{\mathcal M}\). In particular, \(f:\mathcal M\to\mathbb R\) is smooth if and only if there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\mathcal M\) in \(\mathcal E\) and a smooth map \(\bar f:U\to\mathbb R\) such that \(f=\bar f|_{\mathcal M}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A map between embedded submanifolds is smooth exactly when it is the restriction of a single smooth ambient-space map defined on a neighborhood of the whole source manifold. The same equivalence holds for real-valued functions.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal E\) and \(\mathcal M'\subseteq\mathcal E'\) are embedded submanifolds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\in C^\infty(\mathcal M,\mathcal M')\iff \exists\,U\supseteq\mathcal M,\ \exists\,\bar F\in C^\infty(U,\mathcal E'):\ F=\bar F|_{\mathcal M};\quad f\in C^\infty(\mathcal M,\mathbb R)\iff \exists\,U\supseteq\mathcal M,\ \exists\,\bar f\in C^\infty(U,\mathbb R):\ f=\bar f|_{\mathcal M}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Transporter on a manifold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines smooth transport between tangent spaces without requiring isometry or invertibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal M\times\mathcal M\) be open and contain \((x,x)\) for every \(x\in\mathcal M\). A transporter on \(\mathcal V\) is a smooth map \(T:\mathcal V\to\mathcal L(T\mathcal M,T\mathcal M)\), \((x,y)\mapsto T_{y\leftarrow x}\), such that \(T_{y\leftarrow x}:T_x\mathcal M\to T_y\mathcal M\) is linear and \(T_{x\leftarrow x}=\operatorname{Id}_{T_x\mathcal M}\). Smoothness means that its representing matrix in any pair of local frames varies smoothly with \((x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transporter is a smoothly varying family of linear maps from the tangent space at one point to the tangent space at another nearby point, equal to the identity when both points coincide.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\text{ is a transporter iff it is smooth, }T_{y\leftarrow x}:T_x\mathcal M\to T_y\mathcal M\text{ is linear, and }T_{x\leftarrow x}=\operatorname{Id}.

knowledge_statements.title: Immersion Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Immersions characterized by injective differentials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M^m\) and \(N^n\) be smooth manifolds with \(m\leq n\). A smooth map \(F:M\to N\) is an immersion at \(p\in M\) if its differential \(dF_p:T_pM\to T_{F(p)}N\) is injective, equivalently \(\operatorname{rank}(dF_p)=m\). It is an immersion if this holds at every point. Locally near each point, suitable coordinates put it in the form \((x^1,\ldots,x^m)\mapsto(x^1,\ldots,x^m,0,\ldots,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An immersion has injective differential everywhere and locally looks like the standard inclusion of a lower-dimensional Euclidean space.
assumptions_latex: \(M^m\) and \(N^n\) are smooth manifolds with \(m\leq n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\) is an immersion if and only if \(\operatorname{rank}(dF_p)=m\) for every \(p\in M\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank, immersion, and submersion of a smooth manifold map
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the chart-independent rank of a differentiable manifold map and its full-rank injective and surjective cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F:\mathcal M_1\to\mathcal M_2 be differentiable, with \dim\mathcal M_i=d_i. At x\in\mathcal M_1, define \operatorname{rank}_xF=\dim\operatorname{range}\!\left(D\widehat F(\varphi_1(x))\right), where \widehat F=\varphi_2\circ F\circ\varphi_1^{-1}; this rank is independent of the charts. The map F is an immersion if \operatorname{rank}_xF=d_1 for every x, which requires d_1\le d_2, and a submersion if \operatorname{rank}_xF=d_2 for every x, which requires d_1\ge d_2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The rank of a differentiable map between manifolds at a point is the dimension of the range of the derivative of any coordinate representation, independently of the charts. The map is an immersion when this rank equals the source dimension everywhere, and a submersion when it equals the target dimension everywhere.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is an immersion}\iff (\forall x)\,\operatorname{rank}_xF=d_1;\qquad F\text{ is a submersion}\iff (\forall x)\,\operatorname{rank}_xF=d_2.

knowledge_statements.title: Submersion Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Completeness and horizontal lifting under a Riemannian submersion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global consequences of a surjective Riemannian submersion whose total space is connected and complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\pi:\overline{\mathcal M}\to\mathcal M\) be a surjective Riemannian submersion. If \(\overline{\mathcal M}\) is connected and complete, then \(\mathcal M\) is connected and complete, and every fiber \(\pi^{-1}(p)\) is complete, though not necessarily connected. For every smooth curve \(c:I\to\mathcal M\) with \(\dot c(t)\ne0\) for all \(t\in I\), every \(t_0\in I\), and every \(x_0\in\pi^{-1}(c(t_0))\), there exists a unique horizontal lift \(\bar c:I\to\overline{\mathcal M}\) such that \(\pi\circ\bar c=c\) and \(\bar c(t_0)=x_0\). Moreover, \(c\) is a geodesic if and only if \(\bar c\) is a geodesic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A surjective Riemannian submersion from a connected complete total space has a connected complete base and complete, possibly disconnected fibers. Every regular smooth base curve has a unique whole-domain horizontal lift through any selected point of its initial fiber, and the curve is geodesic exactly when its lift is geodesic.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inverse function theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives local smooth invertibility from an invertible derivative between equal-dimensional linear spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\subseteq\mathcal E\) and \(V\subseteq\mathcal F\) be open subsets of linear spaces of equal dimension, and let \(F:U\to V\) be smooth. If \(DF(x)\) is invertible at some \(x\in U\), then there exist neighborhoods \(U'\subseteq U\) of \(x\) and \(V'\subseteq V\) of \(F(x)\) such that \(F|_{U'}:U'\to V'\) is a diffeomorphism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth map between open subsets of equal-dimensional linear spaces is a diffeomorphism on suitable neighborhoods of any point where its derivative is invertible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists U'\ni x,\ V'\ni F(x):\ F|_{U'}:U'\to V'\text{ is a diffeomorphism}.\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local normal-form characterization of embedded submanifolds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes embedded submanifolds by local diffeomorphic flattening onto a coordinate subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal E\) be a linear space of dimension \(d\), let \(\mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal E\), and let \(n=d-k\). Then \(\mathcal M\) is an embedded submanifold of \(\mathcal E\) of dimension \(n\) if and only if, for every \(x\in\mathcal M\), there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x\), an open set \(V\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), and a diffeomorphism \(F:U\to V\) such that \(F(\mathcal M\cap U)=E\cap V\), where \(E=\{y\in\mathbb R^d:y_{n+1}=\cdots=y_d=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subset is an embedded submanifold exactly when it can be locally transformed by a diffeomorphism into the standard coordinate subspace of the same dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal M\text{ is an embedded submanifold of dimension }n\iff\forall x\in\mathcal M\ \exists U,V,F:\ F(\mathcal M\cap U)=E\cap V.\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Coordinate-Slice Characterization of Embedded Submanifolds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes embedded submanifolds by a local coordinate normal form and identifies the induced submanifold charts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\mathcal N$ be a subset of an $n$-dimensional manifold $\mathcal M$. Then $\mathcal N$ is a $d$-dimensional embedded submanifold of $\mathcal M$ if and only if, for every $x\in\mathcal N$, there exists a chart $(\mathcal U,\varphi)$ of $\mathcal M$ about $x$ such that $\mathcal N\cap\mathcal U=\{y\in\mathcal U:\varphi(y)\in\mathbb R^d\times\{0\}^{n-d}\}$. In this case, $\varphi|_{\mathcal N\cap\mathcal U}$, viewed as a map into $\mathbb R^d$, is a chart of $\mathcal N$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subset is a d-dimensional embedded submanifold exactly when it is locally a coordinate slice in every neighborhood of its points; the nonzero coordinates then give charts on the submanifold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal N\text{ is a }d\text{-dimensional embedded submanifold}\iff \forall x\in\mathcal N\;\exists(\mathcal U,\varphi)\text{ about }x:\mathcal N\cap\mathcal U=\varphi^{-1}(\mathbb R^d\times\{0\}^{n-d}),\text{ and }\varphi|_{\mathcal N\cap\mathcal U}\text{ is a chart into }\mathbb R^d.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constant-Rank Level-Set Submanifold Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Establishes embeddedness for a nonempty level set under constant rank on an ambient neighborhood of the entire level set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let h:\overline{\mathcal M}\to\mathcal N be smooth, let \alpha\in\mathcal N, and suppose \varnothing\neq\mathcal M=h^{-1}(\alpha). If there exist a neighborhood V of \mathcal M in \overline{\mathcal M} and an integer r such that \operatorname{rank}\mathrm Dh(x)=r for every x\in V, then \mathcal M is closed in \overline{\mathcal M}, is an embedded submanifold of \overline{\mathcal M} with \dim\mathcal M=\dim\overline{\mathcal M}-r, and satisfies \mathrm T_x\mathcal M=\ker\mathrm Dh(x) for every x\in\mathcal M.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty level set is a closed embedded submanifold when the defining map has constant rank throughout a neighborhood of the whole level set. Its codimension equals that rank, and its tangent space is the kernel of the differential.
assumptions_latex: \exists V\supseteq\mathcal M\text{ a neighborhood and }r\text{ such that }\operatorname{rank}\mathrm Dh(x)=r\quad\forall x\in V
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal M\text{ is closed in }\overline{\mathcal M}\text{ and embedded},\quad \dim\mathcal M=\dim\overline{\mathcal M}-r,\quad \mathrm T_x\mathcal M=\ker\mathrm Dh(x)\quad\forall x\in\mathcal M.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regular Submanifold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local coordinate characterization of a regular embedded submanifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be an \(m\)-dimensional manifold and \(N\subset M\). The subset \(N\) is an \(n\)-dimensional regular submanifold of \(M\) if, for every \(p\in N\), there is a chart \((U;x_1,\ldots,x_m)\) containing \(p\) such that \[N\cap U=\{q\in U\mid x_{n+1}(q)=\cdots=x_m(q)=0\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subset N of an m-dimensional manifold M is an n-dimensional regular submanifold when every point of N has ambient coordinates in which N is obtained by setting the last m−n coordinates to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N\text{ is an }n\text{-dimensional regular submanifold of }M\iff \forall p\in N\;\exists (U;x_1,\ldots,x_m):p\in U,\ N\cap U=\{q\in U\mid x_{n+1}(q)=\cdots=x_m(q)=0\}\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subspace Topology on an Embedded Manifold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative openness and closedness inherited from the ambient linear space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal E\) and \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal M\). The set \(\mathcal U\) is open in \(\mathcal M\) if \(\mathcal U=\mathcal M\cap O\) for some open set \(O\subseteq\mathcal E\), and it is closed in \(\mathcal M\) if \(\mathcal U=\mathcal M\cap C\) for some closed set \(C\subseteq\mathcal E\). This is the subspace topology on \(\mathcal M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subset U of M is open in M when it is the intersection of M with an ambient open set, and closed in M when it is the intersection of M with an ambient closed set. This defines the subspace topology.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal U\text{ is open in }\mathcal M\iff\exists O\subseteq\mathcal E\text{ open with }\mathcal U=\mathcal M\cap O;\quad \mathcal U\text{ is closed in }\mathcal M\iff\exists C\subseteq\mathcal E\text{ closed with }\mathcal U=\mathcal M\cap C.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Restriction and Extension of Smooth Maps on Embedded Submanifolds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smoothness under restriction from the ambient manifold and existence of extensions preserving global or pointwise smoothness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M\) be an embedded submanifold of \(\overline{\mathcal M}\), and let \(\mathcal N\) be a manifold. If \(\bar F:\overline{\mathcal M}\to\mathcal N\) is smooth, respectively smooth at \(x\in\mathcal M\), then \(F=\bar F|_{\mathcal M}\) is smooth, respectively smooth at \(x\). Moreover, there exists a neighborhood \(\overline{\mathcal U}\) of \(\mathcal M\) in \(\overline{\mathcal M}\) such that every map \(F:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N\) has an extension \(\bar F:\overline{\mathcal U}\to\mathcal N\); this extension is smooth if \(F\) is smooth and is smooth at any \(x\in\mathcal M\) at which \(F\) is smooth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricting an ambient smooth map to an embedded submanifold preserves global and pointwise smoothness. Every map from the submanifold extends to a fixed ambient neighborhood, with global or pointwise smoothness preserved whenever present.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}\) is an embedded submanifold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar F\text{ smooth (at }x\text{)}\Rightarrow \bar F|_{\mathcal M}\text{ smooth (at }x\text{)}\), and \(\exists\,\overline{\mathcal U}\supseteq\mathcal M\) such that every \(F:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N\) admits an extension \(\bar F:\overline{\mathcal U}\to\mathcal N\) preserving its global and pointwise smoothness.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometry and Smoothness of Single-Valued Metric Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes the interior of the uniqueness domain and the differential of metric projection along the manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M\) be an embedded submanifold of a Euclidean space \(\mathcal E\), let \(A\subseteq\mathcal E\) be the domain on which \(P_{\mathcal M}\) is single-valued, and let \(\Omega=\operatorname{int}(A)\). If \(y\in A\) and \(x=P_{\mathcal M}(y)\), then \(y-x\perp T_x\mathcal M\) and \(\{x+t(y-x):t\in[0,1)\}\subseteq\Omega\); in particular, \(\mathcal M\subseteq\Omega\). The set \(\Omega\) is dense in \(A\), and if \(\mathcal M\) is closed in \(\mathcal E\), then \(\overline\Omega=\mathcal E\). Moreover, \(P_{\mathcal M}:\Omega\to\mathcal M\) is smooth and \(DP_{\mathcal M}(x)=\operatorname{Proj}_x\) for every \(x\in\mathcal M\), where \(\operatorname{Proj}_x\) is orthogonal projection onto \(T_x\mathcal M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniquely projected point has a normal projection residual, and the segment from its projection toward it, excluding the endpoint, lies inside the uniqueness-domain interior. That interior contains the manifold and is dense in the uniqueness domain. Projection is smooth there, with derivative at a manifold point equal to tangent-space orthogonal projection. If the manifold is closed, the interior is dense in the ambient space.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal E\) is an embedded submanifold of a Euclidean space.
\(A\) is the domain on which \(P_{\mathcal M}\) is single-valued and \(\Omega=\operatorname{int}(A)\).
For \(\overline\Omega=\mathcal E\), additionally \(\mathcal M\) is closed in \(\mathcal E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y-P_{\mathcal M}(y)\perp T_{P_{\mathcal M}(y)}\mathcal M,\quad \{P_{\mathcal M}(y)+t(y-P_{\mathcal M}(y)):t\in[0,1)\}\subseteq\Omega,\quad \overline{\Omega}^{\,A}=A,\quad P_{\mathcal M}|_\Omega\text{ is smooth},\quad DP_{\mathcal M}(x)=\operatorname{Proj}_x;\text{ if }\mathcal M\text{ is closed, }\overline\Omega=\mathcal E.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normal Space, Second Fundamental Form, and Weingarten Map
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection-differential definitions for a Riemannian submanifold of a Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M\) be a Riemannian submanifold of a Euclidean space \(\mathcal E\), and let \(x\in\mathcal M\). The normal space is \(N_x\mathcal M=(T_x\mathcal M)^\perp\). If \(\mathcal P_u:\mathcal E\to\mathcal E\) is the differential at \(x\), along \(u\in T_x\mathcal M\), of \(x\mapsto\operatorname{Proj}_x\), then \[\mathrm{II}:T_x\mathcal M\times T_x\mathcal M\to N_x\mathcal M,\qquad \mathrm{II}(u,v)=\mathcal P_u(v),\] and \[\mathcal W:T_x\mathcal M\times N_x\mathcal M\to T_x\mathcal M,\qquad \mathcal W(u,w)=\mathcal P_u(w).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normal space is the orthogonal complement of the tangent space. Differentiating the tangent projection along a tangent direction defines the second fundamental form on tangent-vector pairs and the Weingarten map on a tangent and a normal vector.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal E\text{ is a Riemannian submanifold of a Euclidean space}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_x\mathcal M=(T_x\mathcal M)^\perp,\qquad \mathrm{II}(u,v)=\mathcal P_u(v)\in N_x\mathcal M,\qquad \mathcal W(u,w)=\mathcal P_u(w)\in T_x\mathcal M

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Relatively Open Subsets Are Embedded Submanifolds

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any relatively open subset U of an embedded submanifold M is itself an embedded submanifold of the same ambient space. It has the same dimension and tangent spaces as M, although it need not be ambiently open.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ambient Characterization of Smooth Maps into an Embedded Submanifold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of intrinsic and ambient smoothness for a submanifold-valued map, globally or at a point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M\) be an embedded submanifold of \(\overline{\mathcal M}\), let \(\mathcal N\) be a manifold, and let \(F:\mathcal N\to\mathcal M\). Define \(\bar F:\mathcal N\to\overline{\mathcal M}\) by \(\bar F(y)=F(y)\). Then \(F\) is smooth if and only if \(\bar F\) is smooth. For every \(x\in\mathcal N\), \(F\) is smooth at \(x\) if and only if \(\bar F\) is smooth at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A map into an embedded submanifold is smooth, globally or at a domain point, exactly when the same map viewed as ambient-manifold-valued is smooth.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M\) is an embedded submanifold of \(\overline{\mathcal M}\).
\(F:\mathcal N\to\mathcal M\), with \(\bar F:\mathcal N\to\overline{\mathcal M}\) defined by \(\bar F(y)=F(y)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\in C^\infty(\mathcal N,\mathcal M)\iff \bar F\in C^\infty(\mathcal N,\overline{\mathcal M})\), and for every \(x\in\mathcal N\), \(F\text{ is smooth at }x\iff\bar F\text{ is smooth at }x\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constant-rank fiber theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Embedded-submanifold structure and dimension of a nonempty fiber when the map has constant rank near that fiber.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F:\mathcal{M}_1\to\mathcal{M}_2 be smooth, with \dim\mathcal{M}_1=d_1 and \dim\mathcal{M}_2=d_2, and let y\in F(\mathcal{M}_1). If F has constant rank k<d_1 on a neighborhood of F^{-1}(y), then F^{-1}(y) is a closed embedded submanifold of \mathcal{M}_1 of dimension d_1-k.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a smooth map has constant rank k less than the source dimension on a neighborhood of a nonempty fiber, then that fiber is a closed embedded submanifold of dimension equal to the source dimension minus k.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ has constant rank }k<d_1\text{ on a neighborhood of }F^{-1}(y)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F^{-1}(y)\text{ is a closed embedded submanifold of }\mathcal{M}_1,\quad \dim F^{-1}(y)=d_1-k.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Embedded submanifold and local defining function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines embedded submanifolds of a finite-dimensional linear ambient space, including open and positive-codimension cases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal E\) be a \(d\)-dimensional linear space and let \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal E\). The set \(\mathcal M\) is a smooth embedded submanifold of dimension \(n\) if either: (i) \(n=d\) and \(\mathcal M\) is open in \(\mathcal E\); or (ii) \(n=d-k\) for some \(k\geq1\), and for every \(x\in\mathcal M\) there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(x\) and a smooth map \(h:U\to\mathbb R^k\) such that \(\mathcal M\cap U=\{y\in U:h(y)=0\}\) and \(\operatorname{rank}Dh(x)=k\). Such an \(h\) is a local defining function at \(x\). A linear subspace that is a manifold is also called a linear manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty subset is an embedded submanifold when it is open of full dimension or, locally at every point, is the zero set of a smooth map whose derivative has full rank. Such a map is a local defining function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal M\text{ is an embedded submanifold of dimension }n\) under exactly the stated open-set or full-rank local zero-set conditions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Defining-Function Characterization of Embedded Submanifolds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes nonempty embedded submanifolds as open submanifolds or locally regular zero sets of fixed positive codimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \varnothing\neq\mathcal M\subseteq\overline{\mathcal M}, where \overline{\mathcal M} is a manifold. Then \mathcal M is an embedded submanifold of \overline{\mathcal M} if and only if either: (i) \mathcal M is open in \overline{\mathcal M}, in which case \dim\mathcal M=\dim\overline{\mathcal M}; or (ii) there is a fixed integer k\geq1 such that, for every x\in\mathcal M, there are a neighborhood \overline{\mathcal U} of x and a smooth map h:\overline{\mathcal U}\to\mathbb R^k with h^{-1}(0)=\mathcal M\cap\overline{\mathcal U} and \operatorname{rank}\mathrm Dh(x)=k. In case (ii), \dim\mathcal M=\dim\overline{\mathcal M}-k and \mathrm T_x\mathcal M=\ker\mathrm Dh(x)\subseteq\mathrm T_x\overline{\mathcal M}, using the identification induced by the inclusion map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty subset is an embedded submanifold exactly when it is open in the ambient manifold or, with a fixed positive codimension, is locally the zero set of a defining function whose differential has full rank at the point. In the latter case its tangent space is the kernel of that differential.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal M\text{ is embedded}\iff\bigl[\mathcal M\text{ is open}\bigr]\lor\bigl[\exists k\geq1\ \forall x\in\mathcal M\ \exists(\overline{\mathcal U},h):h^{-1}(0)=\mathcal M\cap\overline{\mathcal U},\ \operatorname{rank}\mathrm Dh(x)=k\bigr];\quad\text{in the second case, }\mathrm T_x\mathcal M=\ker\mathrm Dh(x).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ambient-Extension Representation of the Manifold Differential
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the intrinsic differential with the restriction of an ambient extension's differential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal E\) and \(\mathcal M'\subseteq\mathcal E'\) be embedded smooth submanifolds, let \(F:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M'\) be smooth, and let \(\bar F\) be a smooth ambient extension of \(F\) on a neighborhood of \(x\in\mathcal M\). Then \[\mathrm DF(x)=\left.\mathrm D\bar F(x)\right|_{T_x\mathcal M}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth map between embedded manifolds, its intrinsic differential is the restriction to the source tangent space of the differential of a smooth ambient extension.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal E\) and \(\mathcal M'\subseteq\mathcal E'\) are embedded smooth submanifolds.
\(F:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M'\) is smooth, \(x\in\mathcal M\), and \(\bar F\) is a smooth ambient extension of \(F\) near \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm DF(x)=\left.\mathrm D\bar F(x)\right|_{T_x\mathcal M}.\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cartesian Products of Embedded Submanifolds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Embeddedness, dimension, and tangent spaces of a product of two embedded submanifolds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M\) and \(\mathcal M'\) be embedded submanifolds of linear spaces \(\mathcal E\) and \(\mathcal E'\), respectively. Then \(\mathcal M\times\mathcal M'\) is an embedded submanifold of \(\mathcal E\times\mathcal E'\) with \(\dim(\mathcal M\times\mathcal M')=\dim\mathcal M+\dim\mathcal M'\). For every \((x,x')\in\mathcal M\times\mathcal M'\), \[T_{(x,x')}(\mathcal M\times\mathcal M')=T_x\mathcal M\times T_{x'}\mathcal M'.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Cartesian product of two embedded submanifolds is embedded in the product ambient space. Its dimension is the sum of the factor dimensions, and its tangent space is the product of the factor tangent spaces.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal E\text{ and }\mathcal M'\subseteq\mathcal E'\text{ are embedded submanifolds}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal M\times\mathcal M'\subseteq\mathcal E\times\mathcal E'\text{ is embedded},\quad \dim(\mathcal M\times\mathcal M')=\dim\mathcal M+\dim\mathcal M',\quad T_{(x,x')}(\mathcal M\times\mathcal M')=T_x\mathcal M\times T_{x'}\mathcal M'.

knowledge_statements.title: Regular Level-Set Manifolds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regular-value theorem for Euclidean equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be smooth, let \(c\in\mathbb R^m\), and suppose \(DF(x)\) has rank \(m\) for every \(x\in F^{-1}(c)\). Then \(M=F^{-1}(c)\) is either empty or an embedded smooth submanifold of \(\mathbb R^n\) of dimension \(n-m\). At every \(x\in M\), its tangent space is \(T_xM=\ker DF(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A level set with full-row-rank constraint Jacobian is an embedded manifold whose tangent space is the Jacobian kernel.
assumptions_latex: \(c\in\mathbb R^m\) is a regular value of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M=F^{-1}(c)\) is an embedded \((n-m)\)-manifold and \(T_xM=\ker DF(x)\) for every \(x\in M\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Embedded Regular Level-Set Manifold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regular common-zero-set representation of a finite-dimensional embedded differentiable manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $h_i\in C^1(\mathbb R^n,\mathbb R)$ for $i=1,\ldots,n-k$, and let $M=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:h_i(x)=0\text{ for }i=1,\ldots,n-k\}$. If $\nabla h_1(x),\ldots,\nabla h_{n-k}(x)$ are linearly independent at every $x\in M$, then $M$ is a $k$-dimensional differentiable manifold embedded in $\mathbb R^n$. Equivalently, every point of $M$ is regular for this constraint representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The common zero set of n−k continuously differentiable functions on R^n is a k-dimensional embedded differentiable manifold if their gradients are linearly independent at every point of the zero set. Every point is then regular for the given constraint representation.
assumptions_latex: \{\nabla h_i(x)\}_{i=1}^{n-k}\text{ is linearly independent for every }x\in M
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ is a }k\text{-dimensional differentiable manifold embedded in }\mathbb R^n.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regular Level-Set Submanifold Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives closedness, embeddedness, dimension, and tangent spaces for a nonempty level set whose defining map is surjective along the level set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let h:\overline{\mathcal M}\to\mathcal N be smooth, let \alpha\in\mathcal N, and suppose \varnothing\neq\mathcal M=h^{-1}(\alpha). If \operatorname{rank}\mathrm Dh(x)=\dim\mathcal N for every x\in\mathcal M, then \mathcal M is closed in \overline{\mathcal M}, is an embedded submanifold of \overline{\mathcal M} with \dim\mathcal M=\dim\overline{\mathcal M}-\dim\mathcal N, and satisfies \mathrm T_x\mathcal M=\ker\mathrm Dh(x) for every x\in\mathcal M.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonempty level set on which the defining map has full rank is closed and is an embedded submanifold. Its codimension is the target manifold's dimension, and its tangent space is the kernel of the differential.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal M\text{ is closed in }\overline{\mathcal M}\text{ and embedded},\quad \dim\mathcal M=\dim\overline{\mathcal M}-\dim\mathcal N,\quad \mathrm T_x\mathcal M=\ker\mathrm Dh(x)\quad\forall x\in\mathcal M.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tangent space from a local defining function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the curve-defined tangent space of an embedded submanifold with the ambient space in the open case and with a defining-map derivative kernel otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M\) be an embedded submanifold of \(\mathcal E\), let \(x\in\mathcal M\), and let \(T_x\mathcal M\) be defined through velocities of smooth curves. If \(\mathcal M\) is an open submanifold, then \(T_x\mathcal M=\mathcal E\). Otherwise, \(T_x\mathcal M=\ker Dh(x)\) for any local defining function \(h\) at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The tangent space of an open submanifold is the whole ambient space. In positive codimension, it is the kernel of the derivative of any local defining function.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M\subseteq\mathcal E\text{ is an embedded submanifold}\)
\(T_x\mathcal M\text{ is defined by smooth-curve velocities}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal M\text{ open}\Rightarrow T_x\mathcal M=\mathcal E;\qquad \mathcal M\text{ not open}\Rightarrow T_x\mathcal M=\ker Dh(x)\text{ for any local defining function }h.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Tangent–Normal Decompositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal splitting for embedded Riemannian submanifolds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be an embedded smooth submanifold with the metric induced by the Euclidean inner product. For every \(x\in M\), define the normal space by \(N_xM=(T_xM)^\perp\). Then the ambient space has the orthogonal direct-sum decomposition \(\mathbb R^n=T_xM\oplus N_xM\). Consequently every \(z\in\mathbb R^n\) has unique components \(z_T\in T_xM\) and \(z_N\in N_xM\) satisfying \(z=z_T+z_N\) and \(\langle z_T,z_N\rangle=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each point of an embedded Euclidean manifold, every ambient vector splits uniquely into orthogonal tangent and normal components.
assumptions_latex: \(M\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is an embedded smooth submanifold.
\(M\) has the metric induced by the Euclidean inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb R^n=T_xM\oplus N_xM\) orthogonally for every \(x\in M\).

knowledge_statements.title: Ambient Projection Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal tangent and normal projectors for regular level sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=F^{-1}(c)\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), where \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is smooth and \(J=DF(x)\) has full row rank at \(x\in M\). Since \(T_xM=\ker J\) and \(N_xM=\operatorname{range}(J^\top)\), the Euclidean orthogonal projectors are \[P_{N_xM}=J^\top(JJ^\top)^{-1}J,\qquad P_{T_xM}=I-J^\top(JJ^\top)^{-1}J.\] Thus any ambient vector \(z\) decomposes as \(z=P_{T_xM}z+P_{N_xM}z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For full-rank equality constraints, tangent and normal projections are explicit matrix expressions involving the constraint Jacobian.
assumptions_latex: \(M=F^{-1}(c)\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a regular level-set manifold.
\(J=DF(x)\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean equality constraints with full-row-rank Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal{M}=\{y\in U:c(y)=0\}\). The embedded constraint-qualification interface at \(x\in\mathcal{M}\) is the surjectivity condition \(Dc(x):\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\). \[
T_x\mathcal{M}=\ker Dc(x),\qquad N_x\mathcal{M}=\operatorname{range} Dc(x)^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Thus ambient equality-constraint derivatives provide the tangent-normal interface used by manifold algorithms.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Armijo Line Search for the Rayleigh Quotient on the Sphere
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies a retraction-based steepest-descent iteration for a symmetric-matrix Rayleigh quotient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A=A^T\), \(\bar\alpha>0\), \(\beta,\sigma\in(0,1)\), and \(x_0\in S^{n-1}\), for \(k=0,1,\ldots\) compute \(\eta_k=-2(Ax_k-x_kx_k^TAx_k)\). Choose the smallest integer \(m_k\geq0\) such that \[f\!\left(R_{x_k}(\bar\alpha\beta^{m_k}\eta_k)\right)\leq f(x_k)-\sigma\bar\alpha\beta^{m_k}\eta_k^T\eta_k,\] where \(f\) is the Rayleigh quotient restricted to \(S^{n-1}\) and \(R\) is the specified sphere retraction. Set \(x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(\bar\alpha\beta^{m_k}\eta_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a unit vector, take the negative Riemannian gradient of the Rayleigh quotient, backtrack geometrically until the retracted trial point satisfies Armijo decrease, and accept that retracted point as the next iterate.
assumptions_latex: R\text{ is the specified retraction on }S^{n-1}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(\bar\alpha\beta^{m_k}\eta_k),\quad m_k=\min\left\{m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}:f(R_{x_k}(\bar\alpha\beta^m\eta_k))\leq f(x_k)-\sigma\bar\alpha\beta^m\|\eta_k\|^2\right\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Orbit and orbit space of a group action
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses a left action; the right-action construction is analogous. No manifold structure on the orbit space is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a left action $\theta$ of $\mathcal G$ on $\overline{\mathcal M}$, the orbit of $x\in\overline{\mathcal M}$ is $\mathcal Gx=\{\theta(g,x):g\in\mathcal G\}$. The relation $x\sim y\iff \exists g\in\mathcal G\text{ such that }y=\theta(g,x)$ is an equivalence relation, and its equivalence classes are precisely the orbits. The quotient $\overline{\mathcal M}/\!\sim$, denoted $\overline{\mathcal M}/\mathcal G$, is the orbit space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The orbit of a point consists of all points reached by the group action. Being in the same orbit is an equivalence relation, and the resulting quotient set is the orbit space.
assumptions_latex: \theta:\mathcal G\times\overline{\mathcal M}\to\overline{\mathcal M}\text{ is a left group action}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\sim y\iff y\in\mathcal Gx,\qquad \overline{\mathcal M}/\mathcal G=\{\mathcal Gx:x\in\overline{\mathcal M}\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Invariant functions and descent to a quotient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines invariance and the uniquely induced function on the quotient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\pi:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M/\!\sim\) be the quotient projection. A function \(f\) on \(\mathcal M\) is invariant under \(\sim\) if \(x\sim y\) implies \(f(x)=f(y)\). In that case there is a unique function \(\widetilde f\) on \(\mathcal M/\!\sim\) such that \(f=\widetilde f\circ\pi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function is invariant when it is constant on every equivalence class. Such a function descends uniquely to the quotient.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Acceleration of a quotient curve through a horizontal lift
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines intrinsic acceleration and gives its total-space horizontal-lift representation and norm bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal M\) be a Riemannian quotient manifold of \(\overline{\mathcal M}\) with canonical projection \(\pi\). If \(\bar c\) is a smooth horizontal curve and \(c=\pi\circ\bar c\), then
\[
c''(t):=\frac{D}{dt}c'(t)=D\pi(\bar c(t))[\bar c''(t)],
\qquad
\operatorname{lift}_{\bar c(t)}(c''(t))=\operatorname{Proj}^{H}_{\bar c(t)}(\bar c''(t)).
\]
Consequently,
\[
\|c''(t)\|_{c(t)}=\|\operatorname{Proj}^{H}_{\bar c(t)}\bar c''(t)\|_{\bar c(t)}\leq \|\bar c''(t)\|_{\bar c(t)}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The acceleration of a quotient curve is the pushforward of its horizontal lift's acceleration. Its horizontal lift is the horizontal projection of the total-space acceleration, so acceleration norm cannot increase upon passage to the quotient.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M\) is a Riemannian quotient manifold of \(\overline{\mathcal M}\) with canonical projection \(\pi\).
\(\bar c\) is a smooth horizontal curve and \(c=\pi\circ\bar c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c''(t)=D\pi(\bar c(t))[\bar c''(t)],\quad \operatorname{lift}_{\bar c(t)}(c''(t))=\operatorname{Proj}^{H}_{\bar c(t)}(\bar c''(t)),\quad \|c''(t)\|_{c(t)}\leq\|\bar c''(t)\|_{\bar c(t)}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Extrema and Saddles of the Spherical Rayleigh Quotient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies eigenvector critical points of a symmetric-matrix Rayleigh quotient on the unit sphere.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=A^T\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) have eigenvalues \(\lambda_1\leq\cdots\leq\lambda_n\) and associated orthonormal eigenvectors \(v_1,\ldots,v_n\). On \(S^{n-1}\), \(\pm v_1\) are local and global minimizers of the Rayleigh quotient, and if \(\lambda_1\) is simple they are its only minimizers. Likewise, \(\pm v_n\) are local and global maximizers, and if \(\lambda_n\) is simple they are its only maximizers. If \(\lambda_1<\lambda_q<\lambda_n\), then \(\pm v_q\) are saddle points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eigenvectors for the smallest eigenvalue minimize the Rayleigh quotient on the sphere, those for the largest eigenvalue maximize it, and eigenvectors for strictly interior eigenvalues are saddle points. Simplicity of an extreme eigenvalue makes its antipodal eigenvectors the only corresponding extrema.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \pm v_1\text{ are global and local minimizers};\quad \pm v_n\text{ are global and local maximizers};\quad \lambda_1<\lambda_q<\lambda_n\Rightarrow \pm v_q\text{ are saddles}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smooth-atlas and Hausdorff components of quotient regularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates the conditions producing the smooth quotient atlas from the closed-graph condition producing Hausdorffness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\sim\) be an equivalence relation on a manifold \(\mathcal M\), and let \(G=\operatorname{graph}(\sim)\). The conditions that \(G\) be an embedded submanifold of \(\mathcal M\times\mathcal M\) and that \(\pi_1:G\to\mathcal M\) be a submersion are necessary and sufficient for \(\mathcal M/\!\sim\) to admit an atlas making the canonical projection \(\pi\) a submersion. Such an atlas is unique, and its atlas topology equals the quotient topology. The condition that \(G\) be closed in \(\mathcal M\times\mathcal M\) is necessary and sufficient for the quotient topology to be Hausdorff.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Embeddedness of the relation graph and submersivity of its first projection are exactly the conditions for a unique quotient atlas under which the canonical projection is a submersion; this atlas induces the quotient topology. Closedness of the graph is exactly the additional condition for that topology to be Hausdorff.
assumptions_latex: \(\sim\) is an equivalence relation on \(\mathcal M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G\text{ embedded and }\pi_1\text{ a submersion}\iff\mathcal M/\!\sim\text{ admits the stated unique atlas}\); its atlas topology equals the quotient topology, and \(G\text{ closed}\iff\text{the quotient topology is Hausdorff}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometry and dimension of quotient fibers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes equivalence classes as embedded positive-dimensional fibers or discrete zero-dimensional fibers according to the quotient dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M/\!\sim\) be a quotient manifold of a manifold \(\mathcal M\), and let \(\pi\) be the canonical projection. For every \(x\in\mathcal M\), if \(\dim(\mathcal M/\!\sim)<\dim(\mathcal M)\), then \(\pi^{-1}(\pi(x))\) is an embedded submanifold of \(\mathcal M\) of dimension \(\dim(\mathcal M)-\dim(\mathcal M/\!\sim)\). If \(\dim(\mathcal M/\!\sim)=\dim(\mathcal M)\), then \(\pi^{-1}(\pi(x))\) is a discrete set of points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the quotient has smaller dimension than the total space, each equivalence class is an embedded submanifold whose dimension is the dimension difference. When the dimensions agree, each equivalence class is discrete.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M/\!\sim\) is a quotient manifold of \(\mathcal M\).
\(\pi:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M/\!\sim\) is the canonical projection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\dim(\mathcal M/\!\sim)<\dim(\mathcal M)\), then \(\pi^{-1}(\pi(x))\) is embedded with dimension \(\dim(\mathcal M)-\dim(\mathcal M/\!\sim)\); if the dimensions are equal, then \(\pi^{-1}(\pi(x))\) is discrete.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compact free actions yield globally liftable quotient manifolds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quotient-manifold existence and horizontal-lifting consequences for compact free Lie-group actions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal G\) be a compact Lie group acting smoothly and freely on \(\overline{\mathcal M}\). Then \(\mathcal M=\overline{\mathcal M}/\mathcal G\) is a quotient manifold. For every smooth curve \(c:I\to\mathcal M\) with \(\dot c(t)\ne0\) for all \(t\in I\), every \(t_0\in I\), and every \(x_0\in\pi^{-1}(c(t_0))\), there exists a unique horizontal lift \(\bar c:I\to\overline{\mathcal M}\) such that \(\pi\circ\bar c=c\) and \(\bar c(t_0)=x_0\). Moreover, \(c\) is a geodesic if and only if \(\bar c\) is a geodesic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth free action of a compact Lie group produces a quotient manifold. Every regular smooth quotient curve has a unique whole-domain horizontal lift through any chosen representative, and the quotient curve is geodesic exactly when its lift is geodesic.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal G\) is a compact Lie group.
\(\mathcal G\) acts smoothly and freely on \(\overline{\mathcal M}\).
\(c:I\to\overline{\mathcal M}/\mathcal G\) is smooth and \(\dot c(t)\ne0\) for all \(t\in I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\overline{\mathcal M}/\mathcal G\text{ is a quotient manifold};\quad \exists!\bar c\text{ horizontal with }\pi\circ\bar c=c,\ \bar c(t_0)=x_0;\quad c\text{ is geodesic}\iff\bar c\text{ is geodesic}.\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalent criteria for a proper Lie-group action
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes properness through convergent sequences and compact transporter sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal G\) act smoothly on \(\overline{\mathcal M}\) through \(\theta\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth Lie-group action, properness is equivalent to a sequential compactness criterion for group elements and to compactness of every compact-set transporter.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quotient set, canonical projection, and quotient topology
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Foundational quotient-space structure induced by an equivalence relation on a manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\sim\) be an equivalence relation on a manifold \(\overline{\mathcal M}\). The quotient set is \(\mathcal M=\overline{\mathcal M}/\!\sim=\{[x]:x\in\overline{\mathcal M}\}\), and the canonical projection is \(\pi:\overline{\mathcal M}\to\mathcal M\), \(\pi(x)=[x]\). The quotient topology is defined by \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal M\text{ open}\iff\pi^{-1}(\mathcal U)\text{ open in }\overline{\mathcal M}\); with this topology, \(\pi\) is continuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quotient consists of the equivalence classes, and the canonical projection maps each point to its class. A subset of the quotient is open exactly when its inverse image is open in the original manifold; consequently, the projection is continuous.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal M=\overline{\mathcal M}/\!\sim\), \(\pi(x)=[x]\), and \(\mathcal U\text{ is open in }\mathcal M\iff\pi^{-1}(\mathcal U)\text{ is open in }\overline{\mathcal M}\); hence \(\pi\) is continuous.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Graph characterization of regular equivalence relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives jointly necessary and sufficient embeddedness, submersion, and closedness conditions, together with the quotient-dimension formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\sim\) be an equivalence relation on a manifold \(\mathcal M\), and let \(G:=\operatorname{graph}(\sim)=\{(x,y)\in\mathcal M\times\mathcal M:x\sim y\}\). Then \(\sim\) is regular if and only if all three conditions hold: \(G\) is an embedded submanifold of \(\mathcal M\times\mathcal M\); the projection \(\pi_1:G\to\mathcal M\), \(\pi_1(x,y)=x\), is a submersion; and \(G\) is closed in \(\mathcal M\times\mathcal M\). Under these conditions, \(\dim(\mathcal M/\!\sim)=2\dim(\mathcal M)-\dim(G)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equivalence relation is regular exactly when its graph is an embedded submanifold, projection from the graph onto the first factor is a submersion, and the graph is closed. When these joint conditions hold, the quotient dimension is twice the dimension of the original manifold minus the graph dimension.
assumptions_latex: \(\sim\) is an equivalence relation on \(\mathcal M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sim\text{ is regular}\iff\bigl(G\text{ is embedded}\bigr)\land\bigl(\pi_1:G\to\mathcal M\text{ is a submersion}\bigr)\land\bigl(G\text{ is closed}\bigr)\), and then \(\dim(\mathcal M/\!\sim)=2\dim(\mathcal M)-\dim(G)\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the quotient set and canonical projection, then defines a quotient-manifold structure by the submersion property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M\) be a manifold with an equivalence relation \(\sim\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vertical geometry of a regular group-action quotient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in M\), the vertical space is the tangent space to the fiber of the quotient projection:
\[
\mathcal{V}_x:=T_x\pi^{-1}([x])=T_x(G\cdot x)=\ker d\pi_x.
\]
Equivalently, if \(\mathfrak{g}\) is the Lie algebra of \(G\), then
\[
\mathcal{V}_x=\{\xi_M(x):\xi\in\mathfrak{g}\},
\]
where \(\xi_M(x)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0}\exp(t\xi)\cdot x\). Freeness makes the map \(\xi\mapsto\xi_M(x)\) injective.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At each \(x\in M\), define the horizontal space by
\[
\mathcal{H}_x:=\mathcal{V}_x^{\perp_g}=\{\eta\,\in T_xM:g_x(\eta,
u)=0\ \text{for every }\nu\in\mathcal{V}_x\}.

Because \(d\pi_x\) is surjective with kernel \(\mathcal{V}_x\), its restriction \(d\pi_x|_{\mathcal{H}_x}\) is a linear isomorphism from \(\mathcal{H}_x\) onto \(T_{[x]}(M/G)\). Metric invariance makes the family \(x\mapsto\mathcal{H}_x\) equivariant along each orbit.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal splitting of total-space tangent vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x\in M\), the vertical and horizontal spaces form the orthogonal direct sum
\[
T_xM=\mathcal{V}_x\oplus\mathcal{H}_x.
\]
Consequently, each \(\eta\in T_xM\) has unique components \(\eta^{\mathcal V}\in\mathcal{V}_x\) and \(\eta^{\mathcal H}\in\mathcal{H}_x\) satisfying \(\eta=\eta^{\mathcal V}+\eta^{\mathcal H}\). The associated linear projections obey \(P_x^{\mathcal V}+P_x^{\mathcal H}=I\), \((P_x^{\mathcal V})^2=P_x^{\mathcal V}\), \((P_x^{\mathcal H})^2=P_x^{\mathcal H}\), and \(P_x^{\mathcal V}P_x^{\mathcal H}=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every total-space tangent vector splits uniquely into orthogonal vertical and horizontal components, with complementary idempotent projections.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local frame existence for the vertical and horizontal subbundles of a quotient manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal M=\overline{\mathcal M}/\!\sim be a quotient manifold with canonical projection \pi, \dim\mathcal M=n, and \dim\overline{\mathcal M}=n+k. Furthermore, W_i=\mathrm D\pi[\widehat W_i] for i=1,\ldots,n form a local frame on \pi(\overline{\mathcal U}).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vertical and horizontal spaces of a quotient manifold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the fiber-tangent vertical space and, when the total space is Riemannian, its orthogonal horizontal complement and the resulting direct-sum decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M=\overline{\mathcal M}/\!\sim\) be a quotient manifold with quotient projection \(\pi:\overline{\mathcal M}\to\mathcal M\). For \(x\in\overline{\mathcal M}\), let \(\mathcal F_x=\{y\in\overline{\mathcal M}:y\sim x\}\). The vertical space is \(\mathrm V_x=\mathrm T_x\mathcal F_x=\ker \mathrm D\pi(x)\). If \(\overline{\mathcal M}\) is Riemannian, the horizontal space is \(\mathrm H_x=(\mathrm V_x)^\perp=\{u\in\mathrm T_x\overline{\mathcal M}:\langle u,v\rangle_x=0\text{ for all }v\in\mathrm V_x\}\), and \(\mathrm T_x\overline{\mathcal M}=\mathrm V_x\oplus\mathrm H_x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a representative x of a quotient manifold, the vertical space is the tangent space to its equivalence-class fiber, equivalently the kernel of the differential of the quotient projection. If the total space is Riemannian, the horizontal space is the orthogonal complement of the vertical space, and the total-space tangent space is their direct sum.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal M=\overline{\mathcal M}/\!\sim\text{ is a quotient manifold with quotient projection }\pi
\overline{\mathcal M}\text{ is Riemannian for the horizontal-space definition and orthogonal decomposition}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm V_x=\mathrm T_x\mathcal F_x=\ker\mathrm D\pi(x),\qquad \mathrm H_x=(\mathrm V_x)^\perp,\qquad \mathrm T_x\overline{\mathcal M}=\mathrm V_x\oplus\mathrm H_x.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vertical–Horizontal Decomposition and Horizontal Lift
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines total-space representations of quotient tangent vectors, vertical and horizontal spaces, and the unique horizontal lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \mathcal M=\overline{\mathcal M}/\!\sim be a quotient manifold with canonical projection \pi, let x\in\mathcal M, and choose \bar x\in\pi^{-1}(x). A vector \bar\xi\in T_{\bar x}\overline{\mathcal M} represents \xi\in T_x\mathcal M if \mathrm D\pi(\bar x)[\bar\xi]=\xi. The vertical space is \mathcal V_{\bar x}=T_{\bar x}(\pi^{-1}(x)). A horizontal distribution assigns a complementary subspace \mathcal H_{\bar x}\subseteq T_{\bar x}\overline{\mathcal M} such that T_{\bar x}\overline{\mathcal M}=\mathcal H_{\bar x}\oplus\mathcal V_{\bar x}. Once such a distribution is chosen, every \xi\in T_x\mathcal M has a unique \bar\xi_{\bar x}\in\mathcal H_{\bar x} satisfying \mathrm D\pi(\bar x)[\bar\xi_{\bar x}]=\xi; this is the horizontal lift of \xi at \bar x.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quotient-manifold tangent vector may be represented by any total-space tangent vector mapped to it by the quotient projection. Vertical vectors are tangent to the fiber. Choosing horizontal spaces complementary to the vertical spaces selects exactly one horizontal representative, called the horizontal lift.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal M=\overline{\mathcal M}/\!\sim\text{ is a quotient manifold with canonical projection }\pi
T_{\bar x}\overline{\mathcal M}=\mathcal H_{\bar x}\oplus\mathcal V_{\bar x}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall\xi\in T_x\mathcal M\;\exists!\,\bar\xi_{\bar x}\in\mathcal H_{\bar x}:\ \mathrm D\pi(\bar x)[\bar\xi_{\bar x}]=\xi.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quotient metric induced by an invariant total-space metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \([x]\in M/G\) and \(u,v\in T_{[x]}(M/G)\), let \(u_x^{\mathcal H},v_x^{\mathcal H}\in\mathcal{H}_x\) be their unique horizontal lifts. Define
\[
\bar g_{[x]}(u,v):=g_x(u_x^{\mathcal H},v_x^{\mathcal H}).
\]
Since the action is isometric, this value is independent of the representative \(x\) in its orbit. It therefore defines a Riemannian metric \(\bar g\) on \(M/G\), uniquely characterized by requiring \(d\pi_x|_{\mathcal H_x}\) to be an isometry for every \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Measure quotient tangent vectors by their horizontal lifts. Isometric group action makes the resulting inner product independent of the chosen representative.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Diffeomorphic shape orbit and stabilizer coset space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the orbit of a reference domain and its coset representation, while preserving the conditional Courant-metric claim and the normality boundary for quotient groups.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subset\mathbb R^N\) be open, let \(\Theta\) be a Banach space of mappings \(D\to\mathbb R^N\), and let \(\mathcal F(\Theta)=\{F:D\to D:F\text{ is a diffeomorphism},\ F-I\in\Theta,\ F^{-1}-I\in\Theta\}\). For \(\Omega_0\subset D\), define \(\mathcal X(\Omega_0)=\{F(\Omega_0):F\in\mathcal F(\Theta)\}\) and \(\mathcal G(\Omega_0)=\{F\in\mathcal F(\Theta):F(\Omega_0)=\Omega_0\}\). Then \(\mathcal X(\Omega_0)\) is identified with the coset space \(\mathcal F(\Theta)/\mathcal G(\Omega_0)\). It is a quotient group only if \(\mathcal G(\Omega_0)\) is normal. For the specific admissible choices of \(D,\Theta,\Omega_0\) considered in the source, a Courant metric makes this shape space complete; the resulting space is neither linear nor convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The admissible diffeomorphisms send a reference domain through a shape orbit. Shapes are identified with cosets modulo the diffeomorphisms that preserve the reference domain. This is generally a coset space, not a quotient group unless the stabilizer is normal. For the specified admissible data, the Courant metric makes the shape space complete, while it remains non-linear and nonconvex.
assumptions_latex: \Theta\text{ is a Banach space of mappings }D\to\mathbb R^N
\mathcal F(\Theta)\text{ is the stated group of admissible diffeomorphisms}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal X(\Omega_0)\simeq\mathcal F(\Theta)/\mathcal G(\Omega_0)\text{ as a coset space};\quad \mathcal G(\Omega_0)\trianglelefteq\mathcal F(\Theta)\text{ is additionally required for a quotient group.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Descent of differentiable objectives through a regular quotient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The objective \(f\) is group invariant when \(f(g\cdot x)=f(x)\) for every \(g\in G\) and \(x\in M\). This holds exactly when there is a unique function \(\bar f:M/G\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfying \(f=\bar f\circ\pi\). If \(f\) is differentiable, invariance implies
\[
df_x(\nu)=0\qquad\text{for every }\nu\in\mathcal{V}_x.
\]
Hence, for any metric defining \(\mathcal{H}_x=\mathcal{V}_x^{\perp}\), the Riemannian gradient \(\operatorname{grad}f(x)\) is horizontal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective descends to the quotient exactly when it is constant on every orbit; its derivative then vanishes in all vertical directions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Variational characterization of a leftmost generalized invariant subspace
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global minimization of the generalized trace Rayleigh quotient over full-column-rank representatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A,B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric with \(B\succ0\), and let \(\lambda_1\le\cdots\le\lambda_n\) be the eigenvalues of the pencil \((A,B)\). For \(1\le p\le n\), define \[f(Y)=\operatorname{tr}\!\left(Y^TAY\,(Y^TBY)^{-1}\right)\] for full-column-rank \(Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\). Then the following are equivalent: \(\operatorname{span}(Y_*)\) is a leftmost \(p\)-dimensional invariant subspace of \((A,B)\); \(Y_*\) is a global minimizer of \(f\); and \(f(Y_*)=\sum_{i=1}^p\lambda_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a symmetric matrix pencil with a positive-definite second matrix, a full-rank matrix spans a leftmost p-dimensional invariant subspace exactly when it globally minimizes the generalized trace Rayleigh quotient. The minimum is the sum of the p smallest generalized eigenvalues.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{span}(Y_*)\text{ is a leftmost invariant subspace}\iff Y_*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\operatorname{rank}(Y)=p}f(Y)\iff f(Y_*)=\sum_{i=1}^p\lambda_i.
