knowledge_statements.title: Special-Orthogonal Group Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Embedded Riemannian geometry of the real special-orthogonal group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer \(n\ge 2\), the special-orthogonal group is \(\mathrm{SO}(n)=\{R\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}:R^{\mathsf T}R=I_n,\ \det R=1\}\). It is an embedded manifold and Lie group of dimension \(n(n-1)/2\). Its tangent space at \(R\in\mathrm{SO}(n)\) is \(T_R\mathrm{SO}(n)=\{R\Omega:\Omega^{\mathsf T}=-\Omega\}\). The Frobenius-induced metric is \(g_R(R\Omega_1,R\Omega_2)=\operatorname{tr}(\Omega_1^{\mathsf T}\Omega_2)\). Under this metric, tangent vectors are represented by skew-symmetric generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The determinant-one orthogonal matrices form a smooth Lie group whose tangent vectors are rotations of skew-symmetric matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_R\mathrm{SO}(n)=\{R\Omega:\Omega^{\mathsf T}=-\Omega\}\) and \(\dim\mathrm{SO}(n)=n(n-1)/2\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition, dimension, tangent-space formula, and Frobenius-induced metric are mathematically standard and fit the geometry leaf, but no inspectable citation supports these nontrivial claims.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Special orthogonal group as a metric probability space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the special orthogonal group, its Frobenius metric, and its uniform Haar probability measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For n\in\mathbb{N} with n\ge 1, \operatorname{SO}(n)=\{A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}:A^{\mathsf T}A=I_n,\ \det(A)=1\}. Thus its elements are the orientation-preserving linear isometries of \mathbb{R}^n. It becomes the metric probability space \bigl(\operatorname{SO}(n),d_F,\mu_{\mathrm{Haar}}\bigr), where d_F(A,B)=\lVert A-B\rVert_F and \mu_{\mathrm{Haar}} is the uniform probability measure on \operatorname{SO}(n).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SO(n) is the group of n-by-n orthogonal matrices with determinant one, equivalently the orientation-preserving linear isometries of Euclidean n-space. Frobenius distance and uniform Haar probability make it a metric probability space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{SO}(n)=\{A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}:A^{\mathsf T}A=I_n,\ \det(A)=1\},\quad d_F(A,B)=\lVert A-B\rVert_F,\quad \mu=\mu_{\mathrm{Haar}}.

knowledge_statements.title: Orientation-Component Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connected-component decomposition of the real orthogonal group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\ge 1\), the determinant map \(\det:\mathrm{O}(n)\to\{-1,1\}\) is continuous and constant on every connected subset. Consequently, \(\mathrm{O}(n)\) is the disjoint union \(\mathrm{O}(n)=\mathrm{SO}(n)\sqcup\mathrm{O}^{-}(n)\), where \(\mathrm{O}^{-}(n)=\{Q\in\mathrm{O}(n):\det Q=-1\}\). Each set is a connected component, and multiplication by any fixed reflection \(F\in\mathrm{O}^{-}(n)\) gives a diffeomorphism from \(\mathrm{SO}(n)\) onto \(\mathrm{O}^{-}(n)\). Thus a continuous path of orthogonal matrices cannot reverse orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The orthogonal group has exactly two connected components, distinguished by determinant; continuous orthogonal motion cannot pass between them.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_0(\mathrm{O}(n))=\{\mathrm{SO}(n),\mathrm{O}^{-}(n)\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-component description is standard and the property kind fits the leaf, but the connectedness and diffeomorphism claims have no cited source or locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Stiefel Manifolds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stiefel geometry defined by a positive-definite weighted inner product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite and let \(1\le p\le n\). The generalized Stiefel manifold is \(\mathrm{St}_B(p,n)=\{X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}:X^{\mathsf T}BX=I_p\}\). It is a smooth embedded manifold of dimension \(np-p(p+1)/2\). Differentiating the constraint gives \(T_X\mathrm{St}_B(p,n)=\{Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}:X^{\mathsf T}BZ+Z^{\mathsf T}BX=0\}\). The constraint means that the columns of \(X\) are orthonormal under the inner product \(\langle u,v\rangle_B=u^{\mathsf T}Bv\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generalized Stiefel manifold consists of matrices whose columns are orthonormal in a fixed positive-definite weighted inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_X\mathrm{St}_B(p,n)=\{Z:X^{\mathsf T}BZ+Z^{\mathsf T}BX=0\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted Stiefel definition, dimension, and tangent-space formula are coherent and locally appropriate, but no authoritative source with a specific locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Orthogonality Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Retraction-based interface that preserves orthogonality at every accepted iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(X_0\in\mathrm{St}(p,n)\), a smooth objective \(f\), and a retraction \(R\), repeat: choose a tangent step \(\eta_k\in T_{X_k}\mathrm{St}(p,n)\), select an accepted step length \(\alpha_k\ge0\), and set \(X_{k+1}=R_{X_k}(\alpha_k\eta_k)\). A retraction satisfies \(R_X(0)=X\), has differential \(\mathrm{D}R_X(0)\) equal to the identity on \(T_X\mathrm{St}(p,n)\), and maps its domain into \(\mathrm{St}(p,n)\). Stop under a prescribed stationarity or iteration criterion and return the last feasible iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tangent steps followed by a retraction keep every accepted iterate orthonormal while exposing a standard optimization interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X_k^{\mathsf T}X_k=I_p\) for every generated iterate \(k\).

notation.meaning: retraction based at the feasible point X

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasible Orthogonality Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambient-space interface allowing intermediate violation of orthogonality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\), define the orthogonality residual \(C(X)=X^{\mathsf T}X-I_p\) and violation \(v(X)=\lVert C(X)\rVert_{\mathrm F}\). An infeasible interface permits trial or accepted iterates with \(v(X)>0\) and supplies the objective data together with \(C(X)\) or \(v(X)\) to a constrained optimization method. Feasibility is recovered only asymptotically or by a separate restoration operation. A terminating point is orthogonally feasible precisely when \(v(X)=0\); approximate feasibility at tolerance \(\varepsilon_{m feas}\ge0\) means \(v(X)\le\varepsilon_{m feas}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infeasible interface represents orthogonality by a measurable residual and allows iterates outside the manifold until convergence or restoration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X^{\mathsf T}X=I_p\iff v(X)=0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual representation is precise, but the assertion that feasibility is recovered only asymptotically or through separate restoration is an interface convention that is not universally implied and requires a defining source or qualification.

children.title: Feasibility-Restoration Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Mechanisms connecting infeasible representations back to the orthogonality manifold.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Restoration Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polar-factor restoration of full-rank matrices to the Stiefel manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(Y\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}\) with full column rank, compute \(G=Y^{\mathsf T}Y\) and return \(\mathcal{P}(Y)=YG^{-1/2}\). Since \(G\) is symmetric positive definite, its principal inverse square root exists, and \(\mathcal{P}(Y)^{\mathsf T}\mathcal{P}(Y)=I_p\). Thus \(\mathcal{P}\) restores exact Stiefel feasibility. In the Frobenius norm, \(\mathcal{P}(Y)\) is the unique nearest matrix in \(\mathrm{St}(p,n)\) when \(Y\) has full column rank. If rank is lost, this formula is undefined and the interface must regularize or use another restoration rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The polar factor maps any full-column-rank matrix to its unique nearest orthonormal-column matrix, restoring exact feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal{P}(Y)=Y(Y^{\mathsf T}Y)^{-1/2}\in\mathrm{St}(p,n)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Grassmann Manifolds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quotient model for fixed-dimensional linear subspaces of Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For integers \(0<p<n\), the real Grassmann manifold \(\mathrm{Gr}(p,n)\) is the set of all \(p\)-dimensional linear subspaces of \(\mathbb{R}^n\). It admits the quotient representation \(\mathrm{Gr}(p,n)\cong\mathrm{St}(p,n)/\mathrm{O}(p)\), where orthonormal matrices \(X\) and \(Y\) represent the same point exactly when \(Y=XQ\) for some \(Q\in\mathrm{O}(p)\). Equivalently, a point is represented by the rank-\(p\) orthogonal projector \(P=XX^{\mathsf T}\). The manifold has dimension \(p(n-p)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Grassmann manifold contains fixed-dimensional subspaces, represented equivalently by orthonormal bases modulo basis rotations or by orthogonal projectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{Gr}(p,n)\cong\mathrm{St}(p,n)/\mathrm{O}(p)\) and \(\dim\mathrm{Gr}(p,n)=p(n-p)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The set, quotient, projector, and dimension descriptions are consistent and fit the Grassmann-manifold leaf, but none is backed by an inspectable citation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Grassmann manifold as a quotient of the Stiefel manifold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes k-dimensional subspaces as orthogonal equivalence classes of Stiefel representatives and records invariance of the unweighted PCA objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $1\le k\le d$ and define $U\sim V$ on $\operatorname{St}(d,k)$ by $V=UQ$ for some $Q\in\mathrm O(k)=\{Q\in\mathbb R^{k\times k}:Q^\top Q=I_k\}$. Then $[U]=\{UQ:Q\in\mathrm O(k)\}$, and $U\sim V$ if and only if $\operatorname{col}(U)=\operatorname{col}(V)$. Consequently, $\operatorname{Gr}(d,k)$, the set of $k$-dimensional subspaces of $\mathbb R^d$, is identified with the quotient manifold $\operatorname{St}(d,k)/\mathrm O(k)$. For $X\in\mathbb R^{d\times n}$, $f(U)=\langle XX^\top U,U\rangle$ satisfies $f(UQ)=f(U)$ for every $Q\in\mathrm O(k)$ and therefore depends only on $[U]$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two Stiefel matrices represent the same Grassmann point exactly when they differ by right multiplication by an orthogonal matrix, equivalently when their columns span the same subspace. Thus the Grassmann manifold is the quotient of the Stiefel manifold by the orthogonal group. The unweighted PCA objective is constant on each equivalence class and depends only on the selected subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U\sim V\iff (\exists Q\in\mathrm O(k))\ V=UQ\iff\operatorname{col}(U)=\operatorname{col}(V),\qquad \operatorname{Gr}(d,k)\equiv\operatorname{St}(d,k)/\mathrm O(k),\qquad f(UQ)=f(U).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence and Local Linear Stability of Grassmann Rayleigh Quotient Armijo Iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set convergence and conditional local linear convergence for Algorithm 3 on the Grassmann manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric, let \(1\le p<n\), and order its eigenvalues as \(\lambda_1\le\cdots\le\lambda_n\). If \(\{Y_k\}\) is an infinite sequence generated by Algorithm 3, then \[\operatorname{dist}\!\left(\operatorname{span}(Y_k),\{\text{\(p\)-dimensional invariant subspaces of }A\}\right)\to0.\] If, additionally, \(\lambda_p\) is simple, then the unique invariant subspace associated with \((\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_p)\) is asymptotically stable for the iteration, and convergence to it is linear with factor no greater than \[r_*=1-2\sigma(\lambda_{p+1}-\lambda_p)\min\!\left(\bar\alpha,\frac{2\beta(1-\sigma)}{\lambda_n-\lambda_1}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every infinite sequence generated by Algorithm 3 approaches the set of p-dimensional invariant subspaces of the symmetric matrix. If the pth eigenvalue is simple, the invariant subspace corresponding to the p smallest eigenvalues is uniquely determined and asymptotically stable, with the stated upper bound on its linear convergence factor.
assumptions_latex: \{Y_k\}_{k\ge0}\text{ is an infinite sequence generated by Algorithm 3}
\lambda_p\text{ is simple for the asymptotic-stability and linear-rate conclusion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{dist}\!\left(\operatorname{span}(Y_k),\{\text{\(p\)-dimensional invariant subspaces of }A\}\right)\to0;\quad \lambda_p\text{ simple}\Longrightarrow\text{the invariant subspace for }(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_p)\text{ is asymptotically stable with linear factor at most }r_*.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Armijo Line Search for the Grassmann Rayleigh Quotient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representative-based line-search iteration on \(\operatorname{Grass}(p,n)\), including conditioning-preserving changes of basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given symmetric \(A\), \(\bar\alpha>0\), \(\beta,\sigma\in(0,1)\), and full-rank \(Y_0\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\), for \(k=0,1,\ldots\) compute \[\eta_k=-2\left(AY_k-Y_k(Y_k^TY_k)^{-1}Y_k^TAY_k\right).\] Choose the smallest integer \(m\geq0\) satisfying \[\bar f(Y_k+\bar\alpha\beta^m\eta_k)\leq \bar f(Y_k)-\sigma\bar\alpha\beta^m\operatorname{tr}(\eta_k^T\eta_k),\] and set \[Y_{k+1}=(Y_k+\bar\alpha\beta^m\eta_k)M_k,\] where \(M_k\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}\) is invertible and chosen to preserve good conditioning; in particular, \(Y_{k+1}\) may be taken as the \(Q\) factor of a QR decomposition of the trial matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a full-rank representative, compute the Grassmann Rayleigh quotient descent direction, backtrack by powers of beta until the Armijo decrease condition holds, and apply an invertible change of basis—such as QR orthonormalization—to keep the next representative well conditioned.
assumptions_latex: Y_0\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\text{ has full column rank}
\bar f\text{ is the representative Rayleigh quotient objective}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{Y_k\}_{k\geq0}\text{ is generated by Armijo backtracking and conditioning-preserving invertible representative updates on }\operatorname{Grass}(p,n).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Grassmann manifold as a full-rank matrix quotient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies subspaces with equivalence classes of their full-column-rank matrix representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(1\le p\le n\), and let \(\mathbb R_*^{n\times p}\) be the set of full-column-rank \(n\times p\) matrices. Define \(X\sim Y\) if and only if \(\operatorname{span}(X)=\operatorname{span}(Y)\). The span map induces a bijection \(\operatorname{Grass}(p,n)\simeq\mathbb R_*^{n\times p}/\!\sim\). Moreover, the equivalence class of \(X\) is \(X\mathrm{GL}_p=\{XM:M\in\mathrm{GL}_p\}\), so \(\operatorname{Grass}(p,n)\simeq\mathbb R_*^{n\times p}/\mathrm{GL}_p\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A p-dimensional subspace is represented by any full-rank matrix spanning it. Two matrices represent the same subspace exactly when they differ by an invertible change of column basis, giving the Grassmann set as a matrix quotient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: [X]=X\mathrm{GL}_p,\qquad \operatorname{Grass}(p,n)\simeq\mathbb R_*^{n\times p}/\mathrm{GL}_p

knowledge_statements.title: Flag Manifolds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Manifold of nested real subspaces with prescribed dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0<d_1<\cdots<d_r<n\). The real flag manifold of type \((d_1,\ldots,d_r;n)\) is \(\mathrm{Fl}(d_1,\ldots,d_r;n)=\{(V_1,\ldots,V_r):V_i\le\mathbb{R}^n,\ \dim V_i=d_i,\ V_1\subset\cdots\subset V_r\}\). Setting \(m_1=d_1\), \(m_i=d_i-d_{i-1}\) for \(2\le i\le r\), and \(m_{r+1}=n-d_r\), it has the homogeneous-space representation \(\mathrm{O}(n)/(\mathrm{O}(m_1)\times\cdots\times\mathrm{O}(m_{r+1}))\). Its dimension is \(\sum_{i=1}^{r}m_i(n-d_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A flag manifold consists of nested subspaces with fixed dimensions and is a quotient of the orthogonal group by blockwise basis changes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{Fl}(d_1,\ldots,d_r;n)\cong\mathrm{O}(n)/(\mathrm{O}(m_1)\times\cdots\times\mathrm{O}(m_{r+1}))\).

notation.meaning: real flag manifold of prescribed type

knowledge_statements.title: Projective-Space Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quotient and projector models of real projective space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Real projective space \(\mathbb{RP}^{n-1}\) is the set of one-dimensional linear subspaces of \(\mathbb{R}^n\). It has equivalent representations \(\mathbb{RP}^{n-1}\cong(\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\})/\!\sim\cong S^{n-1}/\{x\sim -x\}\cong\mathrm{Gr}(1,n)\), where \(x\sim y\) in the first quotient exactly when \(y=\lambda x\) for some nonzero \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}\). A unit representative \(x\) also determines the rank-one projector \(P=xx^{\mathsf T}\), which is unchanged by replacing \(x\) with \(-x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Real projective space models lines through the origin using nonzero vectors modulo scaling, antipodal unit vectors, or rank-one projectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{RP}^{n-1}\cong S^{n-1}/\{\pm1\}\cong\mathrm{Gr}(1,n)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quotient, antipodal, Grassmann, and projector models agree and representation is the correct content kind, but no cited source supports the equivalences.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis-versus-Subspace Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between quotient-basis and orthogonal-projector representations of a subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,Y\in\mathrm{St}(p,n)\). The following conditions are equivalent: \(\operatorname{span}(X)=\operatorname{span}(Y)\); there exists \(Q\in\mathrm{O}(p)\) such that \(Y=XQ\); and \(XX^{\mathsf T}=YY^{\mathsf T}\). Hence a subspace objective represented on bases must satisfy \(f(XQ)=f(X)\) for every \(Q\in\mathrm{O}(p)\). Such an objective descends to a well-defined function on \(\mathrm{Gr}(p,n)\), and it may equivalently be expressed using the projector \(P=XX^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orthonormal bases describe the same subspace exactly when related by an orthogonal basis change, equivalently when their projectors coincide.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{span}(X)=\operatorname{span}(Y)\iff Y=XQ\text{ for some }Q\in\mathrm{O}(p)\iff XX^{\mathsf T}=YY^{\mathsf T}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equivalence between spans, orthogonal basis changes, and projectors is mathematically standard and suits the representation-comparison leaf, but it lacks an inspectable source.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric Positive-Definite Manifold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Open-cone manifold of real symmetric positive-definite matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The symmetric positive-definite manifold is \(\mathcal{S}_{++}^n=\{P\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}:P=P^{\mathsf T},\ x^{\mathsf T}Px>0\text{ for every }x\ne0\}\). It is an open convex cone in the vector space \(\mathcal{S}^n\) of symmetric matrices and therefore a smooth manifold of dimension \(n(n+1)/2\). For every \(P\in\mathcal{S}_{++}^n\), its tangent space is canonically \(T_P\mathcal{S}_{++}^n=\mathcal{S}^n\). The cone is closed under positive scaling and congruence transformations \(P\mapsto APA^{\mathsf T}\) by invertible \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-definite symmetric matrices form an open convex cone whose tangent space at every point is the full space of symmetric matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_P\mathcal{S}_{++}^n=\mathcal{S}^n\) and \(\dim\mathcal{S}_{++}^n=n(n+1)/2\).

notation.meaning: vector space of real symmetric matrices

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The open-cone, tangent-space, dimension, scaling, and congruence claims are coherent, but the record cites no source; the inventory's trust-region SPD locator is not attached and does not evidently establish the stated manifold geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Invariant Metrics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard congruence-invariant Riemannian metric on the positive-definite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P\in\mathcal{S}_{++}^n\) and tangent vectors \(U,V\in T_P\mathcal{S}_{++}^n=\mathcal{S}^n\), the affine-invariant metric is \(g_P(U,V)=\operatorname{tr}(P^{-1}UP^{-1}V)\). For every invertible \(A\), the congruence action \(\Phi_A(P)=APA^{\mathsf T}\) has differential \(\mathrm{D}\Phi_A(P)[U]=AUA^{\mathsf T}\) and satisfies \(g_{\Phi_A(P)}(\mathrm{D}\Phi_A(P)[U],\mathrm{D}\Phi_A(P)[V])=g_P(U,V)\). Thus all invertible linear changes of coordinates act by isometries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The affine-invariant metric weights tangent matrices by the inverse base point and is unchanged under invertible congruence transformations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_{APA^{\mathsf T}}(AUA^{\mathsf T},AVA^{\mathsf T})=g_P(U,V)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The metric and congruence-invariance formula are internally consistent and definition is appropriate for this metric leaf, but the claim has no authoritative citation with a specific locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Principal-logarithm formulation on the real SPD manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(P\in\mathcal S_{++}^n\) and \(U,V\in T_P\mathcal S_{++}^n\cong\mathcal S^n\), the log-Euclidean metric is the pullback of the Frobenius inner product through the matrix logarithm:
\[
g_P^{\mathrm{LE}}(U,V)=\left\langle D\log(P)[U],D\log(P)[V]\right\rangle_F.
\]
Consequently, the logarithm is a global isometry from \(\mathcal S_{++}^n\) to \(\mathcal S^n\), the induced distance is
\[
d_{\mathrm{LE}}(P,Q)=\|\log P-\log Q\|_F,
\]
and the unique minimizing geodesic joining \(P\) to \(Q\) is \(\gamma(t)=\exp((1-t)\log P+t\log Q)\) for \(0\le t\le1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The logarithm identifies positive-definite matrices with a Euclidean space; Euclidean interpolation of their logarithms gives the log-Euclidean distance and geodesic.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representative alternatives to affine-invariant and log-Euclidean metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Two related metric families on \(\mathcal S_{++}^n\) are represented as follows. For \(\alpha\ne0\), the power-Euclidean distance is
\[
d_\alpha(P,Q)=\frac{1}{|\alpha|}\|P^\alpha-Q^\alpha\|_F.
\]
The Bures-Wasserstein distance is
\[
d_{\mathrm{BW}}^2(P,Q)=\operatorname{tr}P+\operatorname{tr}Q-2\operatorname{tr}\!\left(P^{1/2}QP^{1/2}\right)^{1/2}.
\]
The first is obtained by embedding positive-definite matrices through \(P\mapsto P^\alpha/\alpha\); the second is the quotient distance induced by representing \(P\) as \(YY^\top\) and identifying factors under right orthogonal transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Power-Euclidean metrics compare matrix powers, whereas the Bures-Wasserstein metric is induced by Euclidean distances between square-root factors modulo orthogonal transformations.

children.title: Positive-Definite Metric Comparison

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(PQ=QP\), then \(d_{\mathrm{AI}}(P,Q)=d_{\mathrm{LE}}(P,Q)\); their invariance groups differ in general.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison by commuting matrices and transformation invariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The affine-invariant and log-Euclidean distances are
\[
d_{\mathrm{AI}}(P,Q)=\|\log(P^{-1/2}QP^{-1/2})\|_F,
\qquad
d_{\mathrm{LE}}(P,Q)=\|\log P-\log Q\|_F.
\]
If \(P\) and \(Q\) commute, simultaneous orthogonal diagonalization gives \(d_{\mathrm{AI}}(P,Q)=d_{\mathrm{LE}}(P,Q)\). Their global invariances differ: for every \(G\in\mathrm{GL}(n)\),
\[
d_{\mathrm{AI}}(GPG^\top,GQG^\top)=d_{\mathrm{AI}}(P,Q),
\]
whereas the log-Euclidean distance is generally invariant under orthogonal congruence but not under arbitrary invertible congruence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine-invariant and log-Euclidean distances agree for commuting positive-definite matrices, but only the affine-invariant distance is invariant under every invertible congruence.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Rank Positive-Semidefinite Quotients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-rank factors modulo right orthogonal transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(1\le r\le n\), let \(\mathbb R_*^{n\times r}=\{Y\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}:\operatorname{rank}(Y)=r\}\), and let \(\mathrm O(r)\) act by \(Y\cdot O=YO\). The Gram map \(\pi(Y)=YY^\top\) induces the quotient representation
\[
\bar\pi:\mathbb R_*^{n\times r}/\mathrm O(r)\longrightarrow\mathcal S_+^n(r),
\qquad [Y]\longmapsto YY^\top,
\]
where \(\mathcal S_+^n(r)=\{X\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}:X=X^\top,\ X\succeq0,\ \operatorname{rank}(X)=r\}\). Two full-column-rank factors represent the same matrix exactly when they differ by a right orthogonal transformation. Consequently, objectives on \(\mathcal S_+^n(r)\) lift to right-orthogonally invariant objectives on the factor space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank-r positive-semidefinite matrices are represented by full-column-rank Gram factors modulo right orthogonal transformations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb R_*^{n\times r}/\mathrm O(r)\) is identified with \(\mathcal S_+^n(r)\) by \([Y]\mapsto YY^\top\).

assumptions_latex: Convergence is measured in any matrix norm on the finite-dimensional ambient space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\overline{\mathcal S_{++}^n}=\mathcal S_+^n\), but singular points of \(\mathcal S_+^n\) lie outside the SPD manifold and its logarithmic geometry.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of SPD manifold structure at singular limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The positive-semidefinite cone is the closure of the positive-definite cone:
\[
\overline{\mathcal S_{++}^n}=\mathcal S_+^n,
\qquad
\partial\mathcal S_{++}^n=\{P\in\mathcal S_+^n:\lambda_{\min}(P)=0\}.
\]
For any singular \(X\in\mathcal S_+^n\), the sequence \(X_k=X+k^{-1}I\) lies in \(\mathcal S_{++}^n\) and converges to \(X\). However, \(X\) has no finite principal matrix logarithm, and affine-invariant or log-Euclidean expressions requiring an inverse or logarithm do not extend to it by direct substitution. Rank strata on this boundary therefore require fixed-rank or stratified geometry rather than the SPD manifold model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Singular positive-semidefinite matrices are limits of positive-definite matrices, but inverses and logarithms fail there, so SPD metric formulas cannot be directly retained.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Semidefinite Boundary Regime

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed-Rank Matrix Manifold, Factorization, and Closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the exact-rank matrix manifold, its embedded and quotient representations, its closure boundary, and its role as the feasible set in fixed-rank matrix completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For integers \(m,n\ge 1\) and \(1\le r\le \min\{m,n\}\), define \(\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}_r=\{X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}:\operatorname{rank}(X)=r\}\). This set is an embedded submanifold of \(\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\). Every \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}_r\) can be written as \(X=LR^\top\), where \(L\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times r}\) and \(R\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times r}\) have full column rank. For every \(J\in\mathrm{GL}(r)\), the pairs \((L,R)\) and \((LJ^{-1},RJ^\top)\) represent the same matrix, leading to a quotient-manifold representation. Moreover, \(\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}_r\) is not closed and \(\overline{\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}_r}=\{X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}:\operatorname{rank}(X)\le r\}\). When \(r<\min\{m,n\}\), this closure is not a manifold; when \(r=\min\{m,n\}\), it is the ambient space. Given observed entries \(M_{ij}\) indexed by \(\Omega\), fixed-rank matrix completion is modeled by \(\min_{X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}_r}\sum_{(i,j)\in\Omega}(X_{ij}-M_{ij})^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrices of exactly rank r form an embedded manifold. They admit full-column-rank factorizations X = LRᵀ whose equivalent factor pairs differ by an invertible change of basis, yielding a quotient-manifold representation. The exact-rank set is not closed; its closure consists of matrices of rank at most r. That closure is nonmanifold for a nonmaximal rank bound, while for maximal feasible r it is the whole ambient space. Fixed-rank matrix completion performs least-squares fitting of observed entries over this manifold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}_r\text{ is an embedded manifold admitting a quotient factorization model},\quad \overline{\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}_r}=\{X:\operatorname{rank}(X)\le r\},\quad \min_{X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}_r}\sum_{(i,j)\in\Omega}(X_{ij}-M_{ij})^2\text{ models fixed-rank completion.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Noncompact Stiefel manifold of full-column-rank matrices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the full-column-rank manifold, its open-submanifold structure and global coordinate representation, and its cases p=1 and p=n.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For integers $1\le p\le n$, let $\mathbb{R}_*^{n\times p}=\{X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}:\operatorname{rank}(X)=p\}$. Its complement is the closed set $\{X\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}:\det(X^TX)=0\}$, so $\mathbb{R}_*^{n\times p}$ is open in $\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}$ and therefore is an open smooth submanifold. Vectorization gives a global chart from this manifold onto the open subset $\operatorname{vec}(\mathbb{R}_*^{n\times p})\subset\mathbb{R}^{np}$. This is the noncompact Stiefel manifold. Moreover, $\mathbb{R}_*^{n\times1}=\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\}$ and $\mathbb{R}_*^{n\times n}=\mathrm{GL}_n$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For 1 ≤ p ≤ n, the full-column-rank n-by-p matrices form an open smooth submanifold of the ambient matrix space. Vectorization provides global coordinates whose image is an open subset of R^(np). This is called the noncompact Stiefel manifold; for p=1 it is punctured Euclidean space, and for p=n it is the general linear group.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb{R}_*^{n\times p}\text{ is an open smooth submanifold of }\mathbb{R}^{n\times p};\quad \mathbb{R}_*^{n\times1}=\mathbb{R}^n\setminus\{0\},\quad \mathbb{R}_*^{n\times n}=\mathrm{GL}_n.

knowledge_statements.title: Embedded Fixed-Rank Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-exactly-r matrices embedded in Euclidean matrix space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(1\le r<\min(m,n)\), the set
\[
\mathcal M_r=\{X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}:\operatorname{rank}(X)=r\}
\]
is a smooth embedded submanifold of \(\mathbb R^{m\times n}\). Let \(X=U\Sigma V^\top\) be a compact singular value decomposition, where \(U\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}\), \(V\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\), and let \(U_\perp\in\mathbb R^{m\times(m-r)}\) and \(V_\perp\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-r)}\) be orthonormal complements. Then
\[
T_X\mathcal M_r=\{UMV^\top+U_\perp KV^\top+ULV_\perp^\top:M\in\mathbb R^{r\times r},\ K\in\mathbb R^{(m-r)\times r},\ L\in\mathbb R^{r\times(n-r)}\}.
\]
The dimension of \(\mathcal M_r\) is \(r(m+n-r)\), and the ambient Frobenius inner product restricts to a Riemannian metric on its tangent spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrices of rank exactly r form a smooth embedded manifold of dimension r(m+n-r), with explicitly parameterized tangent spaces and the induced Frobenius metric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal M_r\) is an embedded manifold of dimension \(r(m+n-r)\) with the stated tangent-space representation.

notation.meaning: Embedded manifold of matrices of rank exactly r
Compact singular value decomposition of X

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard embedded-manifold model for fixed-rank matrices

knowledge_statements.title: Factorized Fixed-Rank Quotients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-factor model modulo invertible gauge transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(1\le r<\min(m,n)\), let \(\mathcal F=\mathbb R_*^{m\times r}\times\mathbb R_*^{n\times r}\), and let \(\mathcal M_r=\{X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}:\operatorname{rank}(X)=r\}\). Every \(X\in\mathcal M_r\) has a factorization \(X=LR^\top\) with \((L,R)\in\mathcal F\). The group \(\mathrm{GL}(r)\) acts freely on \(\mathcal F\) by
\[
(L,R)\cdot G=(LG,RG^{-\top}),
\]
and the product \(LR^\top\) is constant on each orbit. Two full-column-rank factor pairs represent the same matrix exactly when they lie in the same orbit. Thus the product map induces the smooth quotient representation
\[
\mathcal F/\mathrm{GL}(r)\longrightarrow\mathcal M_r,
\qquad [(L,R)]\longmapsto LR^\top.
\]
An objective depending only on \(LR^\top\) is gauge invariant on \(\mathcal F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-r matrix is represented by two full-column-rank factors modulo invertible changes of basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal F/\mathrm{GL}(r)\) represents \(\mathcal M_r\) through \([(L,R)]\mapsto LR^\top\).

notation.meaning: General linear group of degree r

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard gauge quotient for full-rank matrix factorizations

children.title: Fixed-Rank Matrix Completion
children.top_down_role: Completion problems posed over fixed-rank matrix manifolds.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Rank Matrix Completion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noiseless or least-squares completion with prescribed exact rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), let \(\Omega\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\times\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and let \(P_\Omega:\mathbb R^{m\times n}\to\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) retain entries indexed by \(\Omega\) and set all other entries to zero. For \(1\le r<\min(m,n)\), fixed-rank matrix completion is represented by
\[
\min_{X\in\mathcal M_r}f(X),
\qquad f(X)=\frac12\|P_\Omega(X-M)\|_F^2,
\]
where \(\mathcal M_r=\{X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}:\operatorname{rank}(X)=r\}\). Its Euclidean and embedded-metric Riemannian gradients are
\[
\nabla f(X)=P_\Omega(X-M),
\qquad
\operatorname{grad}f(X)=\operatorname{Proj}_{T_X\mathcal M_r}P_\Omega(X-M).
\]
A zero residual certifies agreement with the observations but does not, without additional assumptions on \(\Omega\) and the unknown matrix, certify uniqueness or recovery of unobserved entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-rank completion fits a specified data matrix on observed entries by least squares; zero residual guarantees consistency but not necessarily unique recovery.
assumptions_latex: \(P_\Omega\) retains entries in \(\Omega\) and sets all other entries to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fixed-rank completion minimizes \(f(X)=\frac12\|P_\Omega(X-M)\|_F^2\) over \(X\in\mathcal M_r\).

notation.meaning: Data matrix whose indexed entries are observed

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: canonical least-squares formulation of fixed-rank matrix completion

children.title: Fixed-Rank Matrix Approximation
children.top_down_role: Approximation problems constrained to fixed-rank matrix models.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has singular values \(\sigma_1\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_p\ge0\), where \(p=\min(m,n)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A truncated singular value decomposition \(A_r\) minimizes \(\|A-X\|_F\) over \(\operatorname{rank}X=r\), with error \(\bigl(\sum_{i>r}\sigma_i^2\bigr)^{1/2}\).

notation.meaning: Rank-r truncated singular value decomposition of A
Singular values of A in nonincreasing order

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem in the Frobenius norm
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Frobenius-norm Eckart-Young-Mirsky statement for exact rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A=U\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_p)V^\top\) be a singular value decomposition, and define
\[
A_r=U_{[:,1:r]}\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r)V_{[:,1:r]}^\top.
\]
Because \(\sigma_r>0\), the matrix \(A_r\) has rank exactly \(r\). The Eckart-Young-Mirsky theorem gives
\[
\min_{\operatorname{rank}(X)=r}\|A-X\|_F
=\|A-A_r\|_F
=\left(\sum_{i=r+1}^{p}\sigma_i^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
If \(\sigma_r>\sigma_{r+1}\), the minimizing matrix is unique; when these singular values coincide, multiple minimizing rank-
\(r\) matrices may exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Truncating the singular value decomposition gives a best rank-r Frobenius approximation; a strict singular-value gap makes the approximating matrix unique.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Rank Matrix Approximation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact-rank Eckart–Young–Mirsky statement, error formula, and uniqueness condition are correct under the stated hypotheses, but no theorem-level citation is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear observations with a differentiable data-fidelity loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A differentiable observation model interfaces with fixed-rank geometry through the composite objective
\[
f(X)=\ell(\mathcal A(X)-y),
\qquad X\in\mathcal M_r.
\]
Its ambient Euclidean gradient is obtained by the adjoint rule,
\[
\nabla f(X)=\mathcal A^*\nabla\ell(\mathcal A(X)-y),
\]
and, for the embedded Frobenius metric, its Riemannian gradient is
\[
\operatorname{grad}f(X)=
\operatorname{Proj}_{T_X\mathcal M_r}\mathcal A^*\nabla\ell(\mathcal A(X)-y).
\]
Thus entry sampling, matrix sensing, and other linear measurements differ only through implementations of \(\mathcal A\) and \(\mathcal A^*\), while the tangent projection supplies the fixed-rank constraint interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear observation operator enters a fixed-rank objective through its forward map and adjoint; tangent projection converts the ambient gradient into a manifold gradient.

children.top_down_role: Fixed-rank sequences approaching matrices of lower rank.

assumptions_latex: \(u_i\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(v_i\in\mathbb R^n\) are orthonormal families for \(1\le i\le r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sequence \(X_k=\sum_{i=1}^{r-1}u_iv_i^\top+k^{-1}u_rv_r^\top\) has rank \(r\) but converges to a rank-\(r-1\) matrix.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete rank loss caused by one vanishing singular value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
X_k=\sum_{i=1}^{r-1}u_iv_i^\top+\frac1k u_rv_r^\top.
\]
For every finite \(k\ge1\), the nonzero singular values of \(X_k\) are \(1,\ldots,1,k^{-1}\), so \(X_k\in\mathcal M_r\). Nevertheless,
\[
X_k\longrightarrow X_\star=\sum_{i=1}^{r-1}u_iv_i^\top,
\]
and \(\operatorname{rank}(X_\star)=r-1\). Thus a bounded sequence in the exact-rank manifold may approach a lower-rank boundary point outside that manifold. The failure mechanism is collapse of the smallest nonzero singular value to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact-rank sequence can lose rank in the limit when its smallest nonzero singular value tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Drop Sequences

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The explicit rank-drop sequence is correct, including the case r=1, and counterexample is the appropriate content kind; a specific source is still absent.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonclosed Fixed-Rank Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ambient Euclidean closure of the exact-rank manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(1\le r<\min(m,n)\), let
\[
\mathcal M_r=\{X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}:\operatorname{rank}(X)=r\}.
\]
The exact-rank set \(\mathcal M_r\) is not closed in the ambient Euclidean matrix space. Its closure is
\[
\overline{\mathcal M_r}=\mathcal M_{\le r}:=\{X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}:\operatorname{rank}(X)\le r\}.
\]
Thus the lower-rank strata form the closure boundary approached when one or more nonzero singular values tend to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrices of rank exactly r are not a closed set; their closure consists of all matrices of rank at most r, with lower-rank strata on the boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal M_r\) is not closed, and \(\overline{\mathcal M_r}=\{X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}:\operatorname{rank}(X)\le r\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Multilinear-Rank Manifolds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Embedded manifold of tensors with prescribed ranks of every mode unfolding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For dimensions \(n_1,\ldots,n_d\) and integers \(1\le r_k\le n_k\), define \[\mathcal M_{\mathbf r}=\{X\in\mathbb R^{n_1\times\cdots\times n_d}:\operatorname{rank}(X_{(k)})=r_k\text{ for }k=1,\ldots,d\}.\] Here \(X_{(k)}\) is the mode-\(k\) unfolding. Whenever \(\mathcal M_{\mathbf r}\) is nonempty, it is a smooth embedded submanifold of the ambient tensor space, of dimension \[\prod_{k=1}^d r_k+\sum_{k=1}^d(n_kr_k-r_k^2).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tensors whose mode unfoldings have prescribed ranks form a smooth embedded manifold, with dimension determined by the Tucker core and mode subspaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal M_{\mathbf r}\) is a smooth embedded manifold of dimension \(\prod_k r_k+\sum_k(n_kr_k-r_k^2)\).

notation.meaning: Mode-k matrix unfolding of the tensor X.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The prescribed multilinear-rank set and dimension formula match the topic, but the record combines a definition with a nontrivial embedded-manifold theorem. No cited source supports the smoothness, nonemptiness conditions, or dimension formula, so the mathematical package cannot yet be accepted.

knowledge_statements.title: Tucker Quotient Manifolds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quotient representation removing Tucker factor-basis nonuniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G\in\mathbb R^{r_1\times\cdots\times r_d}\) have full multilinear rank and let \(U_k\in\operatorname{St}(n_k,r_k)\). The Tucker reconstruction is \(X=G\times_1U_1\cdots\times_dU_d\). For \(Q_k\in O(r_k)\), the tuples \[(G,U_1,\ldots,U_d)\quad\text{and}\quad(G\times_1Q_1^{\mathsf T}\cdots\times_dQ_d^{\mathsf T},U_1Q_1,
\ldots,U_dQ_d)\] reconstruct the same tensor. Thus fixed-multilinear-rank tensors are represented by the quotient of full-rank Tucker tuples by the action of \(O(r_1)\times\cdots\times O(r_d)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Tucker tensor is represented by a core and orthonormal factors modulo simultaneous orthogonal basis changes in each latent mode.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equivalent Tucker tuples form orbits whose quotient represents fixed-multilinear-rank tensors.

notation.meaning: Stiefel manifold of n-by-r matrices with orthonormal columns.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the Tucker quotient container, and the displayed orthogonal gauge action is internally consistent. A specific source is still required to support the claim that the orbit quotient represents the entire fixed-multilinear-rank manifold and to establish the relevant quotient regularity.

knowledge_statements.title: Tensor-Train Manifolds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth manifold of tensors with a prescribed feasible tensor-train rank tuple.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_0=r_d=1\) and let \(r_1,\ldots,r_{d-1}\) be feasible positive integers. A tensor \(X\in\mathbb R^{n_1\times\cdots\times n_d}\) has tensor-train rank \(\mathbf r\) when \[\operatorname{rank}(X^{\langle k\rangle})=r_k\quad(k=1,\ldots,d-1),\] where \(X^{\langle k\rangle}\) matricizes the first \(k\) modes against the remaining modes. The set of tensors with rank exactly \(\mathbf r\) is a smooth embedded manifold of dimension \[\sum_{k=1}^d r_{k-1}n_kr_k-\sum_{k=1}^{d-1}r_k^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tensors with fixed ranks across all consecutive unfolding cuts form a smooth manifold parameterized by tensor-train cores modulo internal gauge transformations.
assumptions_latex: The rank tuple \(\mathbf r\) is feasible for \((n_1,\ldots,n_d)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact tensor-train-rank set is a smooth embedded manifold with the displayed dimension.

notation.meaning: Matricization separating modes 1 through k from modes k+1 through d.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The tensor-train rank definition and stated dimension are plausible and locally appropriate, but smooth embeddedness and the dimension formula are nontrivial claims with no citation. A source must also make the intended feasibility conditions precise.

knowledge_statements.title: Quotient Low-Rank Tensor Optimization Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Descent on factor parameters must respect quotient invariance and horizontal geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\pi:\overline{\mathcal M}\to\mathcal M=\overline{\mathcal M}/\mathcal G\) be a smooth quotient representation of low-rank tensors, and suppose \(\bar f=f\circ\pi\) is \(\mathcal G\)-invariant. For a \(\mathcal G\)-invariant Riemannian metric, \(\operatorname{grad}\bar f(\bar x)\) is horizontal and represents \(\operatorname{grad}f([\bar x])\). Hence an optimization update must use a horizontal tangent direction \(\xi\), a quotient-compatible retraction \(R\), and return the orbit \([R_{\bar x}(\xi)]\); changing the representative of \([\bar x]\) must not change the resulting quotient point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimization on low-rank tensor factors is well defined only when objectives, gradients, and updates are invariant under the factorization’s gauge action.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi:\overline{\mathcal M}\to\overline{\mathcal M}/\mathcal G\) is a smooth quotient map.
The metric and retraction are quotient compatible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Horizontal, equivariant updates induce a representative-independent optimization step on \(\mathcal M\).

notation.meaning: Gauge group acting on factor representations.
Projection from factor space to the quotient.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind is suitable for this optimization-interface leaf, but the gradient correspondence and representative-independent update require precise hypotheses on the group action, quotient metric, horizontal distribution, and equivariance of the retraction. No source is supplied from which those hypotheses can be verified.

knowledge_statements.title: Tensor-Rank Singularity Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank drops form boundary strata where fixed-rank manifold coordinates become singular.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M_{\mathbf r}\) be either an exact multilinear-rank or exact tensor-train-rank manifold. If \(X_j\in\mathcal M_{\mathbf r}\) converges to \(X\) and at least one defining unfolding satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}(X_{(k)})<r_k\), then \(X\notin\mathcal M_{\mathbf r}\) but lies in its closure. Along such a sequence, the corresponding smallest retained singular value tends to zero. Consequently, local fixed-rank factorizations lose full-rank regularity at \(X\), and manifold charts, tangent-space formulas, or retractions requiring that regularity do not extend there unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a defining tensor unfolding loses rank, the limit leaves the fixed-rank manifold and factor-based manifold coordinates become singular.
assumptions_latex: Some defining unfolding of \(X\) has rank below its prescribed value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\in\overline{\mathcal M_{\mathbf r}}\setminus\mathcal M_{\mathbf r}\), and fixed-rank manifold regularity fails at \(X\).

notation.meaning: A defining matrix unfolding of X.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the container, but the statement blends multilinear-rank and tensor-train models while using mode-unfolding notation that is not uniform across them. The claim about charts, tangent formulas, and retractions also needs model-specific qualification and authoritative support.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix Lie-Group Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Riemannian first-order iteration on an embedded matrix Lie group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a matrix Lie group \(G\subseteq\operatorname{GL}(n)\), a smooth objective \(f:G\to\mathbb R\), an initial point \(X_0\in G\), and step sizes \(\alpha_k>0\), compute a Lie-algebra direction \(\Omega_k\in\mathfrak g\) satisfying \(X_k\Omega_k=-\operatorname{grad}f(X_k)\). Update by \[X_{k+1}=X_k\exp(\alpha_k\Omega_k),\] or by a specified retraction replacing the exponential. Stop when \(\|\operatorname{grad}f(X_k)\|\le\varepsilon\), and output \(X_k\). Every exponential update remains in \(G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix Lie-group method converts the Riemannian gradient into a Lie-algebra direction and updates by group multiplication with an exponential or retraction.
assumptions_latex: A Riemannian metric and positive step-size rule are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration is feasible in \(G\) and terminates when the gradient norm is at most \(\varepsilon\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the identification of the Riemannian gradient with a left-translated Lie-algebra element depends on the chosen metric. The alternative retraction update is not explicitly defined, and the stated assumptions do not imply that the stopping test is reached in finitely many iterations. A source and corrected convergence or termination conditions are required.

knowledge_statements.title: Homogeneous-Space Quotients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneous manifold represented as a Lie-group quotient by an isotropy subgroup.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a Lie group \(G\) act smoothly and transitively on a manifold \(M\). Fix \(x_0\in M\) and define its stabilizer \(H=\{g\in G:g\cdot x_0=x_0\}\). If \(H\) is closed, then \(G/H\) is a smooth manifold and \[\Phi:G/H\to M,\qquad \Phi(gH)=g\cdot x_0,\] is a well-defined smooth equivariant diffeomorphism. Thus points of \(M\) are cosets, and tangent computations may be performed using representatives in \(G\) modulo vertical directions generated by \(H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transitive Lie-group action identifies the manifold with the quotient by the stabilizer of any chosen base point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G/H\) is a smooth manifold equivariantly diffeomorphic to \(M\).

notation.meaning: Stabilizer subgroup of the base point.
Space of left cosets of H in G.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quotient construction matches the homogeneous-space leaf, but the record states a nontrivial diffeomorphism theorem rather than only a definition. No authoritative locator is supplied for the closed-stabilizer quotient theorem or the tangent-representative interpretation.

children.title: Group Synchronization Problems
children.top_down_role: Estimation problems involving mutually consistent group-valued states.

knowledge_statements.title: Group Synchronization Problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of group elements from noisy pairwise relative measurements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal G=(V,E)\) be a measurement graph and let \(G\) be a Lie group. Given observations \(Y_{ij}\in G\) approximating unknown relative transforms \(g_i g_j^{-1}\), a group synchronization problem estimates \((g_i)_{i\in V}\in G^{|V|}\) by \[\min_{(g_i)}\sum_{(i,j)\in E}w_{ij}\,\ell\!\left(Y_{ij},g_i g_j^{-1}\right).\] If the loss depends only on relative transforms, then \((g_i)\) and \((g_i h)\) have the same objective value for every common \(h\in G\); the identifiable variable therefore lies in the quotient \(G^{|V|}/G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Group synchronization estimates globally consistent group elements from noisy pairwise ratios, with an unavoidable common right-action ambiguity.
assumptions_latex: \(w_{ij}\ge0\) and \(\ell\) is invariant under the common gauge action.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimization variable is identifiable only as an orbit in \(G^{|V|}/G\).

notation.meaning: Unknown absolute group element at vertex i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind and quotient interpretation fit group synchronization. However, the condition on the loss should be stated precisely enough to guarantee invariance under the diagonal right action, and no source supports the formulation or identifiability claim.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Least-squares formulation of rotation synchronization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the special orthogonal group and gives one optimization formulation for estimating rotations from noisy pairwise relative measurements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathrm{SO}(d)=\{R\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}:R^\top R=I_d,\ \det(R)=1\}\). Given measurements \(H_{ij}\in\mathrm{SO}(d)\) that are noisy versions of \(R_iR_j^{-1}\) for pairs \((i,j)\) corresponding to edges of a graph \(G\), one possible rotation-synchronization formulation is
\[
\min_{\widehat R_1,\ldots,\widehat R_n\in\mathrm{SO}(d)}\sum_{(i,j)\in G}\left\|\widehat R_i-H_{ij}\widehat R_j\right\|^2.
\]
The determinant condition excludes reflections, and the feasible set \(\mathrm{SO}(d)^n\) is a manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The special orthogonal group contains orthogonal matrices with determinant +1, excluding reflections. Given noisy pairwise relative-rotation measurements on a graph, rotation synchronization can be formulated as least-squares estimation of individual rotations over the product manifold SO(d)^n.
assumptions_latex: H_{ij}\in\mathrm{SO}(d)\text{ is a noisy version of }R_iR_j^{-1}\text{ for each observed edge }(i,j)\in G
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{\widehat R_1,\ldots,\widehat R_n\in\mathrm{SO}(d)}\sum_{(i,j)\in G}\left\|\widehat R_i-H_{ij}\widehat R_j\right\|^2\quad\text{is one formulation of rotation synchronization on }\mathrm{SO}(d)^n.

children.title: Geometric Registration Problems
children.top_down_role: Alignment problems posed over transformation groups or homogeneous spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Registration Problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alignment of corresponding geometric data by transformations from a Lie group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_1,\ldots,p_N\) and \(q_1,\ldots,q_N\) be corresponding points in a metric space on which a Lie group \(G\) acts. Weighted geometric registration seeks \[g^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{g\in G}\sum_{i=1}^N w_i\,d(g\cdot p_i,q_i)^2,\qquad w_i\ge0.\] For rigid registration in \(\mathbb R^m\), take \(G=\operatorname{SE}(m)\) and \(g\cdot p=Rp+t\), where \(R\in\operatorname{SO}(m)\) and \(t\in\mathbb R^m\). A minimizer is identifiable only modulo transformations stabilizing all observed data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometric registration chooses a group transformation that minimizes weighted discrepancies between corresponding data, possibly only up to data symmetries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g^\star\) minimizes the displayed alignment loss, modulo the common stabilizer of the data.

notation.meaning: Discrepancy metric on the data space.
Special Euclidean group of rigid motions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The optimization formulation is appropriate for geometric registration, but writing an element of the argmin presupposes existence, which is not guaranteed by the listed assumptions. The assertion that minimizers are identifiable only modulo a data stabilizer also requires a precise action and symmetry hypothesis. These points need authoritative support and corrected assumptions.

children.title: Gauge-Ambiguity Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Shared symmetry ambiguities arising in synchronization or registration models.

knowledge_statements.title: Gauge-Ambiguity Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quotient interface for optimization variables identifiable only up to a group action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a gauge group \(H\) act smoothly, freely, and properly on a parameter manifold \(P\), and suppose the modeled object and objective are invariant: \(F(p\cdot h)=F(p)\) and \(f(p\cdot h)=f(p)\) for all \(h\in H\). Then the identifiable variable is the orbit \([p]=\{p\cdot h:h\in H\}\in P/H\), and there exists \(\tilde f:P/H\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(f=\tilde f\circ\pi\). An optimization interface is gauge consistent precisely when its output and stopping criterion depend only on \([p]\), not on the chosen representative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When parameters differing by a gauge transformation encode the same object, optimization must operate on their orbit or use representative-independent rules.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) acts smoothly, freely, and properly on \(P\).
The model map \(F\) and objective \(f\) are \(H\)-invariant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The objective descends to \(P/H\), and gauge-consistent outputs depend only on \([p]\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the gauge-interface container, and objective descent to the quotient is plausible under the stated invariance. The precise 'if and only if' characterization of a gauge-consistent optimization interface is not formally defined or sourced, so the full statement cannot be verified.

children.title: Hyperboloid Representations
children.top_down_role: Hyperbolic geometry represented through an ambient indefinite-metric model.

knowledge_statements.title: Hyperboloid Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lorentzian hyperboloid model of constant negative-curvature geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(c>0\) and equip \(\mathbb R^{n+1}\) with the Lorentz bilinear form \(\langle x,y\rangle_L=-x_0y_0+\sum_{i=1}^n x_i y_i\). The curvature-\(-c\) hyperboloid model is \[\mathbb H_c^n=\{x\in\mathbb R^{n+1}:\langle x,x\rangle_L=-1/c,\ x_0>0\}.\] Its tangent space is \(T_x\mathbb H_c^n=\{v:\langle x,v\rangle_L=0\}\), with Riemannian metric given by the restriction of \(\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_L\). The geodesic distance satisfies \[d_c(x,y)=c^{-1/2}\operatorname{arcosh}(-c\langle x,y\rangle_L).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hyperbolic space is the upper sheet of a Lorentzian hyperboloid, with tangent metric inherited from the Lorentz form and distance given by arcosh.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb H_c^n\) with the restricted Lorentz metric has the displayed hyperbolic distance.

notation.meaning: Hyperboloid model with sectional curvature minus c.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind, Lorentzian model, tangent space, restricted metric, and distance formula are internally consistent with curvature parameter minus c. The record nevertheless has no citation; an authoritative section or page must support the normalization and distance formula.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Riemannian Hessian in the hyperboloid model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expresses the intrinsic Hessian through the Euclidean gradient and Hessian of a smooth ambient extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \bar f:\mathbb R^{n+1}\to\mathbb R be smooth, let f=\bar f|_{\mathcal M}, and let J=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,\ldots,1). For every x\in\mathcal M and u\in T_x\mathcal M, \operatorname{Hess}f(x)[u]=\operatorname{Proj}_x\!\left(J\operatorname{Hess}\bar f(x)[u]\right)+\langle x,J\operatorname{grad}\bar f(x)\rangle_Mu, where the ambient gradient and Hessian are Euclidean.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The hyperboloid's Riemannian Hessian is the tangent projection of J applied to the ambient Euclidean Hessian action, plus a curvature correction proportional to the tangent direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Hess}f(x)[u]=\operatorname{Proj}_x\left(J\operatorname{Hess}\bar f(x)[u]\right)+\langle x,J\operatorname{grad}\bar f(x)\rangle_Mu.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hyperboloid model of hyperbolic space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the upper sheet of the unit Minkowski hyperboloid and records its induced metric, tangent and normal spaces, projection, and curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let J=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,\ldots,1), \langle u,v\rangle_M=u^\top Jv, and \mathcal M=\{x\in\mathbb R^{n+1}:\langle x,x\rangle_M=-1,\ x_0>0\}. Then \mathcal M is an n-dimensional embedded submanifold, T_x\mathcal M=\{u\in\mathbb R^{n+1}:\langle x,u\rangle_M=0\}, and the restriction of \langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_M to T_x\mathcal M is positive definite. Its Minkowski-orthogonal normal space is N_x\mathcal M=\operatorname{span}(x), and the Minkowski-orthogonal projection onto T_x\mathcal M is \operatorname{Proj}_x(z)=z+\langle x,z\rangle_Mx. For n\geq2, the induced Riemannian metric has constant sectional curvature -1.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The upper sheet of the unit Minkowski hyperboloid is an embedded n-manifold. Minkowski orthogonality describes its tangent and normal spaces, the restricted Minkowski form is a Riemannian metric, and tangent projection has an explicit formula. For dimensions at least two, its sectional curvature is constantly minus one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \dim\mathcal M=n,\quad T_x\mathcal M=\{u:\langle x,u\rangle_M=0\},\quad N_x\mathcal M=\operatorname{span}(x),\quad \operatorname{Proj}_x(z)=z+\langle x,z\rangle_Mx,\quad K\equiv-1\text{ if }n\geq2.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Connection, covariant derivative, and exponential map on the hyperboloid
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives explicit ambient-projection formulas for the hyperboloid's Levi-Civita connection, covariant derivative, and exponential map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On the hyperboloid \mathcal M with its induced Minkowski metric, let V be a smooth vector field, (x,u)\in T\mathcal M, and let \bar V be any smooth ambient extension of V. Then \nabla_uV=\operatorname{Proj}_x(D\bar V(x)[u]) is the Riemannian connection. For a smooth tangent vector field Z along a smooth curve c:I\to\mathcal M, \frac{D}{dt}Z(t)=\operatorname{Proj}_{c(t)}\!\left(\frac{d}{dt}Z(t)\right). Moreover, \operatorname{Exp}_x(v)=\cosh(\|v\|_M)x+\frac{\sinh(\|v\|_M)}{\|v\|_M}v, with the quotient interpreted continuously as 1 at v=0. Thus c(t)=\operatorname{Exp}_x(tu) is the unique geodesic satisfying c(0)=x and c'(0)=u. The exponential map is defined on the whole tangent bundle and is a second-order retraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the hyperboloid, projecting ordinary ambient derivatives gives the Levi-Civita connection and covariant derivative. The exponential map has a closed hyperbolic-function formula, produces the unique geodesic for every initial tangent vector, and is globally defined.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal M=\{x:\langle x,x\rangle_M=-1,\ x_0>0\}\text{ with its induced Riemannian metric}
\bar V\text{ is any smooth ambient extension of }V
c:I\to\mathcal M\text{ and the tangent field }Z\text{ along }c\text{ are smooth}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla_uV=\operatorname{Proj}_x(D\bar V(x)[u]),\quad \frac{D}{dt}Z(t)=\operatorname{Proj}_{c(t)}\left(\frac{dZ}{dt}(t)\right),\quad \operatorname{Exp}_x(v)=\cosh(\|v\|_M)x+\frac{\sinh(\|v\|_M)}{\|v\|_M}v.

knowledge_statements.title: Poincaré Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unit-ball representation of hyperbolic space with curvature \(-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(n\ge 1\), the Poincaré ball representation of \(n\)-dimensional hyperbolic space is \(\mathbb B^n=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\|x\|_2<1\}\), equipped with the Riemannian metric
\[
g_x(u,v)=\frac{4\langle u,v\rangle}{(1-\|x\|_2^2)^2},\qquad x\in\mathbb B^n,\quad u,v\in T_x\mathbb B^n\simeq\mathbb R^n.
\]
Its geodesic distance from the origin satisfies \(d_{\mathbb B}(0,x)=2\operatorname{artanh}\|x\|_2\), and the resulting complete manifold has constant sectional curvature \(-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hyperbolic space is represented by the Euclidean unit ball with a conformally scaled metric whose distance diverges at the sphere boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\mathbb B^n,g)\) is a complete Riemannian model of hyperbolic space with constant sectional curvature \(-1\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geodesic Descent Algorithm on the Poincaré Half-Plane
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative descent using exponential-map curves, including explicit candidate directions and geodesics in half-plane coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let H=\{(x,y):y>0\} and f\in C^2(H,\mathbb R). Starting from M_1\in H, at iteration i choose X_i\in T_{M_i}H with df(M_i)[X_i]<0, then choose t_i\ge 0 such that f(\exp_{M_i}(t_iX_i))<f(M_i), and set M_{i+1}=\exp_{M_i}(t_iX_i). Stop when M_{i+1} or f(M_{i+1}) satisfies the prescribed convergence criterion; otherwise repeat. The choice X_i=-\operatorname{grad}_H f(M_i) gives the gradient method. At M=(x,y), suggested candidate directions and their exponential-map curves are (0,y) with (x,ye^t), (0,-y) with (x,ye^{-t}), (y,0) with (x+y\tanh t,y/\cosh t), and (-y,0) with (x-y\tanh t,y/\cosh t), for t\ge0; any selected direction must satisfy the descent condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a point in the Poincaré half-plane, choose a tangent direction with negative directional derivative, move along its exponential-map curve to a point with smaller objective value, and repeat until a convergence criterion holds. Negative Riemannian gradient directions yield the gradient method. Four coordinate directions are supplied with explicit geodesic curves as candidates, subject to the descent test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_{i+1}=\exp_{M_i}(t_iX_i)\quad\text{and}\quad f(M_{i+1})<f(M_i),\ \text{unless the prescribed stopping criterion terminates the iteration.}

knowledge_statements.title: Hyperbolic Representation Transitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit isometry between curvature-\(-1\) hyperboloid and Poincaré-ball coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathbb H^n=\{y=(y_0,y')\in\mathbb R^{n+1}:-y_0^2+\|y'\|_2^2=-1,\ y_0>0\}\) carry the metric induced by the Lorentz form. The maps
\[
\Phi(y)=\frac{y'}{y_0+1},\qquad
\Phi^{-1}(x)=\left(\frac{1+\|x\|_2^2}{1-\|x\|_2^2},\frac{2x}{1-\|x\|_2^2}\right)
\]
are mutually inverse smooth isometries between \(\mathbb H^n\) and the curvature-\(-1\) Poincaré ball. Consequently, objectives and tangent vectors may be transported by composition with \(\Phi^{-1}\) and by its differential, respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stereographic projection gives mutually inverse isometries between the upper hyperboloid and Poincaré ball models.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi:\mathbb H^n\to\mathbb B^n\) is a smooth Riemannian isometry with the displayed inverse.

notation.meaning: Hyperboloid coordinate split into time and spatial components

children.title: Poincaré Coordinate Boundary
children.top_down_role: Numerical or geometric effects near the boundary of bounded hyperbolic coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Poincaré Coordinate Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric and distance behavior as ball coordinates approach the unit sphere.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In the curvature-\(-1\) Poincaré ball, let \(x_k\in\mathbb B^n\) satisfy \(\|x_k\|_2\to1\). Then
\[
d_{\mathbb B}(0,x_k)=2\operatorname{artanh}\|x_k\|_2\to\infty,
\qquad
\frac{2}{1-\|x_k\|_2^2}\to\infty.
\]
Thus the Euclidean unit sphere is not part of the manifold; it is an ideal boundary at infinite intrinsic distance. Any computation permitting \(\|x\|_2=1\) makes the metric singular, while finite-precision iterates near the sphere encounter an unbounded conformal factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The unit sphere is an ideal boundary infinitely far away; the Poincaré metric becomes singular as coordinates approach it.
assumptions_latex: The Poincaré metric has curvature normalization \(-1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x_k\|_2\to1\) implies \(d_{\mathbb B}(0,x_k)\to\infty\) and divergence of the metric conformal factor.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct boundary consequence of the standard Poincaré metric

children.title: Noncompactness Effects
children.top_down_role: Escape, loss of compactness, unattained solutions, plus coercivity-sensitive regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Noncompactness Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and boundedness limitations caused by optimizing over noncompact manifolds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Continuity of an objective on a noncompact manifold does not ensure attainment of its infimum. Concretely, on the complete noncompact manifold \(M=\mathbb R\), the smooth function \(f(x)=e^{-x}\) satisfies
\[
\inf_{x\in M}f(x)=0,\qquad f(x)>0\quad\text{for every }x\in M.
\]
Hence \(f\) has no minimizer, and the minimizing sequence \(x_k=k\) escapes every compact subset. Compactness must therefore be replaced by an assumption such as compact sublevel sets, coercivity, or an independently established bounded-iterate property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a noncompact manifold, even a smooth objective may have an unattained infimum and minimizing sequences may escape to infinity.
assumptions_latex: \(M=\mathbb R\) with its Euclidean Riemannian metric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Smoothness and completeness without compactness do not imply existence of a global minimizer.

children.title: Coordinate-Boundary Effects
children.top_down_role: Chart-edge singularities, representation blow-up, plus boundary-sensitive computations.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate-Boundary Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization distortions induced by approaching the Poincaré chart boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a differentiable objective \(f:\mathbb B^n\to\mathbb R\) under the curvature-\(-1\) Poincaré metric, its Riemannian and Euclidean gradients obey
\[
\operatorname{grad} f(x)=\frac{(1-\|x\|_2^2)^2}{4}\nabla f(x).
\]
Therefore, if \(\nabla f(x_k)\) remains bounded while \(\|x_k\|_2\to1\), then \(\|\operatorname{grad}f(x_k)\|_2\to0\) in Euclidean coordinates. This coordinate shrinkage alone does not establish convergence to a point of the manifold, because the sequence can approach only the excluded ideal boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near the Poincaré boundary, coordinate components of the Riemannian gradient can vanish even while iterates escape intrinsically.
assumptions_latex: The Euclidean gradients \(\nabla f(x_k)\) are bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\|x_k\|_2\to1\), then the Euclidean coordinate norm of \(\operatorname{grad}f(x_k)\) tends to zero without implying an interior limit point.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: inverse-metric gradient formula in Poincaré coordinates

children.title: Noncompact Coordinate Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Regimes where unbounded geometry amplifies coordinate-boundary artifacts.

knowledge_statements.title: Noncompact Coordinate Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ill-conditioning of model-transition coordinates along intrinsically unbounded sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the inverse transition from the Poincaré ball to the hyperboloid,
\[
\Phi^{-1}(x)=\left(\frac{1+\|x\|_2^2}{1-\|x\|_2^2},\frac{2x}{1-\|x\|_2^2}\right),
\]
both \(\|\Phi^{-1}(x)\|_2\) and the operator norm \(\|D\Phi^{-1}(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\) are unbounded as \(\|x\|_2\to1\). Thus a sequence escaping to infinity in hyperbolic space is compressed into bounded ball coordinates approaching the unit sphere, and converting perturbations back to hyperboloid coordinates becomes arbitrarily ill-conditioned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ball coordinates compress escape to infinity toward the unit sphere, where the inverse model transition becomes arbitrarily ill-conditioned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x\|_2\to1\) implies \(\|\Phi^{-1}(x)\|_2\to\infty\) and \(\|D\Phi^{-1}(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\to\infty\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: boundary asymptotics of the explicit transition map

knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Riemannian Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact first-order stationarity for smooth unconstrained optimization on a Riemannian manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((M,g)\) be a finite-dimensional Riemannian manifold and let \(f:M\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable. A point \(x\in M\) is first-order Riemannian stationary precisely when
\[
\operatorname{grad}f(x)=0,
\]
where the gradient is characterized by \(g_x(\operatorname{grad}f(x),\eta)=df_x[\eta]\) for every \(\eta\in T_xM\). Every local minimizer of \(f\) is first-order stationary, provided it is an interior point of the manifold domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is first-order stationary when its Riemannian gradient vanishes; every unconstrained local minimizer satisfies this condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A local minimizer \(x\in M\) satisfies \(\operatorname{grad}f(x)=0\).

notation.meaning: Tangent space of M at x

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: defining property of the Riemannian gradient and Fermat condition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Riemannian gradient characterization of critical points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent first-order stationarity certificate for smooth real-valued functions on Riemannian manifolds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathcal M\to\mathbb R\) be smooth on a Riemannian manifold \(\mathcal M\). For every \(x\in\mathcal M\), \(x\) is a critical point of \(f\) if and only if \(\operatorname{grad}f(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point of a Riemannian manifold is critical for a smooth function exactly when the Riemannian gradient vanishes there.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\text{ is critical for }f\iff\operatorname{grad}f(x)=0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Riemannian Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact second-order stationarity for twice-differentiable unconstrained manifold optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((M,g)\) be a finite-dimensional Riemannian manifold and \(f:M\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable. A point \(x\in M\) is second-order Riemannian stationary when
\[
\operatorname{grad}f(x)=0,\qquad
g_x(\eta,\operatorname{Hess}f(x)[\eta])\ge0
\quad\text{for every }\eta\in T_xM.
\]
Every local minimizer satisfies these conditions. Equivalently, the self-adjoint Riemannian Hessian at \(x\) is positive semidefinite on \(T_xM\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Second-order stationarity requires a zero Riemannian gradient and a positive-semidefinite Riemannian Hessian on the tangent space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every local minimizer \(x\) satisfies \(\operatorname{grad}f(x)=0\) and \(\operatorname{Hess}f(x)\succeq0\) on \(T_xM\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard Riemannian second-order necessary condition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gradient–Hessian Characterization of Strict Second-Order Riemannian Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic characterization of strict curve-based second-order criticality on a Riemannian manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal M,g)\) be a Riemannian manifold and let \(f:\mathcal M\to\mathbb R\) be smooth. Then \(x\in\mathcal M\) is strictly second-order critical if and only if \(\operatorname{grad}f(x)=0\) and \(\operatorname{Hess}f(x)\succ 0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is strictly second-order critical exactly when its Riemannian gradient vanishes and its Riemannian Hessian is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\text{ is strictly second-order critical}\iff\left(\operatorname{grad}f(x)=0\ \text{and}\ \operatorname{Hess}f(x)\succ0\right)
