directory_assessment.rationale: The supplied deterministic Riemannian-method hierarchy contains conjugate-gradient, quasi-Newton, Newton, and trust-region families but no precise primary home for basic Riemannian steepest descent. A dedicated sibling-level first-order descent topic is suggested, subject to independent structural review; the listed conjugate-gradient node is only a provisional parent candidate because the common deterministic-method parent is absent from the packet.

assumptions_latex: \(g_k=\operatorname{grad}f(x_k)\), and a vector transport \(\mathcal T_k:T_{x_{k-1}}\mathcal M\to T_{x_k}\mathcal M\) is fixed.
Transported differences are \(y_k=g_k-\mathcal T_k g_{k-1}\), with denominators below assumed nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The FR, PRP, HS, and DY coefficient families are given by the displayed transported inner-product ratios.

notation.meaning: previous search direction transported to the current tangent space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Riemannian analogues of classical nonlinear conjugate-gradient coefficients under a fixed transport convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Using the metric at \(x_k\), classical transported coefficients are
\[\beta_k^{\mathrm{FR}}=\frac{\langle g_k,g_k\rangle}{\langle g_{k-1},g_{k-1}\rangle},\qquad
\beta_k^{\mathrm{PRP}}=\frac{\langle g_k,y_k\rangle}{\langle g_{k-1},g_{k-1}\rangle},\]
\[\beta_k^{\mathrm{HS}}=\frac{\langle g_k,y_k\rangle}{\langle\mathcal T_k\eta_{k-1},y_k\rangle},\qquad
\beta_k^{\mathrm{DY}}=\frac{\langle g_k,g_k\rangle}{\langle\mathcal T_k\eta_{k-1},y_k\rangle}.\]
They enter the common update
\[\eta_k=-g_k+\beta_k\mathcal T_k\eta_{k-1}.\]
Safeguarded variants may truncate or restart these coefficients when descent or denominator conditions fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fletcher-Reeves, Polak-Ribiere-Polyak, Hestenes-Stiefel, and Dai-Yuan coefficients extend to manifolds by transporting prior tangent vectors before forming inner products.
knowledge_statements.title: Classical Conjugacy-Coefficient Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the coefficient-family container, but the formulas depend on transport and scaling conventions and have no source. The phrase “using the metric at x_k” is inaccurate for denominators involving vectors at x_{k-1}; each inner product's base point must be explicit.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathcal M\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable, \(R\) is a retraction, and \(\mathcal T\) is a vector transport associated with \(R\).
A coefficient rule \(\beta_{k+1}\) and a line-search acceptance rule are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration produces tangent search directions and manifold iterates through retraction and vector transport.

notation.meaning: retraction used to update the iterate
vector transport between successive tangent spaces

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic retraction and vector-transport formulation of Riemannian nonlinear conjugate gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_0\in\mathcal M\), set \(g_0=\operatorname{grad}f(x_0)\) and \(\eta_0=-g_0\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), choose \(\alpha_k>0\) by the prescribed line search and compute
\[x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(\alpha_k\eta_k),\qquad g_{k+1}=\operatorname{grad}f(x_{k+1}).\]
Transport the previous direction and form
\[\eta_{k+1}=-g_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}\mathcal T_{\alpha_k\eta_k}(\eta_k).\]
If the new direction violates the chosen descent safeguard, replace it by \(-g_{k+1}\). Stop when \(\|g_k\|\le\varepsilon\), and return \(x_k\); otherwise continue until the iteration budget is exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Riemannian conjugate gradient retracts along a tangent direction, transports the old direction to the new tangent space, and combines it with the new negative gradient.
knowledge_statements.title: Vector-Transport Conjugate-Gradient Framework

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the framework container, but the vector transport, coefficient rule, line search, and descent safeguard are left variant-dependent and unsupported by a citation.

assumptions_latex: \(R\) is a retraction, and for consecutive iterates \(x_k,x_{k+1}\), the local inverse \(R_{x_{k+1}}^{-1}(x_k)\) is well defined.
A coefficient rule \(\beta_{k+1}\) and line search are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inverse-retraction displacement supplies a previous-step direction intrinsic to the current tangent space.

notation.meaning: local inverse of the retraction based at x
backward displacement in the current tangent space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transport-free conjugate-gradient template using a local inverse retraction to represent the preceding step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(x_0\in\mathcal M\) and \(\eta_0=-\operatorname{grad}f(x_0)\). After choosing \(\alpha_k>0\), set
\[x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(\alpha_k\eta_k),\qquad s_{k+1}=-R_{x_{k+1}}^{-1}(x_k)\in T_{x_{k+1}}\mathcal M.\]
The vector \(s_{k+1}\) points from \(x_{k+1}\) in the forward orientation of the preceding step without applying a separate vector transport. Define
\[\eta_{k+1}=-\operatorname{grad}f(x_{k+1})+\beta_{k+1}s_{k+1},\]
with any required normalization absorbed into \(\beta_{k+1}\). Restart with the negative gradient if the inverse is unavailable or the direction fails a descent test. Stop at the prescribed gradient tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inverse-retraction method represents the preceding step directly in the new tangent space, then combines that displacement with the new negative gradient.
knowledge_statements.title: Inverse-Retraction Conjugate-Gradient Framework

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the inverse-retraction framework, but the precise recurrence, sign, normalization, and interpretation of the inverse-retraction displacement vary by method and require an inspectable source.

children.title: Scaled Vector Transport
children.top_down_role: Transport scaling used to control norm distortion or preserve descent behavior.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal T_\eta(\xi)\) is a vector transport of \(\xi\in T_x\mathcal M\) to \(T_{R_x(\eta)}\mathcal M\).
Norms are induced by the Riemannian metrics at the corresponding base points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scaled transport never increases the norm of the transported vector relative to its original norm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-capped scaling commonly used to control transported conjugate-gradient directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the scaled vector transport by
\[\mathcal T_\eta^{(0)}(\xi):=
\begin{cases}
\mathcal T_\eta(\xi),&\|\mathcal T_\eta(\xi)\|\le\|\xi\|,\\
\dfrac{\|\xi\|}{\|\mathcal T_\eta(\xi)\|}\mathcal T_\eta(\xi),&\|\mathcal T_\eta(\xi)\|>\|\xi\|.
\end{cases}\]
Equivalently, when \(\mathcal T_\eta(\xi)\ne0\), it is \(\mathcal T_\eta(\xi)\) multiplied by
\[\min\left\{1,\frac{\|\xi\|}{\|\mathcal T_\eta(\xi)\|}\right\}.\]
Therefore \(\|\mathcal T_\eta^{(0)}(\xi)\|\le\|\xi\|\), while its direction agrees with that of the unscaled transported vector whenever the latter is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaled vector transport preserves the transported direction but caps its norm at the norm of the original tangent vector.
knowledge_statements.title: Scaled Vector Transport

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A definition is appropriate for this leaf, but scaled-transport conventions vary and no source is cited. The concluding norm and direction verification is proof-style material rather than part of the definition.

children.title: Conjugate-Gradient Preconditioning
children.top_down_role: Geometry-aware preconditioning for search-direction quality plus conditioning control.

assumptions_latex: For each \(x\in\mathcal M\), \(P_x:T_x\mathcal M\to T_x\mathcal M\) is self-adjoint and positive definite.
A vector transport \(\mathcal T_k\) and conjugacy coefficient \(\beta_k\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing the raw gradient by \(P_x^{-1}\operatorname{grad}f(x)\) yields a preconditioned Riemannian conjugate-gradient direction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variable tangent-space preconditioning within a vector-transport conjugate-gradient iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), compute
\[g_k=\operatorname{grad}f(x_k),\qquad P_{x_k}z_k=g_k.\]
Initialize \(\eta_0=-z_0\). After retracting to \(x_k\), update
\[\eta_k=-z_k+\beta_k\mathcal T_k(\eta_{k-1}),\]
where \(\beta_k\) is formed consistently with the selected preconditioned conjugate-gradient variant. Require the resulting direction to satisfy a descent safeguard such as
\[\langle g_k,\eta_k\rangle<0;\]
otherwise set \(\eta_k=-z_k\). Choose the step by line search, stop when \(\|g_k\|\le\varepsilon\), and return \(x_k\). Positive definiteness ensures \(-z_k\) is descending whenever \(g_k\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-definite tangent-space preconditioner replaces the gradient by an approximate inverse-Hessian action before the transported conjugate direction is formed.
knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate-Gradient Preconditioning

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the preconditioning leaf, but the coefficient must be specified consistently with a particular preconditioned metric or inner-product convention and supported by a source. The final descent justification is proof text.

children.title: Conjugate-Gradient Restart
children.top_down_role: Periodic or diagnostic restart families for restoring effective descent.

assumptions_latex: A Riemannian conjugate-gradient method has computed \(g_k=\operatorname{grad}f(x_k)\) and a provisional direction \(\widehat\eta_k\).
A restart predicate based on descent, periodicity, or gradient orthogonality is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When the predicate fires, setting \(\eta_k=-g_k\) restores a strict descent direction unless \(g_k=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguarded restart that discards unreliable conjugate history and recovers negative-gradient descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Form a provisional direction
\[\widehat\eta_k=-g_k+\beta_k\mathcal T_k(\eta_{k-1}).\]
Given constants \(\sigma\in(0,1]\), \(\tau\in[0,1)\), or a restart period \(m\), trigger restart if any selected test holds, for example
\[\langle g_k,\widehat\eta_k\rangle>-\sigma\|g_k\|^2,\qquad
\frac{|\langle g_k,\mathcal T_k g_{k-1}\rangle|}{\|g_k\|^2}>\tau,\qquad
k\equiv0\pmod m.\]
Set \(\eta_k=-g_k\) when restarting and \(\eta_k=\widehat\eta_k\) otherwise. Then perform the line search and retraction step. If \(g_k\ne0\), a restarted direction satisfies \(\langle g_k,\eta_k\rangle=-\|g_k\|^2<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restart discards the transported conjugate term when descent or orthogonality tests fail, recovering the negative Riemannian gradient as a reliable direction.
knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate-Gradient Restart

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the restart leaf, but the displayed restart tests and thresholds are variant-dependent and uncited. The restart period m needs an explicit positive-integer domain, and the orthogonality ratio is undefined when g_k=0 unless termination is tested first.

children.title: Variant Interaction Regimes
children.top_down_role: Compatibility plus tradeoffs among transport scaling, preconditioning, plus restart choices.

knowledge_statements.title: Variant Interaction Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Descent condition coupling transport, preconditioning, conjugacy coefficient, and restart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the preconditioned gradient be \(z_{k+1}=P_{k+1}g_{k+1}\), where \(g_{k+1}=\operatorname{grad}f(x_{k+1})\), and form \(\eta_{k+1}=-z_{k+1}+\beta_{k+1}\mathcal T_k\eta_k\). The new direction is descending precisely when
\[
\langle g_{k+1},\eta_{k+1}\rangle=-\langle g_{k+1},z_{k+1}\rangle+\beta_{k+1}\langle g_{k+1},\mathcal T_k\eta_k\rangle<0.
\]
Thus transport scaling and the coefficient must jointly satisfy \(\beta_{k+1}\langle g_{k+1},\mathcal T_k\eta_k\rangle<\langle g_{k+1},z_{k+1}\rangle\). If \(P_{k+1}\) is positive definite, restarting with \(\beta_{k+1}=0\) restores strict descent whenever \(g_{k+1}\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transport, preconditioning, and the conjugacy coefficient must jointly preserve a negative gradient-direction inner product; restarting to the preconditioned steepest-descent direction restores descent.
assumptions_latex: \(P_{k+1}:T_{x_{k+1}}\mathcal M\to T_{x_{k+1}}\mathcal M\) is self-adjoint positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\langle g_{k+1},\eta_{k+1}\rangle<0\) under the displayed interaction inequality.

notation.meaning: Riemannian preconditioner at the new iterate
vector transport from the old tangent space to the new one

review_flags: Exact Riemannian interaction statement requires a manifold conjugate-gradient source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the Variant Interaction Regimes leaf and the descent calculation is internally consistent, including the nonzero-gradient qualification for restart. No source is cited for the Riemannian transport, preconditioning, and restart interaction, so the record cannot pass evidence review.

knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate-Gradient Global-Convergence Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zoutendijk-type global convergence for retraction-based Riemannian conjugate gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(\alpha_k\eta_k)\), where every \(\eta_k\) is a descent direction and \(\alpha_k\) satisfies Riemannian strong Wolfe conditions. Suppose the initial level set is compact, the pullback gradients are uniformly Lipschitz along accepted retraction curves, and there is \(c>0\) such that
\[
-\langle g_k,\eta_k\rangle\ge c\lVert g_k\rVert\lVert\eta_k\rVert
\]
for all \(k\). Then the Riemannian Zoutendijk series is finite, and consequently
\[
\liminf_{k\to\infty}\lVert\operatorname{grad}f(x_k)\rVert=0.
\]
Any conjugacy-coefficient, transport, scaling, and restart family maintaining these hypotheses belongs to this global-convergence regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong Wolfe steps and uniformly gradient-related descent directions yield a finite Zoutendijk series and subsequential convergence of gradient norms to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathcal M\to\mathbb R\) is continuously differentiable and bounded below on the initial level set.
The accepted retraction pullbacks have uniformly Lipschitz gradients.
The displayed uniform angle condition and strong Wolfe conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}\lVert\operatorname{grad}f(x_k)\rVert=0\).

notation.meaning: Riemannian gradient at the kth iterate

review_flags: A precise authoritative source for the Riemannian Zoutendijk formulation is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem role fits the global-convergence-family container, but the precise Riemannian Zoutendijk hypotheses depend on the retraction, pullback regularity, and line-search formulation. An authoritative source is required before the stated theorem can be judged reliable.

knowledge_statements.title: Loss-of-Conjugacy Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual criterion marking failure of transported Hessian conjugacy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For consecutive directions compared in \(T_{x_{k+1}}\mathcal M\), define the conjugacy residual
\[
r_{k+1}=\bigl\langle \eta_{k+1},\operatorname{Hess}f(x_{k+1})[\mathcal T_k\eta_k]\bigr\rangle.
\]
Exact local Hessian conjugacy holds only when \(r_{k+1}=0\). If the transported direction is rescaled, the Hessian changes along the step, or \(\beta_{k+1}\) is computed using a transport inconsistent with \(\mathcal T_k\), then the algebraic cancellation defining conjugacy generally fails and \(r_{k+1}\ne0\). In particular, on a nonquadratic objective even exact line search does not generally preserve successive Hessian conjugacy because \(\operatorname{Hess}f(x_{k+1})\) differs from the curvature model used to choose \(\beta_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conjugacy is lost when the transported old direction has nonzero Hessian inner product with the new direction, commonly because curvature or transport changes.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice differentiable near consecutive iterates.
Both directions are compared in \(T_{x_{k+1}}\mathcal M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{k+1}\ne0\) certifies loss of exact successive-direction conjugacy.

notation.meaning: chosen vector transport along the accepted step

review_flags: The nonlinear Riemannian loss mechanism needs a dedicated source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and residual criterion fit the leaf. The broader assertions about rescaling, inconsistent transports, changing Hessians, and exact line search on nonquadratic objectives are uncited and require a dedicated nonlinear Riemannian conjugate-gradient source.

knowledge_statements.title: Riemannian Secant Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Secant equation after placing displacement and gradient difference in one tangent space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(\alpha_k\eta_k)\), choose a vector transport \(\mathcal T_k:T_{x_k}\mathcal M\to T_{x_{k+1}}\mathcal M\) and define
\[
s_k=\mathcal T_k(\alpha_k\eta_k),\qquad y_k=\operatorname{grad}f(x_{k+1})-\mathcal T_k\operatorname{grad}f(x_k).
\]
A direct Hessian approximation \(B_{k+1}:T_{x_{k+1}}\mathcal M\to T_{x_{k+1}}\mathcal M\) satisfies the Riemannian secant equation when \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\). An inverse approximation \(H_{k+1}\) satisfies the dual equation \(H_{k+1}y_k=s_k\). The curvature scalar \(\langle s_k,y_k\rangle\) is well-defined because both vectors occupy the same tangent space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transport places the step and gradient change in the new tangent space, where direct and inverse secant equations can be imposed consistently.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal T_k\) maps the old tangent space into the new tangent space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\) and, dually, \(H_{k+1}y_k=s_k\).
review_flags: A source explicitly supporting this transport convention is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation correctly co-locates the step and gradient difference before stating direct and inverse secant equations, and it fits the Riemannian Secant Geometry container. The particular transported-gradient convention has no citation and must be supported by a Riemannian quasi-Newton source.

children.title: Riemannian BFGS Families
children.top_down_role: BFGS-type inverse-curvature approximations adapted to manifold transport geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Riemannian BFGS Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: BFGS direct-Hessian update within a common tangent space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B_k\) be transported into \(T_{x_{k+1}}\mathcal M\) as a self-adjoint operator \(\widetilde B_k\). For a curvature pair \((s_k,y_k)\) in that space with \(\langle s_k,y_k\rangle>0\), the Riemannian BFGS direct update is
\[
B_{k+1}=\widetilde B_k-
\frac{(\widetilde B_ks_k)\otimes(\widetilde B_ks_k)}{\langle s_k,\widetilde B_ks_k\rangle}+
\frac{y_k\otimes y_k}{\langle s_k,y_k\rangle}.
\]
Here \((u\otimes v)w=u\langle v,w\rangle\). The update is self-adjoint, satisfies \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\), and is positive definite whenever \(\widetilde B_k\) is positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transport the old operator to the new tangent space, then apply the BFGS rank-two formula using a positive-curvature secant pair.

notation.meaning: rank-one operator induced by the Riemannian metric
old direct approximation transported to the new tangent space

children.title: Riemannian DFP Families

knowledge_statements.title: Riemannian DFP Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: DFP inverse-Hessian update within a common tangent space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H_k\) be transported into \(T_{x_{k+1}}\mathcal M\) as a self-adjoint operator \(\widetilde H_k\). For \(s_k,y_k\) in that tangent space with \(\langle s_k,y_k\rangle>0\), the Riemannian DFP inverse update is
\[
H_{k+1}=\widetilde H_k-
\frac{(\widetilde H_ky_k)\otimes(\widetilde H_ky_k)}{\langle y_k,\widetilde H_ky_k\rangle}+
\frac{s_k\otimes s_k}{\langle s_k,y_k\rangle}.
\]
The resulting operator is self-adjoint, satisfies the inverse secant equation \(H_{k+1}y_k=s_k\), and remains positive definite when \(\widetilde H_k\) is positive definite.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On a finite-dimensional Riemannian tangent space, let \(B\) be positive definite and let \(H=B^{-1}\). Then the direct secant equation \(Bs=y\) is equivalent to the inverse secant equation \(Hy=s\). For \(\rho=1/\langle s,y\rangle\), inversion of the direct BFGS update gives the inverse-BFGS update
\[
H_+=\bigl(I-\rho s\otimes y\bigr)H\bigl(I-\rho y\otimes s\bigr)+\rho s\otimes s,
\]
where \((u\otimes v)w=u\langle v,w\rangle\). This inversion correspondence is distinct from the formal exchange of \(s\) and \(y\), which transforms the direct BFGS rank-two expression into the inverse DFP rank-two expression. Thus inversion provides direct–inverse secant duality, while variable exchange provides the BFGS–DFP algebraic correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct and inverse secant equations correspond through operator inversion. Inverting a direct BFGS update yields the inverse-BFGS formula, while exchanging displacement and gradient-difference variables gives the separate formal correspondence between BFGS and DFP expressions.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Definiteness Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature condition preserving positivity of rank-two quasi-Newton updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be self-adjoint positive definite on a finite-dimensional Riemannian tangent space, and let \(s,y\) satisfy \(\langle s,y\rangle>0\). Then the BFGS direct update constructed from \((A,s,y)\) is self-adjoint positive definite. Likewise, if \(H\) is self-adjoint positive definite, the DFP inverse update constructed from \((H,s,y)\) is self-adjoint positive definite. The strict curvature inequality is essential for these undamped formulas: if \(\langle s,y\rangle\le0\), their rank-one curvature term has a nonpositive or undefined denominator, so positive definiteness is not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive initial operators and a strictly positive secant curvature preserve positive definiteness; nonpositive curvature removes that guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(A\succ0\) or \(H\succ0\) on a finite-dimensional tangent space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal B(A;s,y)\succ0\) and \(\mathcal D(H;y,s)\succ0\).

notation.meaning: strict positive definiteness with respect to the Riemannian metric

knowledge_statements.title: Limited-Memory Quasi-Newton Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transported limited-memory inverse-BFGS two-loop recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), retain at most \(m\) curvature pairs and transport them into \(T_{x_k}\mathcal M\). For pairs \((s_i,y_i)\), set \(\rho_i=1/\langle y_i,s_i\rangle\) and initialize \(q=g_k\). In decreasing index order set \(a_i=\rho_i\langle s_i,q\rangle\) and \(q\leftarrow q-a_i y_i\). Choose a positive scalar \(\gamma_k\), set \(r=\gamma_k q\), and in increasing order set \(b_i=\rho_i\langle y_i,r\rangle\) and \(r\leftarrow r+s_i(a_i-b_i)\). Output \(\eta_k=-r\), unless a stopping test such as \(\lVert g_k\rVert\le\varepsilon\) is satisfied.

knowledge_statements.title: Transported Curvature-Pair Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive transport and formation of tangent-space curvature pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
After accepting \(x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(\alpha_k\eta_k)\), a curvature-pair mechanism chooses a transport \(\mathcal T_k\) and forms
\[
s_k=\mathcal T_k(\alpha_k\eta_k),\qquad y_k=g_{k+1}-\mathcal T_k g_k.
\]
For later use at \(x_j\), where \(j>k+1\), both components must undergo the same composed transports:
\[
s_k^{(j)}=\mathcal T_{j-1}\cdots\mathcal T_{k+1}s_k,\qquad y_k^{(j)}=\mathcal T_{j-1}\cdots\mathcal T_{k+1}y_k.
\]
Quasi-Newton updates at \(x_j\) use only the co-located pair \((s_k^{(j)},y_k^{(j)})\); damping or pair rejection may enforce positive curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A curvature pair is formed by consistently transporting the step and old gradient, then transporting both components identically to every later tangent space.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\mathcal T_i\) maps \(T_{x_i}\mathcal M\) into \(T_{x_{i+1}}\mathcal M\).
The same transport chain is used for both components of a stored pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_k^{(j)},y_k^{(j)}\in T_{x_j}\mathcal M\), so their secant products are well-defined.

notation.meaning: Riemannian gradient at the kth iterate

knowledge_statements.title: Quasi-Newton Superlinear-Convergence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local superlinear convergence under a Riemannian Dennis–Moré condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_*\) be a nondegenerate local minimizer of a twice continuously differentiable function, with positive-definite \(\operatorname{Hess}f(x_*)\). Suppose \(x_k\to x_*\), the retraction is second order, the transports used by the method approach parallel transport, and unit quasi-Newton steps are eventually accepted. Transporting all operators and steps to \(T_{x_*}\mathcal M\), assume the Dennis–Moré condition
\[
\frac{\lVert(B_k-\operatorname{Hess}f(x_*))s_k\rVert}{\lVert s_k\rVert}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Then the iterates converge superlinearly in Riemannian distance:
\[
\frac{d(x_{k+1},x_*)}{d(x_k,x_*)}\longrightarrow0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a nondegenerate minimizer, compatible geometry, eventual unit steps, and the Dennis–Moré approximation condition imply superlinear convergence.
assumptions_latex: The retraction and transport have the stated second-order compatibility.
The displayed Dennis–Moré condition holds and unit steps are eventually accepted.

knowledge_statements.title: Secant-Inconsistency Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric and curvature failures that make a secant update invalid or unstable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A secant equation is geometrically meaningful only when its displacement \(s_k\), gradient difference \(y_k\), and approximating operator share one tangent space. Without transport, the expression \(g_{k+1}-g_k\) is generally undefined because its terms lie in distinct tangent spaces. Even after co-location, an undamped positive-definite BFGS or DFP update requires \(\langle s_k,y_k\rangle>0\). If \(\langle s_k,y_k\rangle=0\), the rank-two formula is undefined; if \(\langle s_k,y_k\rangle<0\), no positive-definite operator can satisfy \(Bs_k=y_k\), since that would imply \(\langle s_k,Bs_k\rangle<0\). These cases form the secant-inconsistency boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Secant updates fail when vectors occupy different tangent spaces or when their curvature is nonpositive; zero curvature is singular and negative curvature contradicts positive definiteness.
assumptions_latex: The desired direct approximation is self-adjoint positive definite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid undamped positive-definite secant update requires co-location and \(\langle s_k,y_k\rangle>0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Riemannian Hessian and its calculus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic tensor definition, coordinate formula, elementary identities, and critical-point specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f\in C^\infty(M)\), the Riemannian Hessian is the \((0,2)\)-tensor \(\operatorname{Hess}f=
abla df\) defined by \(\operatorname{Hess}f(X,Y)=g(
abla_X\operatorname{grad}f,Y)=X(Yf)-(
abla_XY)f\). In coordinates, \((\operatorname{Hess}f)_{jk}=\partial_j\partial_kf-\Gamma^i_{jk}\partial_if\). It is linear and satisfies \(\operatorname{Hess}(f_1f_2)=f_1\operatorname{Hess}f_2+f_2\operatorname{Hess}f_1+df_1\otimes df_2+df_2\otimes df_1\), \(\operatorname{Hess}(\varphi\circ f)=(\varphi'\circ f)\operatorname{Hess}f+(\varphi''\circ f)df\otimes df\), and, where \(f_2
e0\), \(\operatorname{Hess}(f_1/f_2)=f_2^{-1}\operatorname{Hess}f_1-f_1f_2^{-2}\operatorname{Hess}f_2-f_2^{-2}(df_1\otimes df_2+df_2\otimes df_1)+2f_1f_2^{-3}df_2\otimes df_2\). At a critical point \(x_0\), its connection term vanishes, so \((\operatorname{Hess}f)_{jk}(x_0)=\partial_j\partial_kf(x_0)\); away from critical points its representation generally depends on the Riemannian metric and connection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Riemannian Hessian is the covariant derivative of the differential, with coordinate components equal to second partial derivatives minus the connection correction. It satisfies linear, product, quotient, and chain rules. At a critical point the connection correction vanishes.
assumptions_latex: (M,g)\text{ is a Riemannian manifold with Levi-Civita connection }\nabla
f_2\ne0\text{ wherever the quotient identity is applied}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Hess}f=\nabla df,\qquad (\operatorname{Hess}f)_{jk}=\partial_j\partial_kf-\Gamma^i_{jk}\partial_if

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear and Quadratic Radial Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local exponential-coordinate models of a twice continuously differentiable function, including the pole case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $(M,g)$ be a complete finite-dimensional Riemannian manifold, let $f\in C^2(M)$, and fix $y\in M$. On a neighborhood of $y$ where $\exp_y^{-1}$ is defined, the linear radial approximation is $L_y(x)=f(y)+df_y(\exp_y^{-1}x)$, and the quadratic radial approximation is $Q_y(x)=f(y)+df_y(\exp_y^{-1}x)+\tfrac12\operatorname{Hess}f_y(\exp_y^{-1}x,\exp_y^{-1}x)$. If $y$ is a pole, these radial approximations are defined on all of $M$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a C² function on a complete finite-dimensional Riemannian manifold, exponential coordinates at y define a linear radial model from the differential and a quadratic radial model obtained by adding one half of the Hessian quadratic form. If y is a pole, the models are defined globally.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Riemannian Gauss–Newton Iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unglobalized iteration for seeking a local least-squares solution associated with a Euclidean-valued residual map on a Riemannian manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M\) be a Riemannian manifold, let \(R\) be a retraction on \(\mathcal M\), let \(F:\mathcal M\to\mathcal E\) with \(\mathcal E\) Euclidean, and choose \(x_0\in\mathcal M\). For \(k=0,1,2,\ldots\), select \(\eta_k\in T_{x_k}\mathcal M\) satisfying \[\bigl(\mathrm DF(x_k)^*\circ\mathrm DF(x_k)\bigr)[\eta_k]=-\mathrm DF(x_k)^*[F(x_k)],\] and set \(x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(\eta_k)\). This generates the Riemannian Gauss--Newton sequence intended to find a local least-squares solution associated with \(F(x)=0\). The iteration is defined only when a solution of the displayed normal equation can be selected at each step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a point on the manifold, each iteration solves the Gauss–Newton normal equation in the current tangent space and retracts the selected tangent step back to the manifold. The method seeks a local least-squares solution for the Euclidean-valued residual map. Without a solvable normal equation at an iteration, the stated algorithm does not define the next iterate.

At each iteration, the displayed normal equation admits a selected solution \(\eta_k\in T_{x_k}\mathcal M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update \(x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(\eta_k)\) generates the Riemannian Gauss--Newton iterate sequence, intended to find a local least-squares solution associated with \(F(x)=0\).

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathcal M\to\mathbb R\) is twice continuously differentiable and \(R\) is a retraction.
The computed tangent step exists and satisfies the displayed residual bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each accepted tangent step approximates the Newton equation with relative residual at most \(\theta_k\).

notation.meaning: Riemannian Hessian at the current iterate
Residual of the approximate Newton equation
Riemannian gradient at the current iterate

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard relative-residual definition of an inexact Newton step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative-residual inexact Newton method on a finite-dimensional Riemannian manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x_0\in\mathcal M\), a stopping tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and forcing terms \(\theta_k\in[0,1)\), stop when \(\lVert g_k\rVert_{x_k}\le\varepsilon\). Otherwise compute \(\eta_k\in T_{x_k}\mathcal M\) such that \[\lVert H_k\eta_k+g_k\rVert_{x_k}\le\theta_k\lVert g_k\rVert_{x_k},\] and update \(x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(\eta_k)\), possibly after a separately specified globalization step. The exact Newton method is recovered when \(\theta_k=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute a tangent step whose Newton-equation residual is bounded by a prescribed fraction of the current gradient norm, then retract it.
knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Riemannian Newton Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The relative-residual algorithm fits the inexact-method leaf and is internally coherent, but it has no source locator supporting this particular Riemannian formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Approximate Riemannian Newton Equation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines simultaneous Jacobian-approximation and linear-solve errors for Newton iteration on a manifold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M\) have a retraction \(R\) and affine connection \(\nabla\), and let \(\xi\) be a vector field. At \(x_k\), define \(J(x_k):T_{x_k}\mathcal M\to T_{x_k}\mathcal M\) by \(J(x_k)[\eta]=\nabla_\eta\xi\). An approximate Newton step \(\eta_k\in T_{x_k}\mathcal M\) satisfies \[(J(x_k)+E_k)\eta_k=-\xi_{x_k}+\varepsilon_k,\] where \(E_k\) is the Jacobian-approximation error and \(\varepsilon_k\) is the residual error in solving the inexact Newton equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a manifold, an approximate Newton step solves a perturbed Newton equation containing both an operator error in the Jacobian and a residual error in the linear solve.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M\) is equipped with a retraction \(R\) and affine connection \(\nabla\).
\(\xi\) is a vector field on \(\mathcal M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (J(x_k)+E_k)\eta_k=-\xi_{x_k}+\varepsilon_k.

source_evidence.locator: A Constellation of Superlinear Algorithms / 8.2. Approximate Newton Methods / Definition 8.2-extra-1

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Superlinear Convergence of Perturbed Riemannian Newton
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Manifold specialization allowing both Jacobian-approximation error and residual error in the Newton equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal M\) be a manifold, let \(\xi\) be a vector field, and suppose \(x_*\in\mathcal M\) satisfies \(\xi_{x_*}=0\) with \(J(x_*)\) invertible. Replace each Newton equation by \[(J(x_k)+E_k)\eta_k=-\xi_{x_k}+\varepsilon_k.\] In a chart containing \(x_*\), suppose constants \(\beta_J\) and \(\kappa\) exist such that, for every \(k\), \[\|\widehat E_k\|\leq\beta_J\|\widehat\xi_k\|,\qquad \|\widehat\varepsilon_k\|\leq\min\{\|\widehat\xi_k\|^\theta,\kappa\}\|\widehat\xi_k\|,\quad\theta>0.\] Then there is a neighborhood \(\mathcal U\) of \(x_*\) such that every \(x_0\in\mathcal U\) generates an infinite sequence converging superlinearly to \(x_*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a zero with invertible Jacobian, the perturbed Riemannian Newton iteration converges superlinearly when the Jacobian error is residual-proportional and the relative equation residual vanishes at a positive power of the vector-field norm.
assumptions_latex: A chart containing \(x_*\) supplies the coordinate expressions denoted by hats.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\mathcal U\ni x_*\;\forall x_0\in\mathcal U:\ \{x_k\}\text{ is infinite and }x_k\to x_*\text{ superlinearly}.

children.title: Truncated Riemannian Newton Methods
children.top_down_role: Newton families terminating inner curvature solves according to computational criteria.

assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathcal M\to\mathbb R\) is twice continuously differentiable and \(R\) is a retraction.
A symmetric Krylov iteration is available for the tangent-space Newton system.
A positive iteration cap or a specified safeguard supplies a finite inner stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method returns either an approximate Newton step or a safeguarded tangent direction after finitely many inner iterations.

notation.meaning: Riemannian gradient and Hessian at iteration k
Inner Krylov iterate in the tangent space

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard truncated Newton construction adapted to the tangent space
exact truncation and negative-curvature conventions vary by algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite Krylov truncation of the tangent-space Newton solve, with explicit safeguard exits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x_k\), apply a symmetric Krylov method to \(H_ks=-g_k\), starting from \(s_{k,0}=0\). Terminate at the first index \(j\le J_k\) for which either \[\lVert H_ks_{k,j}+g_k\rVert_{x_k}\le\theta_k\lVert g_k\rVert_{x_k},\] a prescribed negative-curvature or trust-region safeguard is triggered, or \(j=J_k\). Set \(\eta_k=s_{k,j}\), modified by the triggered safeguard when required, and update through \(R_{x_k}\) subject to the outer globalization rule. The finite cap distinguishes truncation from an unrestricted inexact solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stop the tangent-space Krylov solve at a residual target, safeguard event, or iteration cap, then use the resulting safeguarded step.
knowledge_statements.title: Truncated Riemannian Newton Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the Krylov method, negative-curvature exit, trust-region modification, and returned safeguarded direction are variant-dependent and not specified sufficiently without an algorithm-specific source.

children.title: Forcing-Accuracy Regimes
children.top_down_role: Inner-solve accuracy choices governing local behavior plus computational effort.

assumptions_latex: The inexact Newton residual satisfies \(\lVert r_k\rVert_{x_k}\le\theta_k\lVert g_k\rVert_{x_k}\).
The iterates approach a nondegenerate critical point \(x_\star\).
The local smoothness assumptions required for the corresponding Newton convergence theorem hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A fixed bound below one supports linear local convergence; \(\theta_k\to0\) supports superlinear convergence; and \(\theta_k=O(\lVert g_k\rVert_{x_k})\) supports quadratic convergence under the usual Lipschitz-Hessian assumptions.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical inexact Newton forcing regimes, stated for Riemannian residuals
precise convergence order requires a manifold-specific theorem locator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local forcing-term regimes near a nondegenerate Riemannian critical point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The forcing sequence \(\{\theta_k\}\subset[0,1)\) specifies inner-solve accuracy through \(\lVert r_k\rVert_{x_k}\le\theta_k\lVert g_k\rVert_{x_k}\). Three standard regimes are: \(\theta_k\le\bar\theta<1\) for all sufficiently large \(k\); \(\theta_k\to0\); and \(\theta_k\le C\lVert g_k\rVert_{x_k}\) for some \(C>0\). Under the stated local regularity and nondegeneracy assumptions, these regimes correspond respectively to linear, superlinear, and quadratic local convergence guarantees for the outer iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inner tolerances bounded below one, tending to zero, or proportional to the gradient yield progressively stronger local convergence regimes.
knowledge_statements.title: Forcing-Accuracy Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits forcing-accuracy regimes, but the linear, superlinear, and quadratic conclusions depend on precise bounds, local regularity, retraction assumptions, and a manifold-specific convergence theorem that is not cited.

children.title: Truncation Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Boundary handling for negative curvature, ill-conditioning, or unreliable inner solves.

assumptions_latex: The inner iteration produces tangent candidates and residuals for \(H_k\eta=-g_k\).
The outer method supplies either a trust-region radius or a descent acceptance mechanism.
All safeguard thresholds are fixed before the corresponding inner solve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned inner step obeys a finite termination rule and excludes unchecked steps caused by excessive length, detected nonpositive curvature, or stagnating residuals.

notation.meaning: Current inner candidate and its residual

review_flags: no unique canonical safeguard set is determined by the node title
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic finite inner-solve safeguards; individual implementations may select a subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A safeguarded truncation rule stops the inner iteration at the first occurrence of at least one prescribed event: \(j=J_k\); \(\lVert r_j\rVert_{x_k}\le\theta_k\lVert g_k\rVert_{x_k}\); detected curvature \(\langle s_j,H_ks_j\rangle_{x_k}\le0\); intersection with \(\lVert s_j\rVert_{x_k}=\Delta_k\); or certified residual stagnation. On negative curvature or boundary intersection, the rule returns a point on the generated tangent-space ray or Krylov subspace that satisfies the outer trust-region or descent requirement. Otherwise it returns the current approximate Newton step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Terminate the inner solve on convergence, iteration limit, nonpositive curvature, trust-region contact, or residual stagnation, returning a controlled tangent step.
knowledge_statements.title: Truncation Safeguards

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record belongs under truncation safeguards, but it blends several algorithm-dependent stopping events and asserts a controlled returned step without specifying the construction that guarantees the outer trust-region or descent condition.

assumptions_latex: \(H_k=\operatorname{Hess}f(x_k)\) is available through tangent-space Hessian-vector products.
A Krylov solver uses the Riemannian inner product on \(T_{x_k}\mathcal M\).
Any preconditioner maps \(T_{x_k}\mathcal M\) into itself and satisfies the solver's symmetry and positivity requirements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Newton step is approximated using Hessian-vector products and tangent-space inner products, without explicitly forming or factorizing a Hessian matrix.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: matrix-free Newton-Krylov interface on a Riemannian tangent space
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free interface between Riemannian Newton equations and tangent-space Krylov solvers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x_k\), the Newton equation \(H_k\eta=-g_k\) is exposed to a Krylov solver through the oracle \(v\mapsto H_kv\) for \(v\in T_{x_k}\mathcal M\), together with the metric inner product. Without preconditioning, the \(j\)-th iterate lies in \[\mathcal K_j(H_k,g_k)=\operatorname{span}\{g_k,H_kg_k,\ldots,H_k^{j-1}g_k\}.\] With an admissible \(P_k\), the corresponding preconditioned operator and residual are used. The interface returns a tangent vector, its residual norm, and any detected curvature event to the outer Newton globalization mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tangent-space Krylov solver accesses the Riemannian Hessian only through Hessian-vector products and reports a step, residual, and curvature information.
knowledge_statements.title: Newton–Krylov Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is an appropriate kind for this interface, and the matrix-free tangent-space description is plausible. A source is still required for the Riemannian Krylov interface, admissible preconditioning, and reported curvature events.

children.title: Line-Search Globalization
children.top_down_role: Newton step control through manifold search curves plus acceptance criteria.

assumptions_latex: \(R\) is a retraction and \(f\) is continuously differentiable.
The computed \(\eta_k\in T_{x_k}\mathcal M\) is a descent direction: \(\langle g_k,\eta_k\rangle_{x_k}<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted update satisfies the Riemannian Armijo sufficient-decrease inequality along the retraction curve.

notation.meaning: Newton or modified Newton search direction

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Armijo backtracking along a retraction curve
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Armijo backtracking applied to a descent Newton or modified-Newton direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting with \(\alpha=\alpha_0\), repeatedly replace \(\alpha\) by \(\beta\alpha\) until \[f(R_{x_k}(\alpha\eta_k))\le f(x_k)+c\alpha\langle g_k,\eta_k\rangle_{x_k}.\] Set \(\alpha_k=\alpha\) and \(x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(\alpha_k\eta_k)\). If the raw Newton direction is not a descent direction, it must first be modified, regularized, or replaced; the displayed backtracking rule alone does not repair a non-descent direction. Termination requires the usual local descent regularity along the retraction curve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtrack along a descent Newton direction until the retracted trial point gives Armijo sufficient decrease, then accept that step.
knowledge_statements.title: Line-Search Globalization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Armijo backtracking algorithm fits the line-search leaf and correctly requires a descent direction, but no inspectable source supports the retraction-based formulation and termination qualification.

children.title: Trust-Region Globalization
children.top_down_role: Newton step control through tangent-space model regions plus acceptance ratios.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable and \(R\) is a retraction.
The quadratic model uses the Riemannian gradient and a self-adjoint tangent-space Hessian model.
Trust-region parameters satisfy standard ordered acceptance and radius-update thresholds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each accepted step is selected by agreement between actual and predicted reduction, while the radius contracts or expands according to that agreement.
review_flags: source supports the generic trust-region framework; manifold-specific formulation still requires confirmation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Riemannian trust-region globalization using a quadratic tangent-space model and retraction.

source_refs.locator: II Trust-Region Methods for Unconstrained Optimization p. 113

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form \(m_k(\eta)=f(x_k)+\langle g_k,\eta\rangle_{x_k}+\tfrac12\langle\eta,H_k\eta\rangle_{x_k}\) and compute an approximate minimizer \(\eta_k\) subject to \(\lVert\eta\rVert_{x_k}\le\Delta_k\). Define \[\rho_k=\frac{f(x_k)-f(R_{x_k}(\eta_k))}{m_k(0)-m_k(\eta_k)},\] whenever the predicted reduction is positive. Accept \(x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(\eta_k)\) when \(\rho_k\) exceeds the acceptance threshold; otherwise set \(x_{k+1}=x_k\). Decrease \(\Delta_k\) after poor agreement and permit an increase after strong agreement with an active boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximately minimize a quadratic tangent model inside a radius, then accept and resize the radius using actual versus predicted reduction.
knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Globalization

source_witnesses.locator: II Trust-Region Methods for Unconstrained Optimization p. 113

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and formulas fit trust-region globalization, but the cited locator supports a generic Euclidean trust-region framework rather than the stated Riemannian model, metric ball, and retraction update. A manifold-specific source is required.

children.title: Globalization Selection Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem geometry plus model-quality considerations governing safeguard choice.

assumptions_latex: A Newton-type tangent direction and its curvature information are available.
The algorithm can evaluate either a descent test or a model-agreement ratio.
The chosen globalization mechanism has parameters satisfying its standard admissibility conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Line search is admissible in the descent regime, whereas a trust region remains defined when the Newton model is indefinite or the raw Newton direction is unsuitable for descent.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: selection based on descent and curvature diagnostics
selection regimes are implementation-dependent rather than a unique theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic selection between line-search and trust-region Newton globalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Use line-search globalization only when the proposed direction satisfies \(\langle g_k,\eta_k\rangle_{x_k}<0\) and a retraction-based sufficient-decrease search is well posed. Prefer trust-region globalization when nonpositive curvature is detected, \(H_k\) is ill-conditioned, the Newton equation is solved only coarsely, or the raw direction fails the descent test, because the constrained model subproblem still specifies a bounded trial step. This is a selection principle: the precise thresholds and any preference under positive-definite curvature belong to the chosen implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use line search for a reliable descent direction; use a trust region when curvature, conditioning, or inner-solve quality makes the raw Newton step unreliable.
knowledge_statements.title: Globalization Selection Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Principle is a reasonable kind for this selection leaf, but the asserted preference for trust regions under coarse solves, ill-conditioning, and other diagnostics is implementation-dependent and lacks comparative manifold-specific support.

children.title: Globalization Transition Strategies
children.top_down_role: Hybrid regimes that switch safeguard families as local model reliability changes.

assumptions_latex: Both globalization mechanisms use the same objective, retraction, and tangent-space model data.
Switching thresholds include hysteresis or persistence rules preventing immediate reversal.
Every accepted step satisfies the acceptance condition of the currently active mechanism.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method may change globalization modes without accepting a step that violates the active sufficient-decrease or model-agreement test.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: safeguarded state-machine transition between globalization modes
no canonical transition strategy is determined by the title
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A generic safeguarded transition policy between trust-region and line-search modes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize an active mode \(q_0\). While \(q_k=\mathrm{TR}\), apply trust-region acceptance and radius updates; switch to \(q_{k+1}=\mathrm{LS}\) only after prescribed consecutive iterations exhibit positive-definite model curvature, accurate inner solves, and strong model agreement. While \(q_k=\mathrm{LS}\), apply sufficient-decrease backtracking; switch to \(q_{k+1}=\mathrm{TR}\) after a failed descent test, detected nonpositive curvature, or repeated excessive backtracking, initializing \(\Delta_{k+1}\) from a bounded accepted or attempted step norm. Retain the current mode when no transition predicate holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Switch from trust region to line search after sustained reliable curvature and agreement, and switch back when descent or backtracking diagnostics deteriorate.
knowledge_statements.title: Globalization Transition Strategies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the transition-strategy leaf, but the persistence tests, switching predicates, hysteresis policy, and radius initialization constitute one noncanonical design with no algorithm-specific source.

children.title: Singular Hessian Boundary
children.top_down_role: Rank deficiency, nonisolated solutions, plus ill-posed Newton directions.

assumptions_latex: The Riemannian Hessian \(H_\star:T_{x_\star}\mathcal M\to T_{x_\star}\mathcal M\) is self-adjoint and singular.
The unregularized Newton equation is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Invertibility-based Newton steps and the standard nondegenerate local quadratic-convergence conclusion are unavailable at \(x_\star\); solvability additionally requires the gradient right-hand side to lie in the Hessian range.

notation.meaning: Riemannian Hessian at the critical point
Kernel and range of a linear operator

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: linear-algebraic failure of the Newton equation at a degenerate critical point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of the nondegenerate Newton regime when the critical-point Hessian has a nontrivial kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Singularity means that there exists \(v\in T_{x_\star}\mathcal M\setminus\{0\}\) with \(H_\star v=0\). Hence \(H_\star^{-1}\) does not exist, the Newton step need not be unique, and for nearby \(x\) the equation \(\operatorname{Hess}f(x)[\eta]=-\operatorname{grad}f(x)\) is solvable only when \(-\operatorname{grad}f(x)\in\operatorname{range}(\operatorname{Hess}f(x))\). Therefore the usual local theorem based on a uniformly invertible Hessian cannot be invoked at this boundary without regularization, quotienting of null directions, or additional structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular critical-point Hessian destroys uniqueness and may destroy solvability of the Newton equation, invalidating the usual nondegenerate quadratic-convergence regime.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular Hessian Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure boundary is the correct kind, and the linear-algebraic range and nonuniqueness statements are sound. The conclusion about loss of the standard Riemannian local quadratic-convergence regime requires a specific theorem locator.

children.title: Indefinite Hessian Boundary
children.top_down_role: Negative-curvature regimes producing non-descent or saddle-directed Newton steps.

assumptions_latex: At an iterate \(x_k\), the self-adjoint Hessian \(H_k\) has a direction of negative curvature.
Globalization is based on either descent or bounded model minimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Indefiniteness does not by itself make the Newton equation unsolvable, but it removes convexity of the quadratic model and can make the raw Newton step unsuitable for minimization globalization.

notation.meaning: Riemannian Hessian and gradient at iteration k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: negative curvature makes the Newton quadratic model nonconvex
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the minimization interpretation of Newton steps under negative Riemannian curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Indefiniteness means that some \(v\in T_{x_k}\mathcal M\setminus\{0\}\) satisfies \(\langle v,H_kv\rangle_{x_k}<0\). Consequently the quadratic model \(m_k(\eta)=f(x_k)+\langle g_k,\eta\rangle_{x_k}+\tfrac12\langle\eta,H_k\eta\rangle_{x_k}\) is nonconvex and is unbounded below along the ray generated by \(v\) when unconstrained. Even if \(H_k\eta_k=-g_k\) has a unique solution, \(\eta_k\) need not be a descent direction. A minimization method therefore requires negative-curvature handling, regularization, or a trust-region constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative Hessian curvature makes the quadratic model nonconvex and can make the raw Newton step non-descent, requiring globalization or regularization.
knowledge_statements.title: Indefinite Hessian Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Failure boundary is appropriate, and negative curvature correctly implies a nonconvex, unconstrained quadratic model while not necessarily implying singularity. The prescribed globalization responses need a manifold-specific source.

children.title: Near-Singularity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Severe conditioning plus numerical sensitivity before exact singularity.

knowledge_statements.title: Near-Singularity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ill-conditioning boundary for a Riemannian Newton equation at one iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g=\operatorname{grad}f(x)\) and let \(H=\operatorname{Hess}f(x):T_x\mathcal M\to T_x\mathcal M\) be self-adjoint and invertible. If \(\sigma_{\min}(H)=\varepsilon>0\), then the Newton step \(\eta=-H^{-1}g\) satisfies \(\|\eta\|\leq \|g\|/\varepsilon\), while perturbations obey \(\|\delta\eta\|\leq \|H^{-1}\|\,\|\delta g\|+\|H^{-1}\|\,\|\delta H\|\,\|\eta\|+o(\|\delta H\|)\). Thus, as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), bounded gradient or Hessian errors can produce unbounded relative step errors, so an unregularized Newton direction ceases to be numerically reliable before exact singularity is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the smallest Hessian singular value approaches zero, Newton steps and their perturbations can grow like its reciprocal, making the unregularized solve numerically unreliable.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice differentiable on a Riemannian manifold \(\mathcal M\).
\(H\) is self-adjoint and invertible at the current iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|H^{-1}\|=1/\sigma_{\min}(H)\) controls amplification of gradient and Hessian perturbations.

notation.meaning: Riemannian Hessian at the current iterate
smallest singular value of the Hessian

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, and the conditioning claim is plausible, but no inspectable source supports the manifold-specific perturbation formula or its numerical-reliability conclusion. A source with a section, theorem, or page locator is required.

children.title: Hessian Regularization Interface
children.top_down_role: Regularization, damping, plus curvature modification for unreliable Hessian models.

knowledge_statements.title: Hessian Regularization Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shifted-Hessian interface for stabilizing a Riemannian Newton step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x\in\mathcal M\), set \(g=\operatorname{grad}f(x)\) and \(H=\operatorname{Hess}f(x)\). Choose \(\lambda\geq0\) so that \(H+\lambda I\succeq \mu I\) for a prescribed \(\mu>0\), solve \((H+\lambda I)\eta=-g\), and form the trial point \(x^+=R_x(\eta)\). Increase \(\lambda\) if the factorization fails, the step is too large, or a model-acceptance test fails; decrease it after reliable agreement. Stop when a chosen gradient or step tolerance holds. For \(g\neq0\), the regularized direction is descending because \(\langle g,\eta\rangle=-\langle (H+\lambda I)\eta,\eta\rangle<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add a nonnegative Hessian shift until the tangent operator is uniformly positive definite, solve the shifted Newton equation, and adapt the shift using trial-step reliability.
assumptions_latex: \(R\) is a retraction defined at the computed step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H+\lambda I\succeq\mu I\) yields a uniquely defined descent direction with \(\|\eta\|\leq\|g\|/\mu\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits this interface leaf, but no source supports the particular shift-selection and adaptation rules. The descent and norm conclusions are standard once the shifted operator is uniformly positive definite, but the full algorithmic interface needs a specific source.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Quadratic Convergence of Riemannian Newton's Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local convergence near a nondegenerate stationary point for Newton's method of Algorithm 6.1.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $f:\mathcal M\to\mathbb R$ be smooth on a Riemannian manifold $\mathcal M$. If $x_\star\in\mathcal M$, $\operatorname{grad}f(x_\star)=0$, and $\operatorname{Hess}f(x_\star)$ is invertible, then there exists a neighborhood $U$ of $x_\star$ such that, for every $x_0\in U$, Riemannian Newton's method generates an infinite sequence $(x_k)_{k\ge0}$ that converges at least quadratically to $x_\star$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth function on a Riemannian manifold, Newton's method initialized sufficiently near a stationary point with invertible Riemannian Hessian is defined indefinitely and converges to that point at least quadratically.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists U\ni x_\star\;\forall x_0\in U:\ (x_k)_{k\ge0}\text{ is infinite and converges at least quadratically to }x_\star

source_evidence.locator: Second-order optimization algorithms / 6.2. Riemannian Newton's method / Theorem 6.7

source_refs.locator: Second-order optimization algorithms / 6.2. Riemannian Newton's method / Theorem 6.7

knowledge_statements.title: Local Quadratic Convergence of Riemannian Newton's Method

source_witnesses.locator: Second-order optimization algorithms / 6.2. Riemannian Newton's method / Theorem 6.7

knowledge_statements.title: Local Quadratic-Convergence Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local convergence of exact Riemannian Newton iteration near a nondegenerate critical point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathcal M\to\mathbb R\) be twice continuously differentiable near \(x_\star\), with locally Lipschitz Riemannian Hessian, \(\operatorname{grad}f(x_\star)=0\), and invertible \(\operatorname{Hess}f(x_\star)\). For each sufficiently close \(x_k\), let \(\eta_k\) solve \(\operatorname{Hess}f(x_k)[\eta_k]=-\operatorname{grad}f(x_k)\), and set \(x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(\eta_k)\), where \(R\) is a smooth retraction. Then the iterates are well-defined locally and there exist \(C>0\) and a neighborhood of \(x_\star\) such that \(d(x_{k+1},x_\star)\leq C d(x_k,x_\star)^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact Riemannian Newton iterates converge quadratically when started near a critical point having an invertible, locally Lipschitz Hessian.
assumptions_latex: The Riemannian Hessian is locally Lipschitz and \(R\) is a smooth retraction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d(x_{k+1},x_\star)\leq C d(x_k,x_\star)^2\) for all sufficiently large local iterates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind and local quadratic-convergence statement fit the leaf, but the record has no citation for the precise Riemannian hypotheses, including the regularity and retraction assumptions. An authoritative theorem locator is required before accepting this version.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Newton Superlinear Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-forcing form of local inexact Riemannian Newton convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the local smoothness and nondegeneracy assumptions of exact Riemannian Newton convergence, suppose \(\eta_k\in T_{x_k}\mathcal M\) satisfies \(\operatorname{Hess}f(x_k)[\eta_k]+\operatorname{grad}f(x_k)=r_k\), with \(\|r_k\|\leq\theta_k\|\operatorname{grad}f(x_k)\|\), and set \(x_{k+1}=R_{x_k}(\eta_k)\). If \(0\leq\theta_k<1\) is uniformly bounded away from one, convergence is locally at least linear. If additionally \(\theta_k\to0\), then \(d(x_{k+1},x_\star)/d(x_k,x_\star)\to0\), so convergence is superlinear. The stronger condition \(\theta_k=O(\|\operatorname{grad}f(x_k)\|)\) recovers quadratic convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inexact Newton solves are locally superlinear when their relative residual forcing terms vanish; forcing terms proportional to the gradient recover quadratic convergence.
assumptions_latex: The solution \(x_\star\) is nondegenerate and the Hessian is locally Lipschitz.
The iterates remain in a neighborhood where the Hessian is uniformly invertible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta_k\to0\) implies \(d(x_{k+1},x_\star)/d(x_k,x_\star)\to0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits the superlinear-regime leaf, but no cited source supports the stated residual-forcing implications on a manifold. A precise source is needed to confirm the local assumptions and the linear, superlinear, and quadratic conclusions together.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Rates for Finite-Difference Riemannian Newton
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional local rate result for geometric Newton iteration using vector-transport finite-difference Jacobians.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the geometric Newton method in which \(J(x_k)\) is replaced by the vector-transport finite-difference operator \(A(x_k)\) with step \(h_k\), in the local convergence regime of a nondegenerate zero of \(\xi\). If \(h_k\to0\), then the convergence is superlinear. If, moreover, there exists \(c>0\) such that \(h_k\leq c\|\xi_{x_k}\|\) for every \(k\), then the convergence is at least quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For locally convergent finite-difference Riemannian Newton iteration at a nondegenerate zero, a vanishing differencing step yields superlinear convergence; a step bounded by the vector-field residual yields at least quadratic convergence.
assumptions_latex: The geometric Newton method replaces \(J(x_k)\) by the operator \(A(x_k)\) defined by the vector-transport finite-difference formula with \(h=h_k\).
The local limit is a nondegenerate zero of \(\xi\).
For the quadratic conclusion, additionally \(\exists c>0\;\forall k:\ h_k\leq c\|\xi_{x_k}\|\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: h_k\to0\Longrightarrow\text{superlinear convergence};\qquad h_k\leq c\|\xi_{x_k}\|\ \forall k\Longrightarrow\text{convergence of order at least two}.

knowledge_statements.title: Retraction-Order Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: How retraction consistency enters the local order of Newton-type iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a Newton-type tangent step has intrinsic local error \(O(d(x_k,x_\star)^p)\), with \(p>1\), and the update map satisfies \(d(R_x(\eta),\exp_x(\eta))=O(\|\eta\|^{q})\) uniformly near \(x_\star\), where \(q>1\). Since \(\|\eta_k\|=O(d(x_k,x_\star))\), the retracted iteration satisfies \(d(x_{k+1},x_\star)=O(d(x_k,x_\star)^{\min\{p,q\}})\). In particular, a smooth first-order retraction has \(q=2\) and therefore preserves quadratic convergence of exact Newton steps; higher-order agreement cannot improve an intrinsically quadratic Newton correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The local order is limited by both tangent-step accuracy and the retraction’s agreement with the exponential map; an ordinary smooth retraction preserves quadratic Newton convergence.
assumptions_latex: The stated retraction-error estimate is uniform near \(x_\star\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting local order is at least \(\min\{p,q\}\) under the stated error expansions.

notation.meaning: intrinsic order of the tangent correction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the leaf, but the claimed minimum-order rule and the convention assigning exponent q=2 to a smooth first-order retraction require a source. The record supplies none, and the exact regularity needed for the uniform error estimate is therefore unresolved.

knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate-Solution Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete loss of quadratic Newton convergence at a degenerate critical point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On the Euclidean manifold \(\mathcal M=\mathbb R\), let \(f(x)=x^4\). The point \(x_\star=0\) satisfies \(f'(x_\star)=0\), but \(f''(x_\star)=0\), so the critical point is degenerate. For every \(x_k\neq0\), Newton's equation gives \(12x_k^2\eta_k=-4x_k^3\), hence \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\eta_k=\tfrac23x_k\). Consequently \(|x_{k+1}-x_\star|/|x_k-x_\star|=2/3\): convergence is only linear. Thus removing Hessian invertibility invalidates the general local quadratic-convergence conclusion, even for a smooth objective and the exact exponential update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the smooth objective x⁴, Newton iteration converges to the degenerate minimizer only linearly, showing that Hessian invertibility is essential for generic quadratic convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k=(2/3)^k x_0\), so convergence to \(0\) is linear rather than quadratic.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Radial Linearity and Uniform Boundedness of the RTR Model Map
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-map assumptions at iterations whose Riemannian gradient exceeds the first-order tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every iteration \(k\) with \(\|\operatorname{grad}f(x_k)\|_{x_k}>\varepsilon_g\), require \(H_k(\alpha s)=\alpha H_k(s)\) for all \(s\in T_{x_k}\mathcal M\) and \(\alpha\ge0\). Moreover, there exists \(c_0\ge0\), independent of \(k\), such that \(|\langle s,H_k(s)\rangle_{x_k}|\le c_0\|s\|_{x_k}^2\) for all \(s\in T_{x_k}\mathcal M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the gradient norm exceeds the first-order tolerance, the trust-region model map is radially linear and uniformly quadratically bounded by an iteration-independent constant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall s\in T_{x_k}\mathcal M,\ \forall\alpha\ge0:\ H_k(\alpha s)=\alpha H_k(s),\qquad \exists c_0\ge0\ \text{independent of }k:\ \forall s\in T_{x_k}\mathcal M,\ |\langle s,H_k(s)\rangle_{x_k}|\le c_0\|s\|_{x_k}^2.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Retraction characterization of an order-q model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes intrinsic Riemannian model order through inverse-retraction coordinates on a sufficiently small neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathcal M\to\mathbb R, let x\in\mathcal M, let q>0, and let m_x be a real-valued function defined near x. For any retraction R on \mathcal M, after restricting to a neighborhood on which R_x has a local inverse, m_x is an order-q model of f at x if and only if there exist a neighborhood \mathcal U of x and c>0 such that \left|f(y)-m_x(y)\right|\le c\|R_x^{-1}(y)\|^{q+1} for every y\in\mathcal U.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any retraction, intrinsic order-q model accuracy is equivalent locally to bounding the model error by the inverse-retraction coordinate norm raised to q+1.
assumptions_latex: m_x\text{ is real-valued and defined near }x
R\text{ is a retraction on }\mathcal M
R_x^{-1}\text{ is considered on a neighborhood where it is defined}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m_x\text{ is an order-}q\text{ model of }f\text{ at }x\iff \exists\mathcal U\ni x\ \exists c>0\ \forall y\in\mathcal U:\ |f(y)-m_x(y)|\le c\|R_x^{-1}(y)\|^{q+1}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Negative-Curvature Model Decrease for RTR Steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Required decrease near first-order stationarity when the model operator has sufficiently negative curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: There exists \(c_3>0\) such that, for every iteration \(k\) with \(\|\operatorname{grad}f(x_k)\|_{x_k}\le\varepsilon_g\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(H_k)<-\varepsilon_H\), the step satisfies \[m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)\ge c_3\Delta_k^2\varepsilon_H.\] The operator \(H_k\) satisfies the low-gradient linearity and self-adjointness condition, so \(\lambda_{\min}(H_k)\) is real.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the gradient is small but the self-adjoint model operator has an eigenvalue below minus the curvature tolerance, the step must produce model decrease proportional to the squared radius times that tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)\ge c_3\Delta_k^2\varepsilon_H.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Riemannian Trust-Region Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration, acceptance, and radius-update rules for a retraction-based Riemannian trust-region method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(\bar\Delta>0\), \(\rho'\in(0,1/4)\), \(x_0\in\mathcal M\), and \(\Delta_0\in(0,\bar\Delta]\). At iteration \(k\), choose \(H_k:T_{x_k}\mathcal M\to T_{x_k}\mathcal M\), approximately solve the trust-region subproblem for \(m_k\) to obtain \(s_k\), and set \(x_k^+=R_{x_k}(s_k)\). Define \(\rho_k=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k^+)}{m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)}\). Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k^+\) if \(\rho_k>\rho'\), and \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) otherwise. Set \(\Delta_{k+1}=\Delta_k/4\) if \(\rho_k<1/4\); set \(\Delta_{k+1}=\min(2\Delta_k,\bar\Delta)\) if \(\rho_k>3/4\) and \(\|s_k\|_{x_k}=\Delta_k\); otherwise set \(\Delta_{k+1}=\Delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximately solve a tangent-space trust-region subproblem, retract the trial step to the manifold, accept it when actual-to-model improvement exceeds the threshold, shrink the radius after poor agreement, and enlarge it after very good agreement by a boundary step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (x_{k+1},\Delta_{k+1})\text{ is determined by the stated acceptance and radius-update rules.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Riemannian Cauchy Point and Its Model-Decrease Guarantee
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form minimization along the negative Riemannian-gradient ray and the resulting RTR decrease guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_k=\operatorname{grad}f(x_k)\), and let \(s_k^C=-t g_k\), with \(t\ge0\), minimize \(m_k(-t g_k)\) subject to \(\|s_k^C\|_{x_k}\le\Delta_k\). Under the radial-linearity and uniform-boundedness condition, \[t=\begin{cases}\min\!\left(\dfrac{\|g_k\|_{x_k}^2}{\langle g_k,H_k(g_k)\rangle_{x_k}},\dfrac{\Delta_k}{\|g_k\|_{x_k}}\right),&\langle g_k,H_k(g_k)\rangle_{x_k}>0,\\[4pt]\dfrac{\Delta_k}{\|g_k\|_{x_k}},&\langle g_k,H_k(g_k)\rangle_{x_k}\le0.\end{cases}\] Setting \(s_k=s_k^C\) satisfies the sufficient first-order model-decrease condition with \(c_2=1/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Riemannian Cauchy point minimizes the model along the negative-gradient ray. With positive directional curvature its length is the smaller of the unconstrained minimizer and the trust-region boundary length; otherwise it reaches the boundary. It supplies the required model decrease with constant one half.
assumptions_latex: H_k\text{ satisfies the radial-linearity and uniform-boundedness condition}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: t\text{ has the stated piecewise form, and }s_k=s_k^C\text{ satisfies the sufficient model-decrease condition with }c_2=\tfrac12.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Riemannian Trust-Region Meta-Algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Radius-update and trial-step acceptance rules for deterministic Riemannian trust-region iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal M,g)\) be a Riemannian manifold, \(f:\mathcal M\to\mathbb R\), and \(R\) a retraction. Choose \(\bar\Delta>0\), \(\Delta_0\in(0,\bar\Delta)\), \(\rho'\in[0,1/4)\), and \(x_0\in\mathcal M\). At iteration \(k\), approximately solve the trust-region subproblem for \(\eta_k\) and compute \(\rho_k\). Set \[\Delta_{k+1}=\begin{cases}\Delta_k/4,&\rho_k<1/4,\\ \min\{2\Delta_k,\bar\Delta\},&\rho_k>3/4\text{ and }\|\eta_k\|=\Delta_k,\\ \Delta_k,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\] and \[x_{k+1}=\begin{cases}R_{x_k}(\eta_k),&\rho_k>\rho',\\x_k,&\rho_k\leq\rho'.\end{cases}\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, approximately solve the tangent-space trust-region subproblem, update the radius from the agreement ratio and boundary status, and accept the retracted trial point precisely when the ratio exceeds the acceptance threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x_k\}_{k\geq0}\text{ is generated by the stated radius-update and trial-step acceptance rules}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linearity, self-adjointness, and radius-scaled pullback-Hessian accuracy near first-order stationarity.

knowledge_statements.title: Tangent-Space Quadratic Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic trust-region model defined on one Riemannian tangent space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x\in\mathcal M\), a tangent-space quadratic model is the function \(m_x:T_x\mathcal M\to\mathbb R\) defined by \(m_x(\eta)=f(x)+\langle g_x,\eta\rangle_x+\tfrac12\langle \eta,B_x\eta\rangle_x\), where \(g_x\in T_x\mathcal M\) and \(B_x:T_x\mathcal M\to T_x\mathcal M\) is self-adjoint. The associated trust-region subproblem minimizes \(m_x(\eta)\) subject to \(\|\eta\|_x\leq\Delta\). For the second-order Riemannian model, \(g_x=\operatorname{grad}f(x)\) and \(B_x=\operatorname{Hess}f(x)\); an accepted tangent step is mapped to the manifold as \(R_x(\eta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Riemannian trust-region model is a self-adjoint quadratic function on the current tangent space, minimized inside a norm ball and mapped back by a retraction.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal M\) is a Riemannian manifold and \(B_x\) is self-adjoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model subproblem is \(\min_{\|\eta\|_x\leq\Delta}m_x(\eta)\).
